zh: 8.1　论风格概念
en: 8.1　On the Concept of Style

zh: 本章的目标，是提出一个适应视觉艺术人类学要求的“风格”概念。在艺术人类学语境中，风格概念与西方艺术史和美学中适用的风格概念的区别在于：风格的“单位”（通常）不是单个艺术家、艺术家流派或运动，而是“文化”或“社会”。实际上，风格的单位是按民族志惯例划出的单位。为研究之便，博物馆藏品与已出版的物质文化资料呈现了这些单位。民族志以这种方式划出的单位，既有时间边界，也有地理边界；通常，藏品与文献属于某一特定时期。就博物馆中的民族志艺术研究而言，相关时期大多与殖民时代重合。焦点主要在“传统”艺术形式上，尽管几乎不必多说：殖民时期，殖民边地那些所谓“传统”社会经历了惊人的历史变迁，以多种方式影响了它们的艺术生产。民族志艺术中的传统与创新问题，在此阶段讨论会过于枝蔓；何况这一主题已得到众多其他研究者的细致关注，最突出的是N·托马斯。就本章而言，我们将假定风格的单位是“文化”，所考察的是约定俗成意义上的“传统”艺术。这些假设会带来一些已知的问题，姑且留待以后再谈。
en: In this chapter, my aim is to formulate a concept of ‘style' adapted to the requirements of the anthropology of visual art. In the anthropology-of-art context the concept of style is distinguishable from the concepts of style applicable in Western art history and aesthetics in that the ‘units' of style are not (usually) individual artists, or schools of artists, or movements, but ‘cultures' or ‘societies'. Actually, the units of style are conventional ethnographic isolates as represented for study purposes by museum collections and published sources on material culture. Such ethnographic isolates are historically bounded as well as geographically bounded; usually the collections and documents belong to a particular period. Where studies of ethnographic art in museums are concerned, the period in question coincides mostly with the colonial era. The focus is primarily on ‘traditional' art forms, though it hardly needs to be said that during the colonial period there were startling historical developments in the so-called ‘traditional' societies of the colonial frontier, which affected their art production in diverse ways. The problem of tradition and innovation in ethnographic arts would constitute too much of a diversion to discuss at this stage; besides which the subject has already received detailed attention from numerous other researchers, most notably by N. Thomas. For the purposes of this chapter, it will be assumed that the units of style are ‘cultures' and that we are dealing with ‘traditional' art as conventionally understood, setting to one side the acknowledged problems which these assumptions admittedly raise.

zh: 如何把风格放回历史中考察，并不实质影响我在这里要谈的内容，因为一种风格的描述，其范围可宽可窄，足以容纳任何给定的历史视角。我想处理的问题不是历史性的，而是概念性的：“风格”概念对理解物质文化有何贡献？“风格”是一个定义不确定、用法繁多而颇不统一的含糊字眼。若非这个词用得极普遍，至少经常用来分类，想为它在物质文化人类学中找一种用法，或许会被视为白费力气。我们习惯按物品是否具有共同的风格属性来归类。但在这些情形中，究竟共享（或不共享）的是什么，却难以评估得多。此外，我们倾向于相信：共享风格属性的对象所共有的，不只是某种形式的、外在的属性，而是某种与它们作为广义“文化”之表达的地位内在相关的东西；人工制品共享的风格属性，经由一种基本的图式迁移，与一个共同体中共享的“文化价值”联系起来。
en: The problems of historical contextualization do not materially affect what I have to say about style, since the description of a style may be as broad or as narrow in scope as necessary to accommodate any given historical perspective. The question that I want to address is not historical but conceptual: what does the concept of ‘style' contribute to the understanding of material culture? ‘Style' is a vague word of uncertain definition and many, rather disparate, uses. Finding a use for it in the context of the anthropology of material culture might be considered a waste of effort, were it not, in fact, so pervasive, at least as a mode of classification. As it is, we are routinely accustomed to classifying objects as sharing, or not sharing, stylistic attributes with one another. But exactly what is shared (or not shared) in such instances is much harder to assess. Moreover, we are inclined to believe that what objects with shared stylistic attributes have in common, is not just some formal, external, property, but something integral to their standing as expressions of ‘the culture' in the wider sense; common stylistic attributes shared by artefacts are associated, via a basic scheme transfer, with shared ‘cultural values' in a community.

zh: 我相信，风格概念（作为风格属性的构型）与文化概念（作为主体间理解的构型）之间存在关联，这一直觉是有充分根据的。但要把这一直觉转化为一系列明确而站得住脚的论证，还是一个遥远的目标，只能逐步接近。最初的步骤之一，是澄清“风格”概念，并从这个概念可能承载的众多解释中，区分出我们在人类学语境中特别需要的那一种。据我所知，还没有人类学家尝试对“风格”概念做批判性分析，迄今为止也没有一种真正人类学意义上的风格概念。在这种情况下，唯一可行的做法是转向美学与艺术史关于“风格”的文献，逐一考察各种可能性。
en: I believe that the intuition that there is a linkage between the concept of style (as a configuration of stylistic attributes) and the concept of culture (as a configuration of intersubjective understandings) is well founded. But to convert this intuition into a series of explicit and defensible arguments is a distant goal, which can only be approached by incremental steps. One of the first of these steps is to clarify the notion of ‘style' and to distinguish, from among the many possible interpretations that can be placed on this concept, the one we specifically need in the anthropological context. No anthropologist, to my knowledge, has attempted a critical analysis of the concept of ‘style', and as yet, there is no distinctively anthropological style-concept as such. In this situation, the only possible procedure is to turn to the aesthetic and art-historical literature on ‘style' so as to canvass the various possibilities.

zh: 有一个风格概念，我们大概无法按其原样加以人类学运用，那就是沃尔海姆在其广为人知的绘画风格论述（1987）中提出的概念。这样说并非对沃尔海姆不敬；我只是确信，美学与人类学是非常不同的事业。即便如此，沃尔海姆的讨论仍然非常有用，因为他把某些问题排除在风格分析的视野之外——因为它们与他本人的艺术兴趣不合——从而简洁地勾勒出与他自己的视角相平行的其他视角。他首先区分“一般”（集体）风格与“个体”风格。他感兴趣的是“个体”风格（他认为所有美学家都应当如此）。另一方面，艺术史家（以及人类学家）更有理由把一般风格或集体风格作为主题。在“一般”风格这一类目之内，他又进一步区分“普遍”风格类目，比如把“再现性”（写实）风格与“几何”风格（非写实、抽象等）对立起来的那一种。与“普遍”风格类目相对的，是时代、流派等的一般风格或集体风格——他称之为“历史”风格。“普遍”风格与“历史”（或文化）风格之分，与艺术人类学相关。某些人类学的风格类目在这种意义上是“普遍”的，即不限于特定文化或传统，而是见于不同的文化语境。“分割再现”就是这种“普遍”的风格特征之一（Boas 1927；Levi-Strauss 1963），后文将加以讨论。另一些人类学风格类目则是历史上特定的，或文化上特定的。
en: A concept of style that we probably cannot make anthropological use of in its original form is the one advanced by Wollheim in his deservedly well-known discussion of style in pictorial art (1987). I mean no disrespect to Wollheim in saying so; it is merely my conviction that aesthetics and anthropology are very different enterprises. Even so, Wollheim's discussion is very useful because in excluding certain questions from the purview of stylistic analysis-because they do not coincide with his own interest in art-he succinctly adumbrates perspectives collateral to his own. He distinguishes, first of all, between ‘general' (collective) and ‘individual' style. He is interested in ‘individual' style (as he suggests all aestheticians ought to be). On the other hand, art historians (and anthropologists) have more reason to take general or collective style as their theme. Within the category ‘general' style he further distinguishes ‘universal' style categories, such as the one which opposes ‘representational' (realistic) style to ‘geometric' style (non-realistic, abstract, etc.). Opposed to ‘universal' style categories are the general or collective styles of periods, schools, and so on-these he calls ‘historical' styles. The contrast between ‘universal' styles and ‘historical' (or cultural) styles is relevant to the anthropology of art. Certain anthropological stylistic categories are ‘universal' in this sense, that is, not confined to particular cultures or traditions, but manifesting themselves in disparate cultural contexts: and an instance of such a ‘universal' stylistic trait is ‘split representation' (Boas 1927; Levi-Strauss 1963), which will be discussed at a later stage. Other anthropological stylistic categories are historically specific, or culturally specific.

zh: 沃尔海姆把他自己关于“个体”（绘画）风格的观点——他称之为“生成性的”——与艺术史的风格观——他称之为“分类学的”——对立起来。按他的说法，仅仅编纂一份清单，罗列某位艺术家作品的风格属性，什么也解释不了；这只是分类或归档。要具有解释力，风格分析必须揭示画家作品中在心理上特别显著的那些方面。“风格”被等同于心理显著性，即只有具备成熟的个人风格的画家才拥有的那种能力：如此调动观者的注意力，使艺术品中具有审美意义的方面恰好就是实际吸引我们注意的方面。可以说，毕加索的风格，就是毕加索使我们注意到他那毕加索式艺术意图的能力。风格是审美形式中的人格，是“审美兴趣的先决条件”（Wollheim 1987: 188）。它应当与用于识别作者的“署名特征”区分开来，后者是“我们据以把作品归于某位艺术家的那些作品特征”（同上书：197）。他论证说，界定一种“成型风格”的特征可能非常抽象，我们未必能立刻意识到。他还补充了一个有趣的观察：通常，只有当我们知道某幅画确实出自某位有名有姓的画家之手，而不是出自另一位恰好画了相当类似作品的艺术家之手时，我们才开始注意到这些微妙的特征。
en: Wollheim contrasts his own view of ‘individual' (painting) style, which he calls ‘generative', to the view of style taken by art history which he calls ‘taxonomic'. According to him, nothing is explained merely by constructing compendia of the stylistic attributes manifested in the work of a particular artist; this is mere classification or pigeon-holing. To be explanatory, a stylistic analysis must bring out those aspects of a painter's work which are especially psychologically salient. ‘Style' is equated with psychological saliency, the capacity, possessed only by painters with a developed personal style, to so engage the spectator's attention that the aesthetically significant aspects of the work of art are the ones which actually do attract our notice. Picasso's style, so to speak, is Picasso's ability to cause us to notice his Picasso-ish artistic intentions. Style is personhood in aesthetic form, a ‘precondition for aesthetic interest' (Wollheim 1987: 188). It is to be distinguished from mere ‘signature' those ‘characteristics of an artist's work by reference to which we assign works to him' (ibid. 197). He argues that the traits which define a ‘formed style' may be very abstract ones, of which we may not be immediately aware. And he adds the interesting observation that commonly we start to notice these subtle characteristics only once we know that a particular painting actually is by a certain named painter, and not by another artist who happened to paint rather similar works.

zh: “生成性的”风格概念，最终落实为沃尔海姆所谓的“风格描述”（style-descriptions）：那是对一位艺术家作品（我想他指的是“全部成熟期作品”）的风格特征在高度抽象层面上的描述，使人能够领会这些作品何以在心理上显著。他把这种风格描述与“作品风格描述”（stylistic description）对立起来，后者是对任何一件给定艺术品——而非一位艺术家——的风格特征的说明。
en: The ‘generative' notion of style culminates in what Wollheim terms ‘style-descriptions’, which are descriptions of the stylistic features of the work (I think he means by this, ‘all the mature work') of an artist, at a high level of abstraction, so that one can appreciate the basis upon which this work is psychologically salient. He contrasts such a style-description to a ‘stylistic description' which is an account of the stylistic features of any given work of art, rather than of an artist.

zh: 显然，沃尔海姆那套描述方案针对的是可辨认身份且风格已“成型”（有其独特性）的画家，几乎没有可以为艺术人类学所用的东西。当然，人类学家可以研究特定艺术家及其作品，但如果这样做，他们本质上是在某个（相对）异域的语境中重演西方审美艺术批评的方案；他们并没有解决“民族学”艺术藏品及相关文化材料、文献等的存在所提出的风格问题。这里我假定，艺术人类学家处理的对象无法归属作者，只能归属于某一特定文化，甄别作者不是问题所在（但参见 Price 1989）。另一方面，沃尔海姆主张风格分析应当是“解释性的”、“处于高度抽象层面的”，而不是停留在“分类”上，这一论证显然有令人振奋之处。麻烦在于，按沃尔海姆的论证，除非处理的是显现个体风格的艺术品，否则真正有趣的（即非分类学的）问题似乎根本无法提出，更谈不上回答。
en: Obviously, there is very little in Wollheim's programme for the production of style-descriptions of individually identifiable painters with ‘formed' (distinctive) styles, that can be made use of in the anthropology of art. Of course, anthropologists can study particular artists and their output, but if they do so, they are essentially recapitulating the programme of Western aesthetic art criticism in some (relatively) exotic setting; they are not solving the stylistic problems posed by the existence of collections of ‘ethnological' art and the associated cultural material, documents, etc. Here, I am assuming that what the art anthropologists deal with is unattributable, except to a particular culture, and that sorting out authorship is not the issue (but cf. Price 1989). On the other hand, there is something obviously exciting about Wollheim's argument that stylistic analysis should be ‘explanatory' and ‘at a high level of abstraction' rather than tamely ‘taxonomic'. The trouble is that on Wollheim's argument, it would seem that unless one is dealing with artworks which manifest an individual style, the really interesting (i.e. non-taxonomic) questions cannot really be posed, let alone answered.

zh: 有没有可能重组沃尔海姆的方案，使“生成性”风格分析能够适用于“一般”风格或“历史”（即文化）风格，而不像在我看来他所打算的那样，只适用于个体风格？我认为这很大程度上取决于所处理的材料。沃尔海姆相信，与毕加索相关的重要风格问题关乎毕加索本人，而不是他的时代，也不是他在职业生涯不同阶段（或近或远）隶属的任何“群体风格”，这无疑完全正确。同样的道理也适用于米开朗基罗、安格尔，或西方艺术传统中任何拥有高度个人风格、过去和现在都特别因此受人尊崇的大师。但这一范式特别依赖于西方后文艺复兴艺术传统中艺术身份得以成就的社会过程，无法适用于我本章打算讨论的那类艺术。
en: Is it feasible to rearrange Wollheim's programme so that ‘generative' style analysis can be made applicable to ‘general' or ‘historical' (i.e. cultural) style, and not exclusively to individual style, as it seems to me he intends? I think this rather depends on the kind of material with which one is dealing. Wollheim is no doubt perfectly correct to believe that the important stylistic questions relating to Picasso, have to do with Picasso, not to his period, or to any of the ‘group styles' with which he was (closely or distantly) affiliated at different phases of his career. And the same would apply to Michelangelo, or Ingres, or any of the masters of the Western art tradition who possessed highly individual styles and who were, and are, esteemed particularly on that basis. But this paradigm depends particularly on the social processes through which an artistic identity is achieved in the Western post-Renaissance art tradition, and cannot be applied to the kind of art I intend to discuss in this chapter.

zh: 我即将讨论的这类艺术，不仅参照集体及其历史——而非个体——来界定，而且是“传统”的，意思是创新必须遵守严格的风格规范，保持风格的一致。这并不是说这些艺术生产传统中没有创新；创新持续发生。但它不与艺术身份相联系，只与精湛技艺相联系。例如，我们知道毛利人中个别纹身师享有极大的个人声望（并因此收取更高的费用）。他们之所以如此，是因为他们的作品比竞争者更符合毛利人公认的优秀纹身标准——而不是因为他们的纹身被当作表达其艺术个性的独特创作来欣赏。我们可以去找一位牙医，认为他是补牙、做牙冠和牙桥的顶尖乃至独创的高手。即便如此，我们珍视他的工作，不是因为它表达了他的个性，而只是因为它是能得到的同类中最好的。毛利纹身师如此，一般传统艺术生产体系中的艺术家也是如此。既然在这些体系中，人们衡量技艺高下时，并不看作品能否表现艺术家的个性，既然体裁与母题受制于如此严格的风格连贯性规范，那么处理这类材料时，把“集体”而非个体作为风格单位，就比在西方艺术讨论中恰当得多。何况，鉴于我们手头的艺术品与文献的性质，也几乎没有别的选择。
en: Not only is the kind of art I am about to discuss defined with reference to collectivities and their histories, not individuals, but it is also ‘traditional' in the sense that innovation was constrained within strict parameters of stylistic coherence. This is not to say that in these art-producing traditions innovation did not occur; it did so, continuously. But it was not associated with artistic identity, only with virtuosity. It is known that, for instance, individual tattoo artists among the Maori achieved great personal fame (and charged higher fees accordingly). They did so because their work instantiated, better than their competitors', what Maori collectively regarded as excellence in the matter of tattooing-not because their tattoos were appreciated as distinctive productions expressive of their artistic individuality. We may go to a dentist whom we consider to be a supreme and indeed original exponent of fillings, crownings, and bridgework. All the same, we do not prize his work because it expresses his individuality, but simply because it is the best of its kind available. It was the same with Maori tattoo artists, and artists in traditional art-production systems generally. Since in these systems there was no culturally recognized linkage between artistic excellence and the expression of artistic individuality, and since genres and motifs were subject to such stringent canons of stylistic coherence, it is much more appropriate to treat ‘collectivities' rather than individuals as units of style, when dealing with this kind of material, than it would be in discussions of Western art. Besides which, there is little alternative, given the nature of the artworks and documentation at our disposal.

zh: 即便如此，真的能为“民族学”艺术提供“生成性的”（抽象的、高层次的）风格描述吗，还是我们只能永远停留在分类这一步，辨认各种地方风格的识别特征？能否达成一种适用于某一“文化”之艺术的风格描述，具有沃尔海姆声称适用于个体艺术家的风格描述所具有的那种解释力？一个立刻浮现的解决办法，是把文化看作尺度放大了的个体或人。但这立刻引出一个逻辑困境。“个体”是与“集体”相对照而界定的。毕加索是一个极富个性的艺术家，在艺术中表达他的个性。他凸显于缺乏沃尔海姆所认可的“成型”（个人）风格的次要艺术家的背景之上，后者的艺术努力缺乏这种个体化的显著性，因此在艺术史上重要性较低。不能把“文化”艺术风格当作个体艺术风格的放大版，因为作为“集体”风格，它们对应的正是“风格”（即个体风格）在其上制造个体化效果的“背景”。“个体风格”概念隐含地依赖于集体的、未分化的时代风格的存在，个性正是作为“图”凸显于这一“底”之上。集体风格本身无从成为这个意义上的“图”，因为没有衬托它的“底”。也不能像比较毕加索与布拉克那样，把一种“文化”风格与另一种风格比较，仿佛文化是个体。毕加索与布拉克作为独特风格的拥有者，凸显于同一个（20世纪西方）背景之上；而比方说芳人的艺术与约尔恩古人的艺术，却没有一个共同的背景可供比较。
en: Even so, is it really possible to provide ‘generative' (abstract, high-level) style descriptions for ‘ethnological' art, or must we remain forever in the shallows of taxonomy, detecting the signatures of this or that local style? Can one achieve a style-description applicable to the art of a ‘culture' which has the same kind of explanatory power that Wollheim claims for style-descriptions applicable to individual artists? One solution which immediately suggests itself is to treat cultures as analogous to individuals or persons, but on a different scale, so to speak. But this poses an immediate logical dilemma. ‘Individuals' are defined contrastively with ‘collectivities'. Picasso was a supreme individualist who expressed his individuality in his art. He stands out against the background of lesser artists lacking what Wollheim would recognize as ‘formed' (personal) styles, whose artistic efforts lack this individualizing salience and are consequently of lesser art-historical importance. One cannot treat ‘cultural' art styles as magnified versions of individual art styles because, being ‘collective' styles, they correspond to the ‘background' against which ‘style' (individual style, that is) creates its individuating effect. The notion of ‘individual style' implicitly depends on the existence of collective, undifferentiated, period styles against which individuality emerges as ‘figure' against ‘ground'. One cannot treat collective styles as ‘figural' in this sense, since there is no ‘ground' to set them against. Nor can one compare a ‘cultural' style against another style as if cultures were individuals, in the way that one compares, say, Picasso and Braque. Picasso and Braque stand out as possessors of distinctive styles against the same (twentieth-century Western) background, whereas there is no common background against which one might compare, say, the art of the Fang and the Yolngu.

zh: 与此同时，又很难放弃这样的想法：集体艺术风格具有某种心理显著性，可与个体风格的心理显著性相比，尽管显然并不相同。就文化人类学家运用风格概念而言，这是一个心理的（认知的）概念，而不是分类学的概念，至少他们希望如此。有些人类学家满足于完全在分类学框架内考虑风格问题（即鉴定博物馆标本的出处等），但大多数人类学家把“风格”与“意义”联系起来（Forge 1973）。人类学家把“风格”理解为艺术品的这样一些属性：它们把那些艺术品与其他文化要素——如宗教信仰、亲属价值、政治竞争等——联系起来。由于相关联系常常经由形象的图像志传达（例如一件雕刻刻画的是某种图腾动物），人类学的风格观念与符号学问题致命地纠缠在一起，损害了概念的清晰性。我稍后再回到艺术人类学与符号学之间这种牵强的联姻。眼下，让我们假定图像志不是相关问题，风格才是，即艺术品的形式属性。“艺术品的形式属性”能与其他文化参数相联系吗？若能，一种“人类学的”风格概念就会聚焦于艺术品在把注意力引向文化参数方面的心理显著性。一种“文化”风格描述，将是对艺术品属性的抽象说明，依据的是它们将核心文化要素呈现为主题，使人更容易注意到它们的能力。
en: At the same time, it is hard to give up the idea that collective art styles have a kind of psychological saliency which is comparable to, though obviously not the same as, the psychological saliency of individual styles. In so far as cultural anthropologists operate with a concept of style, this is a psychological (cognitive) concept, rather than a taxonomic one, or at least they would like it to be. Some anthropologists are content to consider stylistic questions entirely within the taxonomic framework (i.e. identifying the provenance of museum specimens etc.) but most anthropologists associate ‘style' with ‘meaning' (Forge 1973). Anthropologists think of ‘style' as the attributes of artworks which associate those artworks with other cultural parameters, such as religious belief, kinship values, political competition, etc. Since often the associations in question are communicated via the iconography of images (e.g. a carving is a carving ‘of' a totemic animal), anthropological notions of style are fatally entangled with semiotic questions, to the detriment of conceptual clarity. I will return to the misalliance between the anthropology of art and semiotics later. For the moment, let us assume that iconography is not the relevant issue, but style, that is, formal attributes of artworks. Can ‘formal attributes of artworks' be associated with other cultural parameters? If so, an ‘anthropological' notion of style would focus on the psychological salience of artworks in directing attention towards cultural parameters. A ‘cultural' style-description would be an abstract account of the attributes of artworks in the light of their capacity to thematize and make cognitively salient essential cultural parameters.

zh: 8.2　汉森论风格与文化
en: 8.2　Hanson on Style and Culture

zh: 这类方案已有多位人类学家付诸实施，尽管未必打着“风格”分析的旗号（人类学著述中的“风格”常常径直被称为“美学”）。一个非常贴切的例子是汉森（1983）的文章，他在其中寻求“艺术形式与其他文化结构或文化模式之间的同构关系”（Hanson 1983: 79）。汉森的文章专论毛利（传统）艺术。首先，他正确地区分了上文提到的图像志与风格；不过他沿用阿奇（Archey 1965）的说法，谈的是“审美形式”，而不是直接用“风格”一词。他说，大多数毛利艺术并没有承载多少图像志象征（但参见 Neich 1996 及下文9.6节）。另一方面，这种艺术并不是“无意义”的装饰，因为毛利艺术的形式特征恰好“例示”了可以在毛利其他制度中察觉到的深层文化模式。他就艺术提出的主要实质性论点，是其中存在多种类型的对称、交替、旋转等（汉森的文章发表的那本文集中，沃什伯恩发表了她关于对称分析作为考古分类学方法的首篇论文，参见上文6.4–5节）。汉森把毛利艺术对对称的专注，与毛利文化所看重的一连串互惠行动，其中的竞争性交换、战争或复仇会逐步升级联系起来。其想法是：从毛利人的观点看，比方说椽木纹样中复杂而在认知上难以把握的对称类型，与毛利社会生活那个整体模式。这种模式也见于艺术之外的日常生活产生了共鸣——在那个模式中，各种层次、各种强度的互惠行动序列无处不在。此外，正如社会生活中的互惠从来不是“完美的”，而总是略微失衡，从而产生竞争进取的向前动力，毛利的两侧对称也总是因有意加入的不对称因素而略受干扰。这种把确认对称的因素与破坏对称的因素并置在一起的巧妙手法，与毛利文化“万物皆非其表象”的预设相吻合（Hanson 1983: 84）。
en: This kind of programme has been carried out by various anthropologists, though not necessarily under the heading of ‘style' analysis ('style' in anthropological writing is often simply called ‘aesthetics'). Very much a case in point is the article by Hanson (1983) in which he seeks ‘homologous relations between artistic forms and other structures or patterns of culture' (Hanson 1983: 79). Hanson's article is devoted to Maori (traditional) art. First of all, he correctly makes the distinction alluded to above between iconography and style; though he speaks of ‘aesthetic form' (following Archey 1965) rather than using the word ‘style' itself. Most Maori art was not heavily invested with iconographic symbolism, he says (but cf. Neich 1996 and below, Sect. 9.6). On the other hand, this art was not ‘meaningless' decoration because the formal characteristics of Maori art were such as to ‘instantiate' underlying cultural patterns detectable elsewhere in other Maori institutions. His main substantive point with regard to the art is the presence therein of many types of symmetry, alternations, rotations, etc. (Hanson's article was published in the volume in which Washburn published her initial paper on symmetry analysis as a method in archaeological taxonomy, cf. Sects. 6.4-5, above.) Hanson associates the preoccupation with symmetry in Maori art with the Maori cultural emphasis on sequences of escalating reciprocal competitive exchange and/or warfare and revenge. The idea is that from the Maori point of view, the presence of complex and cognitively inaccessible types of symmetry in, say, rafter-patterns, resonated with the global, extra-artistic, pattern of Maori social life in which sequences of reciprocal action, at various levels and degrees of intensity, were pervasive. Moreover, just as reciprocity in social life was never ‘perfect' but was always marginally unbalanced, giving rise to the onward momentum of competitive striving, so Maori bilateral symmetry is always marginally disturbed by contradictory elements of wilful asymmetry. This trickiness in the juxtaposition of symmetry-confirming and symmetry-disrupting elements coincided with the Maori cultural presupposition that ‘nothing is what it seems' (Hanson 1983: 84).

zh: 汉森的讨论非常有趣，是艺术人类学文献中最出色的贡献之一。但对他的论证可以提出某些明显的反驳。例如，“两侧对称”与“略微扰动的对称”这两样特征，如果你愿意，既属于“毛利风格”，也属于一种“普遍”风格——也就是说，任何纹样都显现对称，因为“纹样”之为纹样正在于此。“装饰艺术”大体上就是把纹样施加于物的表面，除非这些纹样以各种方式对称，否则就无法被辨认为纹样。实际情况是，存在着一种堪称纹样表面之“普遍美学”的东西：同样的对称构型——即使不是同样的母题——在世界各地都出现，沃什伯恩在她较近的研究中已充分证明这一点（Washburn and Crowe 1992）。用不对称因素破坏纹样表面对称的手法也是如此。此外，不对称往往并非全出于有意安排，因为制纹样者只关心使纹样“大致”对称，而不是数学上精确的对称。因此无法确定，毛利艺术中这些偏离对称之处究竟是有意为之，还是因为制作者无需追求精确对称。
en: Hanson's discussion is of great interest and is one of the most distinguished contributions to the literature of the anthropology of art. But there are certain obvious objections that can be raised to his argument. For instance, both ‘bilateral symmetry' and ‘slightly disturbed symmetry' are features, if you like, of a ‘universal' style as much as of ‘the Maori style'-that is to say, any pattern whatsoever manifests symmetry because that is what a ‘pattern' is. 'Decorative art', by and large, consists of the application of patterns to the surfaces of things, and unless these patterns were in various ways symmetrical, they would not be recognizable as patterns. As it is, there exists what amounts to a ‘universal aesthetic' of patterned surfaces; the same symmetry configurations, if not the same motifs, turn up all over the world, as Washburn has amply demonstrated in her more recent work (Washburn and Crowe 1992). So also does the technique of disrupting the symmetry of patterned surfaces with asymmetric elements. Besides which, asymmetries often arise semi-inadvertently because pattern-makers are concerned only to make their patterns ‘roughly' symmetrical, not mathematically so. One cannot be sure therefore that Maori disrupted symmetry is an intentional disruption of symmetry or merely an unconcern with exact symmetry.

zh: 于是可以反驳说，汉森关于两侧对称在毛利艺术中无处不在的论证，不过是他决定考察艺术的“形式”方面而非图像志方面所导致的同义反复。“形式的”归结为“装饰的”，“装饰的”归结为“有纹样的”，“有纹样的”归结为“对称的”。与此同时，难道要假定每一个生产装饰性（对称的、有纹样的）艺术的文化，都具有同样的互惠不断升级、又屡屡失衡之类的“文化模式”吗？泰姬陵是高度两侧对称的，铭文也使这种对称略有偏离——但没有人觉得应当把毛利会堂与泰姬陵相比，或根据这种对对称的建筑专注（它延伸到莫卧儿许多其他装饰艺术）来推断莫卧儿印度的互惠状况。
en: So it could be objected that Hanson's argument about the pervasiveness of bilateral symmetry in Maori art is just a tautologous consequence of his decision to look at ‘formal' rather than iconographic aspects of the art. ‘Formal' reduces to ‘ornamental', ‘ornamental' to ‘patterned', and ‘patterned' to ‘symmetrical'. Meanwhile, is one to assume that each and every culture that produces ornamental (symmetrical, patterned) art has the same ‘cultural pattern' of escalating and disrupted reciprocity, and so forth? The Taj Mahal is eminently bilaterally symmetrical, and slightly disrupted (by the inscriptions)-but nobody has seen fit to compare Maori meeting houses with the Taj Mahal, or to make inferences about reciprocity in Mughal India on the basis of this architectural preoccupation with symmetry (which extends to much other Mughal ornamental art).

zh: 我从这个相当根本的困难中得出结论：汉森的方案有些为时过早。汉森在毛利艺术中辨识出的形式属性，在各类装饰艺术中太过常见，无法承担他为它们设想的那种区分特定文化的作用。他说毛利艺术提供了毛利文化的一种“地图”；但如果这张“地图”的特征相对于毛利文化本身是任意的——既然它们也出现在莫卧儿印度这样完全不同的文化中，就必然如此——又怎能令人满意地证明这一点呢？其含义似乎是：把毛利艺术与毛利文化其余部分联系起来的，不是对称之类的“形式”审美属性或风格属性，而是艺术中对毛利祖先、神祇等的图像志指涉——这恰恰是汉森起初要质疑的立场。
en: I conclude from this rather fundamental difficulty that Hanson's project is somewhat premature. The formal properties Hanson identifies in Maori art are far too commonly observable in ornamental art of all kinds to serve the kind of culturally diacritic role he proposes for them. He says Maori art provides a kind of ‘map' of Maori culture; but how could this be demonstrated satisfactorily if the distinctive features of this ‘map' are arbitrary in relation to Maori culture specifically, as they must be, if they are also found in totally different cultures, such as Mughal India? The implication would seem to be that what connects Maori art to the rest of Maori culture is not ‘formal' aesthetic or stylistic attributes such as symmetry, but the presence in the art of iconographic reference to Maori ancestors, divinities, etc.-precisely the position which Hanson set out to question in the first place.

zh: 也许并未满盘皆输。汉森在文章结尾提出，毛利艺术品与毛利文化其余部分之间的关系是一种“提喻”关系；艺术品作为文化的一部分，重现了整个文化。必须承认，鉴于刚才提出的反驳，汉森未能证明艺术品作为部分与文化作为整体之间存在这种提喻关系。也许这是理论野心过大的结果；（比方说）一个椽木纹样所能拥有、同时整个文化也能拥有的属性，必然是高度抽象的。正因如此，像“对称”这样非常抽象的属性，几乎不可能只出现在该文化的艺术品中，而且只出现在该文化中。在特定艺术品与整个文化体系之间寻找共享属性，这一企图过于宏大，任何被认定为共通的特征都很可能是牵强附会的。尽管如此，“提喻”的想法仍然引人入胜，似乎与我们的一种直觉合拍：艺术风格与文化以某种幽晦的方式相连。让我们修改所提出的提喻关系，把问题的范围收窄。任何一件给定风格（个人的或集体的）中的给定艺术品，是否与该风格中的所有艺术品构成提喻关系？答案无疑是“是”——因为我们已经发掘出“风格”一词的一个基本含义，即风格属性使个别艺术品能够被归入共享这些特定属性的艺术品之类。于是，任何给定艺术品都“例示”了它出身于其中的物质文化传统的风格规范；它“代表”这种风格。这并没有立刻解决风格与文化的问题，但它提示了一个解决办法，后文将加以勾勒。
en: All is not lost perhaps. Hanson concludes his essay by suggesting that the relationship between Maori artworks and the rest of Maori culture is one of ‘synecdoche'; artworks are parts of culture which recapitulate the whole. It must be admitted that in the light of the objections just raised, Hanson has failed to demonstrate the existence of this synecdochic relationship between artworks as parts and cultures as wholes. Perhaps this is the result of excessive theoretical ambition; the attributes which (say) a rafter-pattern can possess, which can also be possessed by an entire culture, would inevitably be highly abstract ones. And for just this reason, it would be most unlikely that these very abstract properties, such as ‘symmetry', would be exclusively found in the artworks of that culture, and that culture alone. The search for shared attributes between particular artworks and entire cultural systems is so grandiose that whatever is discovered is likely to prove factitious. The idea of ‘synecdoche' is none the less intriguing, and seems to chime with our intuition that art styles and cultures are in some obscure way connected. Let us modify the proposed synecdochic relation so as to make the whole enterprise less ambitious. Is any given artwork, in a given style (personal or collective), related by synecdoche to all the artworks in that style? The answer to this is surely ‘yes'-because we have unearthed one of the basic implications of the word ‘style', namely, that style attributes enable individual artworks to be subsumed into the class of artworks which share these particular attributes. Consequently, any given artwork ‘exemplifies' the stylistic canons of the tradition of material culture from which it originates; it ‘stands for' this style. This does not immediately solve the problem of style and culture, but it suggests a solution which will be outlined later.

zh: 8.3　风格与认知显著性
en: 8.3　Style and Cognitive Saliency

zh: 同样的考虑也适用于沃尔海姆式的个体风格描述。例如，一件被视为例示某位艺术家——比如毕加索——个体风格的艺术品，把毕加索的艺术意图凸显为主题，因为它使人能够基于风格，在这件特定的毕加索作品与其他毕加索艺术品之间建立联系。即使事实上世上只有一件毕加索作品（《格尔尼卡》），情况也一样，只不过在这种情况下，风格分析将局限于对这件独一无二的艺术品不同部分——马、公牛、各个人物等——所显现的风格属性做概括。除非能在《格尔尼卡》这些部分与部分的关系中找到一致性，整幅画就会不属于任何特定风格，并因此“不可解读”（沃尔海姆语）。情况显然并非如此。《格尔尼卡》在风格上可解读、在心理上显著，因为画内部分与部分的关系与整体连贯一致；而《格尔尼卡》是“毕加索风格”（而非“《格尔尼卡》风格”）的一个实例，因为这幅画与其他毕加索画作连贯相关，那些画又与另一些画相关——以至于最终所有毕加索作品彼此之间都有迹可循。这是我们如此推崇毕加索的原因之一：无论他的手法如何变化，他仍然让人认得出他一贯的风格，尽管这很难确切把握。
en: The same considerations apply to Wollheim-type individual style-descriptions. An artwork which is being considered as exemplifying the individual style of an artist, for instance, Picasso, thematizes and makes salient Picasso's artistic intentions because it enables connections to be drawn, on the basis of style, between this particular Picasso and other Picasso artworks. Even if there were, in fact, only one Picasso in existence (Guernica), the same would be true, only in this case stylistic analysis would be confined to generalizing about the stylistic properties manifested in the different parts of this unique artwork-the horse, the bull, the various figures, and so on. Unless it were possible to find consistency in these part-to-part relationships in Guernica, the whole painting would be in no particular style, and would be ‘indecipherable' (as Wollheim put it) as a result. Such is manifestly not the case. Guernica is stylistically decipherable and psychologically salient because part-to-part relationships within the painting cohere with the whole, and Guernica is an instance of 'Picasso's style' (rather than ‘Guernica's style') because this painting is coherently related to other Picasso paintings, which are related to others still—so that ultimately all Picassos are intelligibly related to each. This is one of the reasons that we esteem Picasso so much; however much his manner transforms itself, he maintains a consistent stylistic identity, difficult though this is to pin down.

zh: 因此我希望人们会接受：“风格”把个别艺术品与“同一风格”的艺术品总体联系起来的功能，并不限于“分类学”领域；把“风格”用作兼具认知含义与分类含义的解释性概念，同样与之相关。遗憾的是，大多数关于“风格”的讨论确实聚焦于个别艺术品中的风格（例如“我们说《格尔尼卡》的‘风格’，是相对于其‘内容’或‘意义’而言的，这是什么意思？”，或者“《格尔尼卡》是不是‘立体主义’风格？”）。我倾向于不参照个别艺术品来思考“风格”，而是参照任何给定风格的全部作品所构成的“整体”来思考。“风格”是使人看出一件艺术品所属的整体，即那个“更大的统一体”。然而，这并不是退回到单纯的分类，因为按我的论证，艺术品的心理显著性是任何给定艺术品与同一风格中其他艺术品之间风格关系的函数。艺术品不是孤立地完成其认知工作的；它们之所以起作用，是因为彼此配合，形成合力，而它们协同作用的基础就是风格。这就是我们那种直觉的基础：艺术品之间的风格亲缘以某种方式呼应着把社会群体成员凝聚在一起的思想统一性；风格之于艺术品，犹如群体认同之于社会施动者。但在我们对“风格亲缘”究竟意味着什么——尤其就集体风格而言，比如传统毛利艺术家所遵循的那种——获得清晰得多的理解之前，这充其量只是一个模糊的观念。
en: I hope it will be accepted, therefore, that the function of ‘style' in associating individual artworks with the totality of artworks ‘in the same style' is not confined to the ‘taxonomic' domain, but is equally pertinent with respect to the use of ‘style' as an explanatory concept with cognitive, as well as classificatory implications. It is unfortunately true that most discussions of ‘style' focus on style in individual artworks (e.g. ‘What do we mean by the "style" of Guernica, as opposed to the "content" or "significance"?', or, ‘Is Guernica in the "cubist" style or not?'). I prefer to think of ‘style' with reference not to individual artworks but in relation to the ‘wholes' constituted by all the works in any given style. ‘Style' is what enables any artwork to be referred to the whole(s), or ‘larger unities' to which it belongs. However, this is not to capitulate to mere taxonomy, because, according to my argument, the psychological saliency of artworks is a function of the stylistic relationship between any given artwork and other artworks in the same style. Artworks do not do their cognitive work in isolation; they function because they co-operate synergically with one another, and the basis of their synergic action is style. This is the basis of the intuition we have that in some way stylistic affinity among works of art echoes the unity of thought which binds members of social groups together; style is to artworks what group-identification is to social agents. But this is at best a cloudy notion until we have arrived at a much clearer understanding as to exactly what 'stylistic affinity' means, particularly with reference to collective styles, such as the one observed by traditional Maori artists.

zh: 如前所述，汉森在他那个野心过大的尝试中，想在毛利艺术与毛利社会文化实践之间寻找统一模式，却只在艺术中寻找“无处不在的两侧对称”之类的抽象属性。他没有非常细致地考察艺术，因为这类对称几乎可以在毛利人制作过的每一件人工制品中找到，所以他选择哪些具体例子并不太要紧。不幸的是，这种不系统的方法无法排除这样一种可能性：被挑出来的抽象风格特征，同样容易在非毛利艺术中察觉到——事实正是如此。如何克服这个问题？显然，要为毛利艺术提供一种不适用于任何其他艺术风格的风格描述，就必须对艺术做比仅仅察觉各种对称和／或不对称类型细致得多的分析。必须关注那些真正告诉我们某件特定艺术品是毛利艺术品的风格属性；例如表现人手的典型方式、无处不在的“蕨芽”母题，等等。换言之，必须对艺术进行形式分析，完全不参照“文化模式”。一旦形式分析产出一种风格描述，捕捉到毛利人工制品中的维系风格连贯的主轴，恰好把这些人工制品与任何其他文化的人工制品区分开来，那时也许就可以尝试把这一特定的风格描述同毛利文化的具体特点联系起来。汉森做不到这一点，因为他缺乏进行这种形式分析的方法，也无法在毛利风格的一切表现中辨识其连贯性的来源。
en: As we noted before, Hanson, in his over-ambitious attempt to find unifying patterns in Maori art and Maori socio-cultural practices, only looked for abstract properties such as ‘pervasive bilateral symmetry' in the art. He does not consider the art in very much detail because such symmetries can be found in almost every artefact the Maori ever made, so it does not matter much which specific examples he chooses. Unfortunately, this unsystematic approach cannot exclude the possibility that the abstract stylistic features singled out are such as can be just as easily detected in non-Maori art, as is the case. How can this problem be overcome? Clearly, in order to provide a style-description for Maori art which would be applicable to no other art style, the art must be subjected to a much more detailed analysis than the mere detection of a variety of types of symmetry and/or asymmetry. Attention has to be paid to the stylistic attributes which actually tell us that a particular artwork is a Maori artwork; for example, the typical way in which the human hand is represented, the omnipresent ‘fern-shoot' motif, and so on. In other words, a formal analysis of the art has to be undertaken, quite without reference to ‘cultural patterns'. Once formal analysis produces a style-description which captures axes of coherence in the Maori artefacts which distinguish just those artefacts from any other culture's artefacts, then it might be feasible to attempt to align this specific style-description with the specifics of Maori culture. This Hanson cannot do, because he lacks the methodology to undertake such a formal analysis or to identify the source of the coherence of the Maori style in all its manifestations.

zh: 8.4　形式分析与语言学幻象
en: 8.4　Formal Analysis and the Linguistic Chimera

zh: 可惜，“形式分析”在艺术人类学中不是时髦的做法。在解释人类学的时代，形式分析面临两重冷遇：它要么与老式民族学相联系，要么与“民族科学”的过度做法相联系。20世纪70年代“结构主义”符号学人类学的失败，对形式分析在艺术人类学中的地位产生了特别恶劣的影响。在那个时期，人们习惯于把各种体系都当作“语言”来讨论。亲属制度像语言，烹饪也像（Levi-Strauss 1970），表达敬意的行为也像（Goodenough 1956），于是艺术必然也像。艺术是（文化的）“视觉形式语言”。民族科学时期“语言模型”在文化分析中的支配地位，导致把语言学的方法应用于视觉“语言”：分解为“成分”，并编写成分的“短语结构语法”，即关于成分如何组合成“合式串”或可接受的“话语”的规则集。每种文化被设想为不仅拥有一种口头语言，还拥有各种非口头语言，其中之一就是（艺术）形式的语言，即“视觉语”。视觉语的“成分”是形式，典型的是椭圆、圆、线、锯齿形等几何形式。例如，短语结构规则会告诉你如何组合线与锯齿形，以便在努巴视觉语中生成一个合式的“毒蛇”话语（Faris 1971: 103）。人们在这类视觉语法上倾注了大量精力（Korn 1978），但可以说，成果与付出的劳动不相称。正如E·贡布里希在评论法里斯关于努巴身体彩绘的“视觉语法”时所说，这类分析的成品只相当于一份编织图样，同样不产生洞见。无论形式分析还有什么用处，为假定的“视觉语言”编写指南，教人重新合成“合式话语”，肯定不是其中之一。谁想知道如何按部就班地做努巴身体彩绘？除了努巴人没有谁——何况，以伪语言学形式提供的指令，相对于实际图案本身的简单性而言复杂得离谱；那些图案，最没有天赋的绘图者也能通过简单的观察与摹仿过程轻易复制。
en: ‘Formal analysis', alas, is not a fashionable procedure in the anthropology of art. The formal approach is doubly overshadowed in the age of interpretative anthropology, in that it is either associated with old-fashioned ethnology or with the excesses of ‘ethnoscience'. The failure of ‘structuralist' semiotic anthropology in the 1970s has had a particularly pernicious impact on the status of formal analysis in the anthropology of art. At that period, it was customary to discuss systems of all kinds as ‘languages'. Kinship was language-like, so was cookery (Levi-Strauss 1970), so was respect-behaviour (Goodenough 1956), and so, necessarily, was art. Art was the (cultural) ‘language of visual forms'. The dominant position of the ‘linguistic model' in cultural analysis in the ethnoscience period resulted in the application, to visual ‘language' of the linguistic method of decomposition into ‘constituents' and the writing of constituent ‘phrase-structure grammars', that is, sets of rules about how constituents could be combined into ‘well-formed strings', or acceptable ‘utterances'. Each culture was imagined to possess, not just a verbal language, but various non-verbal languages, one of which was the language of (artistic) form, or ‘visual-ese'. The ‘constituents' of visual-ese were forms, typically geometric forms such as ovals, circles, lines, zigzags, and so on. The phrase-structure rules would, for instance, tell one how to combine lines and zigzags so as to generate a well-formed utterance of ‘poisonous snake' in, for instance, Nuba visual-ese (Faris 1971: 103). A great deal of effort was lavished on visual grammars of this kind (Korn 1978) but it is fair to say that the results were not commensurate with the labour expended. As E. Gombrich remarked, in a review of Faris's ‘visual grammar' of Nuba body-painting, the end-product of this type of analysis was only equivalent to a knitting-pattern, and no more productive of insight. Whatever formal analysis might be good for, providing instructions as to how to re-synthesize ‘well-formed utterances' in putative ‘visual languages' is not one of them. Who wants to know how to do Nuba body-painting by being given step-by-step instructions? Nobody but a Nuba-besides which, the instructions provided in pseudo-linguistic form are inordinately complicated given the simplicity of the actual designs themselves; which can be easily copied by the most untalented draughtsman by a simple process of inspection and imitation.

zh: 语言模型之所以搁浅，是因为视觉世界中不存在与自然语言的多重层次相对应的“层次”等级——自然语言的层次从“最小成分”（音位）向上延伸到语素（词），再到句法结构（短语和句子中的词，表达命题）。线、圆、椭圆、锯齿形等不是“视觉音位”（视素）。视觉音位的观念之所以流行，部分是由于艺术家的一些著名说法，尤其是塞尚（他只是重复美术学院的流行见解）所说：视觉形式都可以还原为立方体、圆锥体、圆柱体等。形式可以由以平面几何或立体几何界定的“基本积木”组装而成，这一想法不仅古老，而且实用——艺术家实际处理绘画任务时常常正是这样着手的；而且，如果马尔的视觉理论正确（Marr 1982），几何类的“基本积木”也许确实在视觉感知过程中起作用。但这一切都与音位毫不相干。立方体、圆柱体、圆锥体等代表或表现对象的物理部分，还原到几何的骨架；而音位并不表现语素——音位的组合——所表现之物的部分。语素表现语言编码中的概念，音位却不表现这些概念的部分。
en: The linguistic model founders because there is no hierarchy of ‘levels' in the visual world corresponding to the multiplicity of levels in natural languages, extending upwards from ‘minimal constituents' (phonemes) to morphemes (words) to syntactic structures (words in phrases and sentences, expressing propositions). Lines, circles, ovals, zigzags, etc. are not ‘visual phonemes' (visemes). The notion of visual phonemes gained currency partly as a result of certain well-known statements made by artists, notably Cezanne (who was only repeating the received wisdom of the art schools) that visual forms could all be reduced to cubes, cones, cylinders, etc. The idea that forms can be assembled from ‘basic building blocks' definable in terms of plane or solid geometry is not only ancient, but also practical, to the extent that this is often how artists actually do approach the task of drawing, and indeed, ‘basic building blocks' of a geometric kind may actually be implicated in the process of seeing, if Marr's theory of vision is correct (Marr 1982). But none of this bears any relation to the phoneme. Cubes, cylinders, cones, etc. stand for, or represent, physical parts of objects, reduced to their geometrical bare bones, whereas phonemes do not represent parts of what morphemes-combinations of phonemes-represent. Morphemes represent concepts within the linguistic code, but phonemes do not represent parts of these concepts.

zh: 几何形式作为图形符号出现时，本身就有意义（一个圆可以表现一只眼睛）；当它们作为其他图形符号的部分（组件）出现时（一个圆表现眼的虹膜，包在一个椭圆之内），它们代表整个图形符号所表现之物的部分（虹膜作为眼睛的部分）。相比之下，dog一词中的字母d并不代表狗的一部分，og也不代表狗的其余部分。然而，包含在狗的图画中的任何一条线，都表现狗的某个部分。构成再现性图像的各条线与整幅图像之间的关系，在逻辑上与音位和语素之间的部分—整体关系截然不同。因此，把视觉呈现分解为“元素”或“成分”、指望编写“视觉语法”的整个策略，都是误入歧途。
en: Where geometric forms occur as graphic signs, they are meaningful in themselves (a circle can represent an eye) and where they occur as parts (components) of other graphic signs (a circle representing the iris of an eye, enclosed within an oval) they stand for parts of whatever the graphic sign as a whole represents (the iris as part of the eye). By contrast, the letter ‘d' in dog, does not stand for part of a dog, and ‘og' for the remainder of the dog. Any line which is included in a drawing of a dog, however, represents some part of a dog. The relationships between the lines entering into the composition of a graphic representation, and the representation as a whole are logically quite distinct from the part-whole relationship between the phonemes and morphemes. Consequently, the whole strategy of decomposing visual presentations into ‘elements' or ‘constituents' in the hope of writing ‘visual grammars' is misconceived.

zh: 8.5　提喻：贯通风格整体的主轴
en: 8.5　Synecdoche: Axes of Coherence in Stylistic Unities

zh: 形式的风格分析必须关注作为整体的视觉形式，而不是它们的几何成分。
在我看来，形式分析的目标是为风格讨论提供基础。在确定风格单位的范围之前——即如前所述，是一位个体艺术家的作品，还是一个文化／时代的作品，等等——风格是一个没有意义的观念。
en: The stylistic analysis of forms has to concern itself with visual forms as wholes, rather than with their geometrical constituents.

The aim of formal analysis, as I see it, is to provide a basis for the discussion of style. Style is a meaningless idea until it has been decided what the scope of the unit of style is, that is to say, the works of an individual artist, a culture/period, etc. as discussed previously.

zh: 本章要分析的“更大统一体”，是马克萨斯的人工制品，尤其是卡尔·冯·登·施泰因得以接触的那批器物。他于1925–8年出版了一部插图宏富的三卷本马克萨斯物质文化论著；此前他曾在1898年亲赴群岛，采集自己的藏品，做民族志记录，并记下下文将讨论的纹身图案。形式风格分析的目标，是展示每件具体的器物如何与整批器物相联系。为此，完全不需要借助任何语言学类比。
en: In the present chapter, the ‘larger unity' which will be analysed is the corpus of Marquesan artefacts, in particular the corpus available to Karl von den Steinen, who published a lavishly illustrated three-volume treatise on Marquesan material culture in 1925-8, having visited the islands himself in 1898 in order to make his own collections, document them ethnographically, and record the tattoo designs which will be discussed below. The aim of formal stylistic analysis is to show how each particular item in the corpus is connected to the corpus as a whole. In order to do this, there is no need to make any use at all of any linguistic analogy.

zh: 然而，形式分析在某种意义上内在地是符号学的，即使不是语言学的。这个意义就是：任何部分都“代表”它所属的整体（提喻；参见上文）。任何一件马克萨斯艺术品，都或多或少具有所属作品集合的典型特征，也确实代表了那个集合。这种意义上的“代表”显然是一种符号学关系：对象是符号，而它所指的，是它所属的、在风格上彼此关联的那批作品。这种“提喻”在语义上提供的信息不多，因为其中每一件作品所意指的几乎完全是同一个东西，即除它自身之外的所有其他作品。
en: However, there is a sense in which formal analysis is intrinsically semiotic, if not linguistic. This is the sense in which any part ‘stands for' the whole of which it is a part (synecdoche; cf. above). Any example of Marquesan art is, to a greater or lesser extent, representative of the corpus to which it can be referred, and does indeed represent it. ‘Representing' in this sense is clearly a semiotic relation, in which the object is a sign, and the corpus of stylistically related objects from which it is drawn, is what is signified thereby. This kind of ‘synecdoche' is not very semantically informative, since every work in the corpus signifies almost exactly the same thing, namely all the other ones except itself.

zh: 不过，提喻确实提示了另一个思考风格的有用隐喻。有一种被称为全息图的图像（通过拍摄相干激光光源照亮的物体所反射的干涉条纹制成），它有一个奇特的性质：全息图像的任何部分，都包含全息图整体所含的信息，只是清晰度下降了。例如，从全息图的左下角，就可以（把激光照到蚀刻的全息底板上）重建原物的图像，尽管相当模糊。艺术中的风格与此类似：从一组作品中的一件或若干件出发，至少可以在某种程度上重建其余物品。当然，除非考察整批作品，否则并不知道给定对象的哪些特征是风格上显著的或提供信息的，所以这个类比并不精确。结合其他作品来看，每一件作品都是整批作品的缩影。我们之所以会这样看，是因为已经了解它所从属的那个更广大的整体。
en: However, synecdoche does suggest another useful metaphor for thinking about style. There is a kind of image known as a hologram (made by photographing the interference fringes reflected off objects illuminated by a coherent laser light-source) which has the curious property that any part of a holographic image contains an attenuated version of the information contained in the hologram as a totality. From, say, the bottom left-hand corner of a hologram, it is possible to reconstitute (by shining laser light onto the etched holographic plate) the image of the original object, though rather blurred. Style in art is like this in the sense that from one item in the corpus (or a selection of them) it is possible to reconstruct the others to at least some degree. Of course, one does not know which features of a given object are the stylistically significant or informative ones except with reference to the corpus as a whole, so the analogy is inexact. Each object, seen in the light of all the others in its corpus, appears as a microcosm of the corpus because our perception of it is informed by our knowledge of the macrocosm of which it is a fragment.

zh: 这种情形类似于古生物学家：他必须基于一块骨头重建一个灭绝物种，正如居维叶男爵那著名的本领所示。居维叶能够基于比方说一根股骨重建整只动物，因为他熟悉的不仅是股骨与骨架中相邻骨骼的关系，还有所考察脊椎动物属的骨骼架构中“关系之间的关系”。可以说，他把一根股骨看作形态已知的动物股骨的变换版本；把在这根孤立股骨上看到的那同一套一贯的变换，应用于灭绝动物骨架的所有其他骨骼，他就能重建其形态。换言之，他通过与相关物种股骨的比较，推断出这根股骨的“风格”，并把这种“风格变换”应用于骨架其余部分缺失的骨骼。单块骨头与骨架之间的关系是“全息式的”，不是因为孤立的骨头在外形上与其他缺失的骨头相似，而是因为相关形式的比较揭示了怎样从已知骨骼经由变换来“生成”缺失的骨骼。
en: The position is akin to that of the palaeontologist, who has to reconstruct an extinct species on the basis of a single bone, as Baron Cuvier was famously able to do. Cuvier could reconstruct an entire animal on the basis of say, a single femur, because he was familiar, not just with the relationship between the femur and adjacent bones in the skeleton, but with the ‘relations between relations' in the skeletal architecture of the vertebrate genus under consideration. He could, so to speak, see a femur as a transformed version of the femur of animals whose morphology was known, and by applying the same consistent series of transformations seen in the isolated femur to all the other bones of the extinct animal's skeleton, he could reconstruct its form. He could, in other words, infer the ‘style' of the femur by comparison with the femurs of related species, and he could apply this ‘style transformation' to the missing bones of the rest of the skeleton. The relation between the single bone and the skeleton is ‘holographic' not because the isolated bone outwardly resembles in form the other, missing ones, but because the comparison of related forms suggests a transformational rule for ‘generating' missing bones from known ones.

zh: 与其把形式分析看作符号学的附庸，不如把它设想为应用于视觉对象的“形态学”，这更有助益。目标是通过相关形式的比较，得出一系列变换，使给定的艺术品或人工制品能够转换为其他作品。当然，目标不是像造假者那样应用这些变换去“生产”新的（假想的）艺术品。制作赝品不需要对风格理论做智识上的精加工，那是一个相当直觉的过程。形式分析的目的，是在汇集起来供分析的作品中，找出贯通各件作品的主轴。一旦这些维系风格连贯的主轴被辨识出来，就有可能理解一种“文化”风格怎样使文化特征凸显出来，容易被人认知。
en: Rather than think of formal analysis as an adjunct to semiotics, it is more helpful to imagine it as ‘morphology' applied to visual objects. The aim is to derive, by the comparison of related forms, a series of transformations through which given artworks or artefacts can be converted into other ones. The aim is not, of course, to apply these transformations so as to ‘produce' new (hypothetical) artworks in the way a maker of forgeries does. The making of forgeries requires no intellectual elaboration of stylistic theory, being a quite intuitive process. The purpose of formal analysis is to identify axes of coherence within the corpus of works brought together for the purpose of stylistic analysis. Once these axes of stylistic coherence have been identified, it then becomes possible to understand the cognitive significance of a ‘cultural' style in rendering features of the culture cognitively salient.

zh: 某种意义上，感知“贯通各部分的主轴”和运用变换规则，本来就是视觉过程的一部分。任何熟悉的对象，比如一把剪刀，能在视网膜上投下无数差异很大的影像，大脑必须加以解释。从手柄一端正面看去，一把剪刀可能显现为一根扁平的金属条，中间有奇怪的明暗，在任何明显的方面都不像我们关于剪刀的“标准”图像（即我们可能放进图解词典的那种剪刀图）。但按吉布森（1986: 73–5）的说法，我们的视觉系统能够识别立体物体。观察点一移动，我们便能把眼下的视图与同一物体的其他视图对应起来。轮廓复杂的对象被看作“结构在变换下保持不变”。同样，风格分析寻找“变换下的结构不变量”，它们界定的是比孤立对象——比如一把剪刀——更高层级的对象。于是，“伦勃朗的全部作品”可以被看作不是一批分离对象的集合，而是一个有许多部分分布在许多不同地方的单一对象。一个由一组从属对象构成的单一对象并不难想象；一套十二件的餐具就是这样一个对象，一副棋具是另一个。如果我们把伦勃朗的“全集”当作这样一个复合的或“分布式的”对象，那么就会看到，确定伦勃朗“风格”的过程，与确定一把剪刀之类的吉布森式对象的“变换下的不变量”的过程完全相同。“变换下的不变量”就是把任何一件伦勃朗作品与所有其他作品联系起来的东西；但除非我们能看出这些结构不变者是什么，我们就没有把这件特定的伦勃朗作品“作为伦勃朗”来看，即没有把它看作某位画家整个创作的一部分。对伦勃朗的“训练有素的眼光”不外乎此。我主张，风格知觉就是我们处理这类复合的或分布式对象的知觉方式。就此而言，风格理论只是知觉理论本身的延伸。不过，要把伦勃朗作品中的“变换下的不变量”概念化，是一项非常专门的任务，我不打算承担——尽管我相信这将相当于一种沃尔海姆式的“风格描述”。就马克萨斯艺术而言，把这种风格连贯性观念操作化要容易得多，因为正如我即将展示的，马克萨斯艺术特别适合以视觉上显著的形态变换来分析。伦勃朗的风格隐藏在他笔触处理的微妙之处，而马克萨斯风格——或我们现在能接触到的那部分——用纸和笔就能发掘出来。
en: In a sense, cognitive sensitivity to ‘axes of coherence' and the application of transformational rules is built into the process of seeing itself. Any familiar object, such as a pair of scissors, is intrinsically capable of casting infinitely many highly dissimilar images on the retina, which the brain has to interpret. Looked at end-on, from the handle end, a pair of scissors may appear as a flat bar of metal, curiously shaded in the middle, resembling the ‘canonical' picture we have of scissors in no obvious respect (i.e. the picture of scissors we might insert in an illustrated dictionary). But our visual system, according to Gibson (1986: 73-5), is tuned to detecting solid objects because they map onto other available views of the same object that can be obtained by shifting the point of observation. An object of complicated contours is seen as ‘structurally invariant under transformation'. In the same way, style analysis looks for the ‘structural invariants under transformation' which define objects of a higher hierarchical order than the isolated object, such as a pair of scissors. Thus, ‘all the works of Rembrandt' could be considered, not a collection of separate objects, but just one object with many parts distributed in many different places. A single object which is a set of subordinate objects is not hard to imagine; a twelve-piece dinner set is one such object, a chess-set another. If we take Rembrandt's ‘complete works' as such a multiple, or ‘distributed' object, then it will be seen that the process of determining Rembrandt's ‘style' is precisely the same as the process of determining the ‘invariants under transformation' of a Gibsonian object, such as a pair of scissors. What is ‘invariant under transformation' is what links any one Rembrandt work to all the others, but unless we can see what these invariants of structure are, we are not seeing this, particular Rembrandt, ‘as a Rembrandt', that is, as a component of an oeuvre. ‘Educated perception' of a Rembrandt amounts to nothing else. Stylistic perception, I argue, is the perceptual mode with which we deal with multiple or distributed objects of this kind. As such, stylistic theory is just an extension of the theory of perception itself. However, it is a very specialized task to conceptualize what the ‘invariants under transformation' in Rembrandt's works are, and I do not propose to undertake it-though I believe that this would amount to a Wollheim-type ‘style-description'. It is much easier to operationalize this notion of stylistic coherence with respect to Marquesan art, because, as I will shortly demonstrate, Marquesan art is particularly susceptible to analysis in terms of visually salient morphological transformations. Rembrandt's style is hidden in the subtleties of his handling, whereas Marquesan style-or such of it as we now have access to—can be disinterred with paper and pencil.

zh: 8.6　马克萨斯器物集
en: 8.6　The Marquesan Corpus

zh: 施泰因（1925）汇集的马克萨斯器物在风格上连贯一致，特别适合做形态学研究。这批器物分成几类，其中最重要的是：(i) 纹身母题，(ii) 长笛等人工制品上的类似装饰，(iii) 平面刻纹，即极浅浮雕的雕刻，(iv) 三维雕刻，有些尺寸宏大，但许多是小尺寸乃至微型的。在这些类目中，纹身母题无疑最重要、记录也最充分，尽管在欧洲接触早期（18世纪末至19世纪中叶），马克萨斯人大量制作和使用各类器物。马克萨斯社会对华美与炫耀的取向，超过任何其他波利尼西亚社会，新西兰毛利人可能是例外（参见 Gell 1993；Thomas 1990）。我稍后再多谈马克萨斯社会的社会、政治与意识形态特征。眼下我只关心马克萨斯艺术严格的形式方面，只需指出：几乎所有马克萨斯艺术都附着于人体（如纹身、饰身）。此外，那些并非内在地属于人体一部分的艺术（如武器、独木舟、房屋陈设等），在概念上被当作人体的一部分来对待。于是，酋长的独木舟是他身体的一部分，有一个专名，那也是酋长自己的几个名字之一；独木舟受到伤害，就是他受到伤害，如此等等。因此，像施泰因那样从纹身艺术开始研究马克萨斯艺术是合理的，因为这种艺术确实为所有其他艺术确立了模式。
en: The artefacts in the Marquesan corpus assembled by Steinen (1925) are particularly suited to morphological study, because they form a very coherent set. The corpus consists of a number of categories of artefacts, of which the most important are (i) tattooing motifs, (ii) similar decoration on artefacts such as flutes, (iii) incised work on the flat, that is, carving in very low relief, and (iv) three-dimensional carving, some of it monumental but much of it on a small, and even miniature scale. Of these categories, tattooing motifs are certainly the most important and best documented, though during the early period of European contact (from the late eighteenth to the middle of the nineteenth century) the Marquesans were prolific producers and consumers of artefacts of all kinds. Marquesan society was orientated towards magnificence and display to a greater extent than any other Polynesian society, with the possible exception of the Maori of New Zealand (see Gell 1993; Thomas 1990). I will say more about the social, political, and ideological characteristics of Marquesan society at a later stage. For the present I am concerned only with strictly formal aspects of Marquesan art, and it is sufficient to note only that almost all Marquesan art was attached to the human body (e.g. tattooing, adornment). Moreover, the art that was not intrinsically part of the human body (e.g. weapons, canoes, furnishings of houses, etc.) was conceptually treated as if it were. Thus, a chief's canoe was part of his body, had a personal name which was one of his own set of names, if injury was done to it, injury was done to him, and so on. Consequently, it is reasonable to commence the study of Marquesan art, as Steinen did, by considering tattoo art, in that this art really sets the pattern for all the others.

zh: 下面的分析从施泰因那里获得的，远不止所用的资料。施泰因没有引用他那个时代母题分析的艺术史文献——里格尔、古德伊尔与维克霍夫的著作，贡布里希（1984: 180–200）已为我们发掘出来——但他大概知道这些著作，因为施泰因那一代艺术专家对它们都很熟悉。施泰因的理论框架（与里格尔的一样）是进化论的；他关心的是勾勒母题的历史：从马克萨斯纹身最早图像中记录的相对“写实”的版本（尤其是兰斯多夫关于1804年的记录（1813–14）

），到他自己在19世纪90年代记录的抽象得多的版本。但进化论与比较的思辨并不占主导；他也花大量注意力于母题的共时变异，特别是只能描述为母题与形式之间的派生关系或变换关系的东西。他在一系列分析图中阐明这些关系，那些图常常既巧妙又富于启发。施泰因自己绘制全部插图，是一位能力非凡的绘图艺术家；他那部三卷本的马克萨斯著作，堪称人类学学科有史以来出版的美学上最精湛的作品（该版本的设计与版式是藏书家的梦想）。我希望下面这些页面——我强调，它们非常广泛地依赖施泰因的原著——能促使更多人赏识他的贡献。我认为，他是物质文化领域中结构主义的先驱，正如他的同胞歌德是植物形态学领域的先驱。这个比较是贴切的：正如歌德设想所有植物都可以看作一种“原植物”（Ur-plant）的变异版本（预示了进化思想中的一个重要因素），施泰因也把马克萨斯母题与人工制品看作一系列原母题的变换：埃图阿（小神）、“面部”母题、“手形纹”（chiroid，半卵形）、“编织”母题，等等。正如他所展示的，这些母题每一个都可以变换为其他母题。施泰因对母题的“派生”或“词源”的专注，嵌在他19世纪的演化（或退化）观之中，在这一点上我不打算追随他。相反，我要论证，他所展示的母题变换与派生无法放进进化论框架，因为资料缺乏足够的时间深度；所有可靠的纹身视觉记录都来自跨越世纪之交的那二十年，而马克萨斯纹身的早期图像，包括兰斯多夫的，准确性存疑。甚至施泰因讨论的雕刻人工制品，也几乎全是（大概）19世纪的。我希望展示，马克萨斯艺术的风格特征，最好用共时的意识形态与文化力量来解释，而施泰因由于进化论的专注，倾向于忽视这些力量。
en: The following analysis owes much more to Steinen than the data it uses. Steinen does not cite the art-historical literature of motif-analysis of his period, the work of Riegel, Goodyear, and Wickhoff, which has been excavated for us by Gombrich (1984: 180-200), but he probably knew of it, since these works were well known to art experts of Steinen's generation. Steinen's theoretical framework (like Riegel's) is evolutionary; he is concerned to chart the history of motifs from relatively ‘realistic' versions documented in the earliest images of Marquesan tattooing (especially from Langsdorff's publication of 1804 (1813-14)) to the very much more abstract versions he himself documented in the 1890s. But evolutionary and comparative speculation hardly predominates; he also devotes a great deal of attention to synchronic variation in motifs, and particularly what one can only describe as derivational or transformational relationships between motifs and forms. These he elucidates in a series of analytical figures which are frequently both ingenious and revelatory. Steinen, who made all his own illustrations, was a graphic artist of remarkable ability, and his three-volume work on the Marquesas is arguably the most aesthetically accomplished work ever to have been published in the discipline of anthropology (the design and layout of the edition is a bibliophile's dream). I hope that the following pages, which, I emphasize, rely very extensively on Steinen's original work, will encourage wider appreciation of his contribution. He was, I think, a forerunner of structuralism in the domain of material culture, like his compatriot Goethe in the domain of plant morphology. The comparison is apt, in the sense that just as Goethe imagined that all plants could be seen as modified versions of an ‘Ur-plant' (anticipating an important element in evolutionary thought) so Steinen sees Marquesan motifs and artefacts as transformations of a series of Ur-motifs, the etua (godling), the ‘face' motif, the ‘chiroid' (halfoval), the ‘woven' motif, and so on. Each of these can be transformed into the others, as he demonstrates. Steinen's preoccupation with the ‘derivation' or ‘etymology' of motifs is embedded in his nineteenth-century evolutionary (devolutionary) mind-set, and to this extent I shall not follow him. On the contrary, I would argue that the motivic transformations and derivations he demonstrates cannot be placed in an evolutionary framework, since the data lack sufficient time-depth; all the reliable visual documentation of tattooing comes from the twenty years spanning the turn of the present century, while early representations of Marquesan tattooing, including Langsdorff's, are of questionable accuracy. Even the carved artefacts Steinen discusses are almost entirely of (probable) nineteenth-century date. I hope to show that the stylistic features of Marquesan art are best explained in terms of synchronic ideological and cultural forces that Steinen tended to overlook, because of his evolutionary preoccupations.

zh: 无论马克萨斯艺术中的变换关系或派生关系该如何解释，首要之务是证明它们的存在，在这里我沿用施泰因的做法。
en: In whatever way the transformational or derivational relationships in Marquesan art are to be explained, the first necessity is to demonstrate their existence, and here I follow in Steinen's footsteps.

zh: 马克萨斯艺术风格是一套艺术实践的集合，展现出视觉上立即可见的连贯性，但只有细致的母题分析才能充分揭示。就本分析而言，母题之间的“关系”用一些程序来表达，这些程序使人能够把任何给定的母题（或形式）变成这批作品中的另一个母题（或形式）。与20世纪70年代民族科学的母题分析或“视觉语言”分析相反，目标不是从母题的元素“生成”母题，而是经由规定的步骤从一个母题行进到另一个母题；也就是说，分析只预设一个层次，即母题（或形式）的层次。母题之所以可辨认，既因为它们在这批作品中以相同形式反复出现（也有变异形式），也因为它们有记录在案的母题名称，其中一些颇能透露文化信息，尽管绝非全部。此阶段我不讨论母题名称的含义，但为方便起见，将用马克萨斯名称来标识母题。
en: The Marquesan art style is an assemblage of artistic practices demonstrating a coherence which is visually immediately apparent, but which only careful motif-analysis can fully reveal. For the purposes of this analysis ‘relationships' between motifs are expressed by procedures which permit one to turn any given motif (or form) into another motif (or form) found in the corpus. By contrast to the motif-analyses of 1970s ethnoscience or ‘visual language' analyses, the aim is not to ‘generate' motifs from their elements, but to proceed, via specified steps, from one motif to another; that is, the analysis presupposes only one level, that of the motif (or form). Motifs are recognizable both because they recur in identical form repeatedly in the corpus (as well as modified forms) and because they have documented motif-names, some of which are culturally revealing, though by no means all of them. I will not discuss the implications of motif-names at this stage, but I will use the Marquesan names to identify motifs as a matter of convenience.

zh: 在这批马克萨斯作品中，从一个母题变成另一个母题，可采用以下变换：
en: The types of procedures for transforming one motif in the Marquesan corpus into another motif can be briefly enumerated at this stage. They are:

zh: (i) 平面刚体运动（平面变换：平移、旋转、反射、滑移反射；参见 Washburn and Crowe 1988）；
en: (i) rigid motions in the plane (plane transformations: translation, rotation, reflection, glide reflection; cf. Washburn and Crowe 1988);

zh: (ii) 坐标变换（以达西·汤普森（1961: 第9章（1917））的变换为模型），即母题比例的改变；
en: (ii) coordinate transformations (modelled on those of D'Arcy Thompson (1961: ch. 9 (1917)), i.e. changes in the proportions of motifs;

zh: (iii) 层级化／分解（一个母题成为另一个母题的一部分，或从一个母题中分出一部分，使之成为独立的母题）；
en: (iii) hierarchization/decomposition (one motif becomes a component of another motif, or a component of a motif becomes a motif);

zh: (iv) 维度变换，即二维母题变换为三维母题，反之亦然。
en: (iv) transformations of dimensionality, i.e. a two-dimensional motif is transformed into a three-dimensional motif and vice versa.

zh: 这些程序既可以应用于整个母题，也可以应用于母题的部分。于是，为了把一个母题变换为另一个母题，可以把它拆开，仅对其中一部分施加平面运动、改变相对比例等。
en: These procedures can be applied both to motifs as a whole, or to parts of motifs. Thus, in order to transform a motif into another motif it can be split apart, and just part of it may be subjected to a motion in the plane, or a change in relative proportions etc.

zh: 沿这些路线分析形式的结果，是创建一个母题之间的变换关系网络。这个关系网络没有中心，因为没有任何一个母题可以被看作其余母题都由之派生的始祖。理论上，这个网络中描述的所有关系都是对称的；如果母题A可以从母题B派生，那么母题B也可以从A派生，并不因此断定其中哪一个在演化上更早。然而，分析总得从某个地方开始，从一个视觉显著性尽可能大的母题开始无疑很方便。施泰因对纹身母题的讨论分为三部分：i.“编织源纹样”（Plectogene Muster）——与编辫、织席、编篮等相关的纹样；ii.“提基源纹样”（Tikigene Muster）——包含人体形象的纹样；iii.“面部母题”（Gesichtsmotiv）——显现面部或由面部派生的母题。我暂且把“编织源纹样”搁在一旁，集中讨论ii和iii，它们包含最复杂、视觉上最有趣的母题。这两者之中，冯·登·施泰因的“提基源纹样”提供了最自然的出发点。如前所述，马克萨斯艺术要么直接置于人身上，要么置于被当作人来对待的人工制品上。“提基源纹样”是这样一些母题：它们本质上通过在人物身上添画从属的小“人”，以图形方式复制他（参见上文关于分形人格的讨论，7.10–11节）。
en: The outcome of the analysis of forms along these lines is the creation of a network of transformational relationships among motifs. This network of relations has no centre in that there is no one motif which can be regarded as the apical ancestor from which all the rest are derivative. Theoretically, all the relations described in this network are symmetrical; if motif A can be derived from motif B, then motif B can be derived from A, there being no imputation of evolutionary priority either way. However, the analysis has to begin somewhere, and it is certainly convenient to commence with a motif which has as much visual saliency as possible. Steinen's discussion of tattoo motifs is divided into three sections; i. ‘Plectogene Muster' patterns which relate to plaiting, matting, basketry, etc.; ii. ‘Tikigene Muster’—patterns which contain images of the human body; and iii. ‘Gesichtsmotiv’—motifs which show or are derived from the face. I will leave ‘Plectogene Muster' aside for the moment and will concentrate on ii and iii, which comprise the most complicated and visually interesting motifs. Of these two, it is von den Steinen's ‘Tikigene Muster' which provide the most natural point of departure. As I noted earlier, Marquesan art was either placed directly on the human person, or on artefacts which were treated as persons. The ‘Tikigene Muster' are motifs which essentially reduplicate the person by appending additional, subsidiary ‘persons' to it in graphic form (cf. above on fractal personhood, 7.10–11).

zh: 因此，先从埃图阿（etua）说起。埃图阿是各类小神的通称。
en: The motif with which to commence therefore is etua, the generic word for any kind of godling.

. I shall use this table as a point of departure for exploring the entire range of Marquesan motifs. In this table Steinen distinguishes seven types of etua motifs (in rows) which he groups into two main classes; ‘standing' etua and ‘sitting' etua. No iconographic significance should be attached to this distinction, which is entirely conventional. A ‘standing' etua is one whose lower limbs form a convex curve relative to the body vertical, a ‘sitting' etua is one whose lower limbs form a concave curve relative to the body vertical: see

This is a typical instance of the ‘visual logic' of Marquesan art, and is the first of many examples of a similar kind that I will discuss.

zh: 查看埃图阿表即可发现，站姿或坐姿埃图阿的各类型表现出高度的可变性。最上面一行是取自浮雕雕刻的实例（石上、骨上，E则是玳瑁上的埃图阿剪影）。接下来两行站姿埃图阿是高度简化的形式，见于纹身或竹刻（其母题库与纹身相同）。我稍后处理这些简化形式，因为将会看到，它们汇入施泰因的另一大类“编织源纹样”，即“编辫或编织”母题。我起初将集中讨论第四、五行的“坐姿埃图阿”，尤其是L、M、N、O。L是G的线条化版本，用作纹身母题；M是它的对应形式，通过让“手”以竖轴反射（或者等价地，左右手互换）产生。要产生N的“方折螺旋”臂形，只需再做一次反射（以横轴反射）（
）。N的“腿”是把如此产生的“臂”以横轴反射，再逆时针旋转90度而产生的——这种腿形也可以看作出发点G中所见基本“坐姿”腿形的反射变异版本。
en: As inspection of the table of etua shows, types of standing or sitting etua show a high degree of variability. The uppermost row are examples taken from relief carving (on stone, bone, or in the case of E an etua silhouette in tortoiseshell). The next two rows of standing etua are very reduced forms, found in tattooing or in engraving on bamboo (whose motif repertoire is identical to tattooing). I will deal with these reduced forms later, since, as will be seen, they merge into Steinen's other major category of Plectogene Muster, ‘plaited or woven' motifs. It is on the ‘sitting etua' in the fourth and fifth rows that initially I shall concentrate, especially L, M, N, and O. L is a linear version of G, used as a tattoo motif, and M is its counterpart, produced by subjecting the ‘hands' to reflection in the vertical plane (or alternately, exchanging the left for the right hand and vice versa). To produce the ‘squared-off spiral' arm form of N, another reflection (in the horizontal plane) is all that is necessary (

). The ‘legs' of N are produced by subjecting the ‘arms' so produced, to a reflection in the horizontal plane and a rotation of 90 degrees anticlockwise—this leg-form can also be seen as a reflected, modified version of the basic ‘sitting' leg-form seen in G, the starting-point.

zh: O中可见一种略微不同的腿形，其余方面O与N是近亲。这种腿形与G相同，只是去掉了基部表示蹲坐姿势中大腿与小腿分界的小缺口。这条线加以复制，就产生I和K的手风琴式腿形，它们通向我稍后将提到的其他母题。但O的腿形（椭圆的四分之一）消除了这条线，可以视为一大类半圆形与抛物线形母题的起源。
en: A slightly different leg-form is seen in O, which is otherwise a close relative of N. This leg-form is the same as G but minus the nick at the base indicating the boundary between the thigh and calf of the leg in the squatting position. This line, duplicated, produces the concertina-like leg-forms of I and K, which lead towards other motifs I will mention later. But the leg-form of O (which is 1/4 of an ellipse) eliminates this line and can be treated as the origin of a very large class of semicircular and paraboloidal motifs.

zh: 母题O在男性纹身中是拟人化的，因为与L、M、N一样，它是凯纳的一种形式——凯纳是与纹身相关的神话英雄，被表现为坐姿埃图阿。但按施泰因获得的资料，女性纹身中相同的埃图阿形式名为凯阿（Kea），他认定指的是龟。在像这样的形式分析中，这些命名细节本来无关紧要，但有一点例外。马克萨斯人把各种龟和海龟都视为神圣的、神性的，所以龟类（testudo）作为神圣埃图阿出现在纹身母题中并不奇怪。但要注意：龟的标准视图在水平平面上，与地面平行；而坐姿埃图阿的标准视图相对于地面是垂直的。因此这里还有另一种“几何”变换，取决于把图像看成竖向剖面图还是水平俯视图：当观察者与埃图阿的隐含朝向从垂直转为水平时，坐姿埃图阿就变成了从上方俯瞰的龟神，母题的形态本身没有任何实际改变（
）。坐姿埃图阿的水平的龟形还能衍生出多种母题（我将在适当时候讨论的其他凯阿与卡凯形式）。
en: Motif O, in male tattooing, is anthropomorphic, since, like L, M, and N it is a form of Kena, a mythological hero connected with tattooing, who is shown as a sitting etua. But according to Steinen's information, the identical etua form in female tattooing is named Kea, which he identifies as referring to the tortoise. These details of nomenclature would be beside the point in a formal analysis such as this but for one thing. All members of the tortoise/turtle family were considered sacred and divine by the Marquesans, so there is nothing surprising about species of testudo appearing as sacred etua in tattoo motifs. The point to note though, is that the canonical view of a tortoise is in the horizontal plane, parallel with the earth, whereas the canonical view of a sitting etua is vertical relative to the plane of the earth. So there is another kind of ‘geometric' transformation here dependent on whether the image is viewed as a section or a plan: a sitting etua becomes, when the implied orientation of the observer and the etua are shifted from the vertical to the horizontal, a tortoise-divinity viewed from above, without any actual change in the morphology of the motif whatsoever (
). The horizontal (tortoise) form of the sitting etua is highly productive of further motifs (other forms of kea and kake which I will discuss in due course).

zh: 以O为出发点，我接下来考虑一个非常突出的母题，即名为霍佩韦希内（hope vehine）的那一个（字面意思是“臀部—女人”，我相信指的是背部相连的女性双神；参见 Gell 1993: 193）。这个母题可以用多种方式派生，但最容易的是从埃图阿的某种形式派生，比如
下一行中的O或“r”。在另一幅图中，施泰因通过比较取自纹身的一系列相关形式，非常清晰地展示了霍佩韦希内的派生（

）。该图显示，坐姿埃图阿经由埃图阿一条“腿”的缩减、以及对侧“臂”补偿性地变换为四分之一卵形，逐渐变成霍佩韦希内特有的形态，即两个位于直径两端的四分之一卵形（参见第1行ii、iv、v与第2行ii、iii，它们是标准的霍佩韦希内母题）。这种渐变提示了一条可能的演化路径，但如前所述，我感兴趣的不是进化关系，而是能够直接在一个图形上执行、把它转换为另一个图形而无需中间步骤的变换。因此，从我的观点看，更有用的是把坐姿埃图阿与霍佩韦希内之间的关系设想为
所示的样子。该图显示，把
所见形式的埃图阿垂直劈开，将其中一半旋转180度，再把两半重新接合，就能把埃图阿变换为霍佩韦希内。这产生了一个类似
第2行ii的霍佩韦希内。
en: Taking O as the starting-point, I shall next consider a very prominent motif which goes under the name of hope vehine (literally ‘buttocks-women', which I believe refers to back-to-back siamese-twin female divinities; cf. Gell 1993: 193). This motif can be derived in a number of ways, but most readily from a form of etua such as O or ‘r’ in the next row in
. In a separate figure, Steinen shows the derivation of hope vehine very perspicuously by the comparison of a series of related forms, taken from tattooing (

). This figure shows the sitting etua sliding, by degrees, into the form of diametrically opposed quarter-ovals which is distinctive of hope vehine via a reduction of one ‘leg' of the etua, and a compensating transformation of the ‘arm' on the opposite side into a quarter-oval form (cf. row 1, ii, iv, v, and row 2, ii, iii, which are standard hope vehine motifs). These smooth transitions indicate an evolutionary pathway, but, as I noted earlier, I am not so interested in evolutionary relationships as in transformations which can be carried out on one figure so as to convert it directly into another, without intermediary steps. Consequently, from my point of view, it is more useful to think of the relation between the sitting etua and hope vehine as shown on
. In this figure, it is shown that the etua can be transformed into hope vehine by splitting an etua of the form seen in
vertically, and rotating one half of it through 180 degrees before rejoining the two halves. This produces a hope vehine-like
, row 2, ii.

zh: 霍佩韦希内本身也可以再经变换，产生更多母题。我要考虑的第一个，是名为瓦伊奥凯纳（vai o Kena）的那一个，即“凯纳之浴”——凯纳就是前面提到的纹身英雄，他的神话我在别处已详细讨论过（Gell 1993: 186–8）。这个母题有三种记录在案的形式，每一种都以略微不同的方式从霍佩韦希内派生。瓦伊奥凯纳最基本的形式不过是一个霍佩韦希内加上它的镜像。另一种更复杂的瓦伊奥凯纳形式如
所示产生。在该图中，一个霍佩韦希内经反射与平移，形成一个与原形相邻并相连的反射副本。下一步是把这两个霍佩韦希内母题各自水平“拉伸”，使它们在中间重叠、彼此部分遮挡。这产生了一种站姿埃图阿母题的形式，其中双重霍佩韦希内相对的四分之一卵形成为“臂”，相连的四分之一卵形成为“腿”。再加上简化成痕迹的“头”和身体，它与埃图阿母题的合流便告完成。
en: Hope vehine, in turn, can be subjected to transformation so as to produce further motifs. The first of these I shall consider is the one known as vai o Kena, the bath of Kena, the tattooing hero mentioned earlier, whose mythology I have discussed at length elsewhere (Gell 1993: 186-8). There are three documented forms of this motif, each of which is derived from hope vehine in a slightly different way. The most elementary form of vai o Kena consists of no more than a hope vehine and its reflection. A different, more complex, form of vai o Kena is produced as shown in

. In this figure, a hope vehine is subjected to reflection and translation so as to form a reflected duplicate adjacent to the original, to which it is joined. The next step is to ‘stretch' each of these hope vehine motifs horizontally so that they overlap in the middle and partially occlude each other. This produces a form of standing etua motif, in which the opposed quarter-ovals of the double hope vehine become ‘arms' and the conjoined quarter-ovals become ‘legs'. The merging between this and the etua motif is completed by the addition of vestigial ‘head' and body elements.

zh: 瓦伊奥凯纳最复杂的版本也以霍佩韦希内为基础（
，III）。要产生这个瓦伊奥凯纳，先把霍佩韦希内母题复制并旋转90度。然后把所得叠合的霍佩韦希内母题拉开，产生一个面积为原来四倍的正方形母题，每个四分之一卵形占据一角。在这些四分之一卵形之间，霍佩韦希内中原有的黑色凹透镜形（如今已复制）显现为一个黑色的X，沿对角线把它们连接起来。最后，霍佩韦希内顶部与底部那些未包含在四分之一卵形之内的小方形形式向下延伸，成为母题的中轴，表现正在沐浴的凯纳。
en: The most complex version of vai o Kena is also based on hope vehine (

, III). To produce this vai o Kena the hope vehine motif is first of all duplicated and rotated 90 degrees. The resulting superimposed hope vehine motifs are then drawn apart so as to produce a square motif four times larger, in which each quarter-oval occupies one corner. Between these quarter-ovals, the original black concave lens shape seen in hope vehine (now duplicated) appears as a black X joining them diagonally. Finally, the small square forms on the top and the bottom of hope vehine, not included within the quarter-ovals, are extended down to become the central axis of the motif, representing Kena in his bath.

zh: 8.9　从霍佩韦希内到卡凯／凯阿
en: 8.9　From Hope Vehine to Kake/Kea

zh: 接下来，我转向可以从霍佩韦希内派生的第二类母题，即卡凯（kake，“攀爬”）母题，它们汇入凯阿，有时也以凯阿之名为人所知。卡凯母题是拉伸并扭转了的霍佩韦希内（
），是达西·汤普森式的“坐标变换”的实例，而不是我们迄今考虑的那类沃什伯恩式的对称变换——尽管我刚才讨论的霍佩韦希内→瓦伊奥凯纳的例子中也涉及一些“拉伸”。不过在卡凯母题中，坐标被扭曲得多。
所示的卡凯（取自威洛迪恩·汉迪，图版xxvi）由复制的霍佩韦希内构成，其中一个经平移与第一个相连。然而，两个霍佩韦希内的对称被相对比例的改变掩盖了：左上与右下孤立的四分之一卵形被缩小，而相连的两个四分之一卵形被放大（
en: Next, I shall turn to the second category of motifs which can be derived from hope vehine, the kake ('climbing') motifs, which merge into kea, and are sometimes known by that name. The kake motif is a stretched and twisted hope vehine (

), an instance of ‘coordinate transformation' in the manner of D'Arcy Thompson, rather than symmetry transformations a la Washburn of the type we have been considering hitherto-though some ‘stretching' was involved in the hope vehine → vai o Kena example I discussed a moment ago. In the case of kake motifs, the coordinates are much more distorted though. The kake shown in

(from Willowdean Handy, plate xxvi) consists of duplicated hope vehine, one of which is translated and joined to the first. However, the symmetry of the two hope vehine is disguised by changes in relative proportions; the top left and bottom right isolated quarter-ovals are reduced, while the two quarter-ovals which join up are expanded (

zh: 然后，如此形成的整个图形被拉伸、弯曲，使较小的四分之一卵形成为施泰因术语中“足形纹”（podoid）或“有足生物”的头与尾。施泰因还有另一种卡凯形式，直接由坐姿埃图阿而非霍佩韦希内派生（
）。要产生施泰因ii型卡凯，把埃图阿表中像O那样的坐姿埃图阿复制，副本旋转180度后与原形相连，产生另一种“足形纹”。然后像i型卡凯（
）那样拉伸、扭转，产生特征性的弯曲卡凯母题。i型与ii型卡凯母题之间存在微妙的对称差异，即使它们看起来都是双头霍佩韦希内母题，差别取决于副本是否经过旋转（ii型如此，i型则否）（Steinen, iii. 162, illus. 110，对比 Handy, pl. xxvi）。卡凯可以、而且通常成对绘制，一个相对另一个旋转180度，以填满一个矩形空间。
en: Then the entire figure so formed is stretched and bent so that the smaller quarterovals become the head and tail of a ‘podoid' or ‘footed creature' in Steinen's terminology. Steinen also has a different form of kake, which is derived directly from a sitting etua, rather than from hope vehine (

). To produce a Steinen type ii kake, a sitting etua like O in the table of etua is duplicated, and the duplicate is joined to the original after 180 degrees rotation, producing a different kind of ‘podoid'. This is then stretched and twisted, as with the type i kake,

, to produce the characteristically bent kake motif. There is a subtle difference in symmetry between type i and type ii kake motifs, even when they appear to be double-headed hope vehine motifs, depending on whether the duplicate has been rotated (as in type ii) or not, type i (Steinen, iii. 162, illus. 110, vs. Handy, pl. xxvi). Kake can be, and commonly are, drawn in pairs, one rotated 180 degrees relative to the other, so as to fill a rectangular space.

zh: 最后，在结束卡凯的讨论前，我可以提一下汉迪记录的一个独特图案（

；Handy, pl. xv），那是一位女酋长臀部上方、骶骨区域纹的“腰带”。施泰因没有记录到类似的东西，但那也许是因为作为男性民族志者，他不便请这位女酋长展示她的纹身。左右两侧的大母题是（单头）卡凯（汉迪本人写作“ka'ake”，我认为这是错的）。这种大的“腰拱”是许多波利尼西亚纹身传统的特征（例如社会群岛；参见 Gell 1993）。不过，风格上有趣的是，这里有一个层级化的实例，而我迄今还没有机会提到层级化。到目前为止我讨论的所有图案都相当小，但这里我们看到两对（镜像的）卡凯（共四个）作为主要构图要素，统摄着许多从属的“简化”埃图阿图形（确切说是波胡与法努阿）。此外，整个组合还可以读作一个超大尺度的“面部”母题，不过我要等处理完埃图阿→“面部／眼睛”母题的转变之后，再回到这种可能性。母题包含于其他母题之内的更多实例还会出现，但这是一个醒目的例子。
en: Finally, before leaving kake, I may mention a unique design recorded by Handy (

; Handy, pl. xv) which is the ‘girdle' tattooed above the buttocks and over the sacral area of a female chief. Steinen recorded nothing like it but that may be because as a male ethnographer, he was not in a position to persuade this particular female chief to reveal her tattoo. The large motifs to the left and right are (single-headed) kake (Handy herself writes ‘ka'ake', which I think is mistaken). Such large ‘loin arches' were a feature of many Polynesian tattooing traditions (e.g. the Society Islands; see Gell 1993). What is stylistically interesting though is that here we have an instance of hierarchization, which I have hitherto not had any occasion to mention. All the designs I have discussed so far are quite small, but here we see a double pair of (mirror-image) kake (four in all) as major compositional elements, subsuming many subsidiary ‘reduced' etua figures (Pohu and fanaua to be precise). Furthermore, the whole assemblage may be read as a ‘face' motif on a very large scale, though I shall return to this possibility later, when I have dealt with the etua → 'face/eye' motif transition. Further instances of the inclusion of motifs within other motifs will crop up again, but this is a striking example.

en: It will have been noted that the heads of the ‘podoids' in

, resemble neither our type i or type ii kake very closely. They resemble, in fact are identical to, the small etua immediately adjacent to them, which are instances of the etua motif Pohu (a mythological hero) here depicted with particularly large hands (or forefeet) which these kake also have. They are similar in this respect to another category of elongated, but not twisted ‘podoids' categorized, once again, as kea (testudinates). These are podoids which are produced by setting etua motifs end to end in opposed pairs (i.e. one rotated 90 degrees; see

). Such kea are especially common in hand tattoos from which these examples are drawn (Steinen, i. 166, illus. 119). A large selection are found as decoration applied to a soup-bowl (terrine) which is itself the shape of a tortoise, where they are arrayed like the plates on a tortoise's shell-a tortoise of tortoises:
. In these kea, the eight legs may be turned into squared-off meanders, rather than the spirals seen in the original etua motifs (i.e. N on row 5 of the table of etua,
In so far as these ‘tortoise' motifs created from etua set end to end have ‘shells', these are represented by the second and third sets of ‘legs' of the resulting eight-legged creature.
