zh: 兰斯多夫1804年发表过一幅版画，画的是一个青年，肘部纹着一只相对“写实”的龟；在这个版本的龟母题中，甲壳画成一个椭圆，龟本身画成包含在这个椭圆内的一个埃图阿（
）。如果把它与施泰因在19世纪90年代记录的凯阿（龟）形式相比，甲壳已经消失，我们看到的只有一排埃图阿母题。但也许并非完全消失，因为凯阿腿的画法（大的四分之一卵形）提示，原龟母题的“甲壳”被分成四份，重新分配为埃图阿的“腿”——事实上，相邻的埃图阿共享半个甲壳。
en: In 1804 Langsdorff published an engraving of a youth with a relatively 'realistic' tortoise tattooed on his elbow; in this version of the tortoise motif, the carapace is drawn as an oval, and the tortoise itself as an etua contained within this oval (

). If we compare this with the form kea (tortoise) as recorded by Steinen in the 1890s the carapace has disappeared, and we have only a row of etua motifs. But perhaps not entirely, because the way in which the legs of kea are drawn (large quarter-ovals) suggests that the ‘carapace' of the original tortoise motif has been divided into quarters and redistributed as ‘legs' for the etua-in fact, adjacent etua share a half-shell between them.

zh: 8.10　从埃图阿到面部母题（马塔霍阿塔）
en: 8.10　From the Etua to the Face Motif (Mata Hoata)

zh: 接下来要讨论的埃图阿母题变换，或许最能说明马克萨斯风格何以浑然一体。这就是坐姿埃图阿向“眼睛”或“面部”母题马塔霍阿塔（mata hoata）的变换。面部母题由埃图阿母题升到更高层级，成为独立整体。两者的形态大致相同。这一派生在“巴多拉夫人”腿部纹身的马塔霍阿塔（“闪光的眼睛”）版本中看得最清楚（
）。巴多拉的马塔霍阿塔有一个特别清晰的埃图阿（与波胡相同，即
中的“r”），构成“鼻子”，鼻子上方两个巨大的半卵形就是醒目的双眼。如此并置之后，马塔霍阿塔图案与埃图阿（波胡）图案的同一性变得特别明显：前者是后者的放大版。埃图阿母题伸展的双臂变换为眼睛下方的深曲线，埃图阿的“手”成为虹膜，埃图阿的头成为鼻梁。更常见的是，马塔霍阿塔的“鼻子”是波胡的一个不那么易读的变换版本。

en: The next transformation of the etua motif to be considered is perhaps the most fundamental one of all to the integrity of the Marquesan style. This is the transformation of the sitting etua into the ‘eye' or ‘face' motif, mata hoata. The face motif is produced by hierarchization or hypostasization of the etua motif, with which it is morphologically speaking more or less identical. The derivation is most perspicuously seen in a version of mata hoata ('shining eyes') featuring on the leg tattoo of ‘Frau Badora’ (
). Badora's mata hoata features a particularly explicit etua (identical to pohu = ‘r' on

) forming the ‘nose' element above which are to be seen the large half-ovals forming the prominent eyes of this face design. Placed thus in conjunction, it becomes particularly apparent that the mata hoata design is identical to the etua (pohu) design, of which it is a scaled-up version. The outstretched arms of the etua motif become transformed into the deep curve under the eyes, the ‘hands' of the etua become the irises, and the head of the etua becomes the bridge of the nose. More usually, the ‘nose' of mata hoata is a transformed version of pohu which is not so legible.

shows some more standard forms of mata hoata from male tattoos recorded by Steinen. To produce this type of nose, the ‘arms' of small etua are reflected horizontally so that they form opposed half-ovals, and the head is eliminated. Thus a shape more reminiscent of nostrils is produced. However, mata hoata as a whole remains a legible derivative of the basic etua motif. Further reflected half-ovals may be added to the curved eye margins to add extra potency to the design. zh: 在埃图阿“臂”的末端与头的两侧添加螺旋，就产生另一个母题，比例上与马塔霍阿塔相似，名为瓦乌（vau，岩石）。这个母题令人想起拍岸浪涛冲击沿海礁石的情景，尤其常纹在臀部上方。因此，瓦乌是埃图阿／马塔霍阿塔的又一个派生母题；不过，为使母题更逼真，人们常以各种方式破坏这些螺旋的对称，产生
所示的一系列替代形式。
en: Adding spirals to the ends of the etua's ‘arms' and on each side of the head produces a further motif, similar in its proportions to mata hoata, called vau (rocks). This motif recalls the ocean swells breaking over coastal rocks and was particularly placed over the buttocks. en: 8.11　From Mata Hoata to Ipu: Additional Face Motifs

zh: 把马塔霍阿塔眼部的半卵形成对复制，就产生下一个重要母题伊普（ipu）。伊普的意思是“碗”或葫芦，通常沿手臂下侧成排布置，两两成对。马塔霍阿塔→伊普的变换如
所示。这个伊普母题水平一分为二，立刻变换为马塔霍阿塔。通常，伊普被一个名为帕普阿（papua）的母题环绕，那是马塔霍阿塔中“鼻子”形状重复排列后派生的母题（参见

所示那件独一无二的塔帕面具）。

zh: 接下来，我转向马塔霍阿塔之外、以圆眼为特征的那一族“面部”图案。这类图案常见的布置部位是手，各式图形组成的“脸”能护住手背。
显示了这样一张“手背脸谱”。可以看到，这里的眼睛由两个相对的半埃图阿图形构成，置于一个“鼻子”要素之上，其形式与马塔霍阿塔中所见的相同。手背脸谱的“嘴”由马塔霍阿塔深“眼”曲线的变换版本构成。

的插图中可见另一种“D”形而非圆形的眼睛形式。这里，眼睛由单个埃图阿构成，不过右边那只眼睛内部还包藏了一个小埃图阿图形，两者都趋近于成为马塔霍阿塔的微型版本。换言之，这个单一母题可以同时以三种截然不同的方式解读：(i) 作为手背脸谱的一只眼睛；(ii) 作为一张独立的面部，即马塔霍阿塔；(iii) 作为一个埃图阿，乃至两个埃图阿，一个包含另一个。一个母题能有这么多种读法，四周又有数十个同样让人费神的母题，足以显示马克萨斯风格怎样在图形上巧设机锋。这种图形创造力的展示意义何在？这个问题必须搁置，等更细致地探索了马克萨斯艺术风格特征的整个范围之后再说。
en: Next, I turn to the family of ‘face' designs other than mata hoata which feature circular eyes. A common site for the placement of this category of designs was on the hands, the backs of which were protected by ‘faces' composed of a variety of elements.

shows such a ‘hand face'. It will be seen that here the eyes are composed of two opposed half-etua figures, placed over a ‘nose' element identical in form to that seen in mata hoata. The ‘mouth' of the hand-face is composed of a transformed version of the deep ‘eye' curves of mata hoata. An alternative ‘D'-shaped rather than circular eye form is seen in the illustration in

. Here, the eye is formed by a single etua, though the right-hand one of these has a small additional etua-figure encapsulated within it, and both verge towards becoming miniature versions of mata hoata. In other words, this single motif can be read simultaneously in three quite distinct ways: (i) as a single eye of the hand-face; (ii) as a face by itself mata hoata; and (iii) as an etua, or indeed, as two etua, one containing the other. This overflow of possible readings attaching to a single motif-surrounded by dozens of others, equally perplexing-perfectly instantiates the cerebral wit of the Marquesan style. What was the point of such displays of graphic inventiveness? That question must be set aside until the entire range of stylistic characteristics of Marquesan art has been explored in more detail.

en: 8.12　Some Additional Motif-Transformation

zh: 剩下的几个常见母题可以简短处理。一个非常常见的“填充”母题是帕普阿（见

），它以各种构型呈现小半卵形，和／或来自马塔霍阿塔的“鼻子”要素——如我们所见，那是一个小型的变换埃图阿母题。有一个母题我找不到令人满意的派生关系，即帕希托（pahito），也称波卡卡（pokaka，意为“包裹”或“捆束”，图形与之相似）。这个母题由以各种方式布置的相对半卵形构成。实际上，帕希托只是划定一个空间，其中通常填满霍佩韦希内或马塔霍阿塔的派生物。另一个常见母题是团花（feo'o），由原本用来排成一行、在这里改排成一圈的母题（如波胡或法努阿的形式）构成（
en: The few remaining common motifs can be dealt with briefly. A very common ‘filler' motif is Papua (see

), which features small half-ovals in a variety of configurations, and/or the ‘nose' element from mata hoata, which, as we saw, was a small transformed etua motif. A motif for which I can find no satisfactory derivation is pahito which is also called pokaka (a package or bundle, which it does indeed recall). This motif is formed from opposed half-ovals in various dispositions. In practice pahito just delimits a space, which is usually filled with derivatives of hope vehine or mata hoata. Another common motif is the rosette (feo'o) which is made up of row motifs (such as forms of pohu or fanaua) arranged in a circle (

zh: 最后，我只提一下施泰因在“编辫”或编织母题名下讨论的一些较小母题。其中一些由三角形的各种排列构成，被认作“牙齿”或鲣鱼刺（牙齿可以简单地变换为刺）。牙齿母题（niho，尼霍）的一个常见用途，是在男性纹身中为大片的纯黑三角形纹身块“披甲”，那些黑块位于大腿内侧（
）。这些以三角形装饰的三角形，很清楚地展示了层级化。其他行母题是小埃图阿图形波胡与法努阿，前面已作为更大母题的组件提到过。不过它们的主要用途是作填充，排成单行或多行（它们显示在埃图阿母题表的第3行，
）。这类小埃图阿母题的一个有趣变体，是把它们连接起来，或者同向排列，或者让相邻两个互成90度（
显示了阿尼亚蒂乌母题中这种交替带纹，取自埃图阿表的“t”）。最后，埃图阿母题最极端的简化是棋盘格纹。这种纹样如何从“站立”埃图阿母题派生，在施泰因的埃图阿母题表中表现得非常清楚（第2行，a–l，显示各变体；棋盘格纹的象征与政治意义在 Gell 1993 中讨论）。
en: Finally, I shall only mention some of the smaller motifs which Steinen discussed under the rubric of ‘plaited' or woven motifs. Some of these consist of various arrangements of triangles, identified as ‘teeth' or bonito spines (teeth can be simply transformed into spines). A common use of teeth motifs (niho) is to ‘armour' the triangular patches of solid black tattoo on the inner thighs, in male tattoo (

). These triangles ornamented with triangles provide a particularly transparent instance of hierarchization. Other row-motifs are the small etua figures, pohu and fanaua, that have already been mentioned as components of larger motifs. Their main use, however, is as fillers, arranged in single or multiple rows (they are shown on row 3 of the table of etua motifs (
)). An interesting variation in such small etua motifs is achieved by joining them up, either in the same orientation, or in alternation rotated by 90 degrees. (

shows this alternating band pattern in the motif aniatiu, from the table of etua 't'.) Finally, the most extreme simplification of the etua motif is the chequerboard pattern. Just how this pattern can be derived from the ‘standing' etua motif is made very apparent in Steinen's table of etua motifs (row 2, a-l, showing variants: the symbolic and political significance of the chequerboard pattern is discussed in Gell 1993).

zh: 8.13　图底反转（玳瑁头饰）
en: 8.13　Figure-Ground Reversal (Tortoiseshell Diadems)

zh: 关于纹身母题，我想说的就是这些。接下来要讨论的艺术类别是马克萨斯的玳瑁工艺，它在二维的纹身艺术与浮雕及圆雕之间架起桥梁。最精细的玳瑁制品是一类完全平面的“头饰”：一片精雕的玳瑁圆片衬在一片稍大的珍珠贝圆盘上，形成极为优雅的前额饰物。如

所示，这种玳瑁透雕和纹身的风格十分接近。我所示的这片圆盘（Salem 1807）乍看令人想起马塔霍阿塔。但所见的那些面部究竟是如何安排的，它们各自的组件又是什么？围绕中央孔口，有四只大“眼睛”——通常说来，足够两张脸用了。然而，鉴于图案的圆形布局，这四只眼睛不属于两张脸，而属于四张脸，每张脸都与左右相邻的脸共享眼睛。从圆盘中心读起，那些大眼睛由看似拟人化的要素构成——一个举臂的人形，或半个埃图阿。
en: This is as much as I wish to say about tattoo motifs. The next category of art to be discussed is Marquesan work in tortoiseshell, which forms a bridge between the two-dimensional art of tattoo, and carving, in relief and in the round. The most delicate shell work is entirely two-dimensional, and consists of ‘diadems' in which a finely incised disc of tortoiseshell is shown off against a slightly larger disc of pearl-shell, forming a most elegant ornament for the forehead. As

shows, there is a great deal of continuity between the style of this pierced shell work and tattooing. The disc I illustrate (Salem 1807) reminds one, at first glance, of mata hoata. But exactly how are the faces one sees arranged, and what are their separate components? Around the central aperture, there are four large 'eyes'--enough eyes for two faces, normally speaking. Given the circular layout of the design, however, these four eyes belong, not to two, but to four faces, each of which shares its eyes with its neighbour on either side. The large eyes, read from the centre of the disc, are composed of elements which look anthropomorphic--a figure with raised arms, or half an etua.

zh: 每对眼睛之间，有一个复杂的形式，构成面部的其余部分。从圆盘边缘向内读每张脸，可以辨认出鼻孔和嘴。如果从圆盘中心向外读这些嘴／鼻孔部分，就会浮现出一组完全不同的面部。从圆盘边缘看时大脸的“鼻孔”，变成了从圆盘中心看时较小的、骷髅般的脸的眼睛（

）。还不止此，因为这些置于大眼睛之间的小骷髅脸（以黑底白纹呈现），本身又是由站姿埃图阿图形（以白底黑纹呈现）构成的。这是图底反转的一个令人叫绝的实例，比所有心理学教科书都引用的那个老套的脸／烛台例子有趣得多。正如我稍后将展示的，这种精湛技艺远非看似随意之举，而是与马克萨斯文化体系的某些根本属性直接相关——但与此同时，如前所述，这些属性只有只有仔细分析过物质文化的风格与形态，才能看出这些属性在作品中怎样成为主题。
en: Between each pair of eyes, there is a complex form which constitutes the rest of the face. Reading each face from the rim of the disc inwards, one can make out nostrils and a mouth. If one reads these mouth/nostril parts from the centre of the disc outwards, a quite different set of faces emerge. What were the ‘nostrils' of the big faces seen from the rim of the disc, become the eyes of smaller, skull-like faces which are seen from the centre of the disc (

). Nor is this all, for these smaller skull-faces set between the large eyes (which one sees in white-on-black) are themselves created from standing etua figures (which one sees in black-on-white). This is a stunning example of figure-ground reversal, much more interesting than the hackneyed face/candlestick one cited in all the psychology textbooks. As I will show later, such virtuosity is far from the arbitrary exercise it might seem, and relates directly to certain fundamental attributes of the Marquesan cultural system-but at the same time, as I noted earlier these attributes only become thematic after one has taken the trouble to dissect the style and morphology of the material culture, not before.

zh: 这类头饰由三件组成：中央圆盘加两片端板，端板如
所示（有些头饰有三片圆盘和两片端板）。端板值得仔细研究，因为在这里可以看到一种过渡：“两只大眼睛”型（黑底白纹）转变为某种显然完全不同的东西——蜥蜴／埃图阿的形象（白底黑纹）。这种图底反转与上一段讨论的那种之间有明显的关联。“眼睛”与“蜥蜴”之间显而易见的过渡，为施泰因的演化解读提供了材料，人们很容易看出原因（
）。但同时必须记住，这些端板的设计不是为了放在一起比较观看，而是分开单独观看的，所以我们能看到的过渡，对马克萨斯人未必以同样的方式显现。只有那些在单件端板内同时呈现的可作多种解读的图像，才具有无可置疑的风格显著性。不过，这样的图像还有很多（例如“o”“h”，其中眼睛与埃图阿／蜥蜴明显共存）。
en: Diadems of this kind were made in three pieces, the central disc plus two end-plates of the kind shown in

(some diadems had three discs and two end-plates). The end-plates make an interesting study, in that one can see here a transition between a ‘two large eyes' type (white on black) transforming itself into something apparently quite different—the image of a lizard/etua (in black-on-white). There is an obvious relationship between this figure-ground reversal and the one discussed in the preceding paragraph. The evident transition between ‘eyes' and ‘lizards' was grist to Steinen's evolutionary mill, and one can readily see why (

). At the same time, one must recall that these end-plates were not designed to be seen grouped together for comparison, but separately and individually, so that the transitions that we can see would not necessarily have been apparent in the same way to Marquesans. Only those visual ambiguities which are co-present within a single end-piece are of unquestionable stylistic saliency. There are many such ambiguities, however (for example, 'o', ‘h', where eyes and etua/lizards clearly coexist).

zh: 就马克萨斯艺术整体而言，这些端板也许最重要的方面，是它们对正面埃图阿图形经由“蜥蜴”向“侧面”埃图阿变换的启示。在纹身中找不到“侧面”埃图阿；它们只出现在小型造型艺术品中，比如这些端板，尤其是雕刻的象牙耳栓，我稍后将描述。侧面埃图阿形式的起源在端板“p”中很容易看到，其中底部的生物既可以是一个蜥蜴型埃图阿（如“r”中的那个），也可以是两个屈膝、以侧面呈现的埃图阿。关于背对背的神祇，我稍后还有更多要说，因为它们是马克萨斯各类圆雕作品中的主导母题。不过在端板中，它们通常经受一种变换：背对背的侧面埃图阿之一被反射，于是两者现在朝向同一方向（
，“i”；母题的两个版本在“m”中同时出现）。
en: Perhaps the most significant aspect of these end-plates, in terms of Marquesan art as a whole, is the light they shed on the transformation of the frontal etua figure into the ‘profile' etua, via the ‘lizard'. In tattooing, ‘profile' etua are not to be found; they only occur in ‘miniature' forms of plastic art, such as these end-plates, and particularly in carved ivory earplugs, which I will describe later. The genesis of the profile-etua form is easily seen in end-plate ‘p', in which the creature at the base could equally be a lizard-type etua like the one in ‘r' or two etua with bent knees seen in profile. I shall have more to say about back-to-back divinities later, since they are the dominant motif in all forms of Marquesan plastic art in the round. In the end-plates, though, they are commonly subjected to a transformation whereby one of the back-to-back profile etua is reflected, so that both now face the same way (
, ‘i'; both versions of the motif occur simultaneously in ‘m').

zh: 8.14　从二维到三维
en: 8.14　From Two to Three Dimensions

zh: 现在是时候转向不止二维的马克萨斯造型艺术了。我想可以公允地说，没有任何马克萨斯艺术是在充分占据三维空间这个意义上完全三维的。马克萨斯雕塑被构想为围绕一个内核（圆柱体或立方体——纹身的情形则是人体）的一层“皮”。内核可以是三维的，但雕刻图案常常似乎是在平面上构想的，是浅浮雕，是“包裹”在这个内核周围的贴饰。这甚至适用于大型独立圆雕人像，尤其是头部。这引出了一个有趣的问题：三维造型艺术与我们迄今一直在考虑的二维图形艺术究竟如何关联。马克萨斯人以与我们习惯的思维完全相反的方式，构想二维艺术与三维艺术之间的过渡，我现在就试图解释。
en: Now it is time to turn to Marquesan plastic art in more than two dimensions. I think it would be fair to say that no Marquesan art is fully three-dimensional in the sense of fully occupying three-dimensional space. Marquesan sculpture is conceived as a ‘skin' around a core (a cylinder or cube-or a human body in the case of tattooing). The core may be three-dimensional but the carved design often seems to be conceived in the flat, in low relief, as applique decoration which is ‘wrapped' around this core. This even applies to large free-standing figure sculpture, especially the heads. This raises an interesting point about exactly how plastic art in three dimensions is related to graphic art in two dimensions, of the kind we have been considering up to now. The Marquesans conceptualized the transition between two-dimensional and three-dimensional art in a way quite contrary to our own habitual way of thinking, as I shall now attempt to explain.

zh: 假设我给你看一张纸上用墨水画的人像，并提出问题：“这个图像的从背面看是什么样？”某种意义上，这个问题本身就不成立，因为图画是二维的图形（上下与左右），所以它们没有“背面”或“正面”。然而，我们自然地把这个问题理解为等价于：“你在画中看到的那个人的背面是什么样子？”——或者，如果我们选择照字面理解——“画着这个人的那张纸的背面是什么样子？”既然按字面理解这个问题显得愚蠢，我们自然会假定它问的是人从背面看是什么样子，并可能这样回答：画一幅像这样的画，同一个人、同一个姿势，从背后看。我们这样做，是因为我们把图画“看作”图画所表现的三维对象的“平面”投影，尤其当画的是人这类熟悉对象时。这种视觉预设是艺术表现中数百年自然主义熏陶的结果；任何图画都是“关于”某物的图画，那物独立于图画而存在（图画的“主题”），而图画的主题通常是一个三维对象，有正面有背面，也有左有右、有顶有底。
en: Suppose I present you with the image of a person, drawn in ink, on a sheet of paper, and I pose the question: ‘what is the back view of this image?' In a sense, this is a non-question, because drawings are graphs in two dimensions (up-down and left-right) so they do not possess ‘backs' or ‘fronts'. We, however, naturally interpret this question as equivalent to: ‘What does the back of the person you see in the drawing look like?'-or perhaps, if we choose to be literal-minded-‘What does the back of the piece of paper on which this person is drawn look like?' Since the question seems a silly one in its literal interpretation, it would be natural for us to assume that the question is one about what people look like when seen from the back, and we might answer it by producing a drawing like this which is the same person in the same pose seen from the rear. We do this because we ‘see' drawings as ‘flat' projections of the three-dimensional objects that drawings represent, especially when these are drawings of familiar objects, such as human beings. This visual presupposition is the outcome of centuries of conditioning to naturalism in artistic representation; any drawing is a ‘drawing of' something which exists separately from them (the ‘subject' of the drawing) and the subject of a drawing is typically a three-dimensional object with a front and a back as well as a left and a right and a top and a bottom.

en: FIG. 8.14/1. From three dimensions to two in Western art: the back view of the image as the back view of the prototype

zh: 这些预设对马克萨斯艺术不成立，它根本不是我们意义上的“再现性”艺术，但也并非“抽象”艺术。马克萨斯艺术是一种仪式艺术，目的是使人获得力量，免受伤害。我将在本章结论中回到这个话题。眼下只需说：例如在身上纹一个埃图阿母题，并不是表现一个存在于别处（作为三维固体对象）的埃图阿。纹身的埃图阿保护其人，因为它就是一个埃图阿，就在身上，而不是因为它“像”别处的某个埃图阿。刻画本身就是仪式。画出一个合乎规矩的图形（即与既有风格相称的图形），便让一位护佑之灵得以存在。这种刻画有直接创生的作用，所以不能用我们通常所说的“再现”来理解。这就是马克萨斯偶像崇拜（以及一切偶像崇拜）的本质，它贯穿于他们看待图形艺术与造型艺术的方式。
en: These presuppositions do not hold for Marquesan art, which was not 'representational' in our sense at all, without being ‘abstract' either. Marquesan art was a ritual art whose purpose was to render the person powerful and invulnerable. I will return to this subject in the conclusion of this chapter. For the present, it is sufficient to say that the tattooing of, for example, an etua motif on the body was not a matter of representing an etua which existed (as a three-dimensional solid object) somewhere else. The tattooed etua was protective of the person because it was an etua, right there on the body, not because it ‘looked like' an etua somewhere else. The graphic act was a ritual performance which brought into being a protective spirit through the utterance of a ‘legitimate' (stylistically coherent) graphic gesture. One cannot speak of graphic gestures of this kind as representational in our sense; they are constitutive. This is the essence of Marquesan idolatry (and of all idolatries), which informed their entire approach to graphic and plastic art.

zh: 现在让我们重新考虑图画背面视图的问题，记住马克萨斯图形姿态不是表现某物，而是构成某物。一个埃图阿母题本身就是一束线条。如果我们不再把这些线条看作“表现”（别的）某物，而只把它们看作线条，那么最初问题的答案就清楚了：一幅人物图画的“背面视图”，就是从纸张背后看到的画，也就是原画的镜像。
en: Let us now reconsider the question about what the back view of a drawing looks like, bearing in mind that a Marquesan graphic gesture does not represent something, but constitutes something. An etua motif consists, in itself, of a bundle of lines. If we stop thinking of these lines as ‘representing' something (else) and just think of these lines as lines, then the answer to our initial question is plain; the ‘back view' of a drawing of a person, is that drawing seen from the point of view of the paper, that is, the mirror-reversed view of the same drawing.

zh: 这个命题可以应用于马克萨斯三维造型的形成：西方图形艺术是把“压扁的”三维对象表现在二维中，而马克萨斯三维艺术则是经由镜像原则把二维“平面”母题投射到三维中，也就是说，三维图像的背面是正面的镜像反射。马克萨斯母题由直接创生形象的刻画动作产生，没有“背面”。从任何角度看，都是合乎规范的图形，因为仪式要奏效，刻画动作就必须合乎风格规范，做得“正确”。人不能从上帝的背面看他，因为如果他没有注视我们，他就不是上帝。同样，马克萨斯艺术同样不允许人从会让母题失去力量的角度看它（正如在马克萨斯与大多数波利尼西亚社会，走近或经过酋长的背后都是亵渎）。
en: This proposition may be applied to the genesis of three-dimensional plastic art in the Marquesan style; whereas Western graphic art is the representation of ‘flattened' three-dimensional objects in two dimensions, Marquesan three-dimensional art is the projection of two-dimensional ‘flat' motifs in three dimensions via the mirror principle, that is to say, the back of a three-dimensional image is the mirror reflection of the front. Marquesan motifs, which are constitutive graphic acts rather than acts of representation, have no ‘backs'; all the available views are canonical, because the principle of ritual efficacy depends on the stylistic legitimacy and ‘correctness' of the gesture. One cannot see God from the back, because if he is not watching us, he is not God. In the same way, Marquesan art cannot permit motifs to be witnessed, so to speak, at a disadvantage (just as it was sacrilege, in the Marquesas as in most Polynesian societies, to approach, or pass by, the back of a chief).

zh: 8.15　没有背面与分割再现：玳瑁冠
en: 8.15　Backlessness and Split Representation: Shell Crowns

zh: 马克萨斯艺术中最能说明形象怎样做到没有背面的实例，是玳瑁“冠”：由一系列弯曲的长方形玳瑁片制成，板上刻着极为繁复精巧的埃图阿形象（

）。这些冠是“证明规则的例外”，因为它们是浅浮雕的二维雕刻，而不是三维雕刻。这些板大多（但见下文）只装饰一面，即朝外的一面。然而事实上，它们在概念上被当作三维作品来对待，以马克萨斯的方式，即背面映照正面。这可以从所示的板（ii. 176, illus. 166“A”）看出。这是一个典型例子，主母题是一个正面全身可见的埃图阿。但主人形两侧还有两个侧面可见的埃图阿图形。这类板的另一种标准布局见“D”：这里只有两个埃图阿，每一个都是另一个的镜像反射（看手臂的安排）。同时，没有任何一块板是单个埃图阿填满整个空间的。我主张，这应归因于一种需要：确保这些独立的埃图阿形象至少在概念上有一面能够映照其正面的背面。这些形象可以说被向外翻折，于是它们的背面如今到了前面。于是，如果我们想象

“A”是用柔性材料做的，就可以把外侧两个“侧面”埃图阿面孔绕到中央那个的背后，使它们在中间相遇，接合成一个与正面埃图阿互为镜像的背面埃图阿。换言之，这些“侧面”是可以重新拼合的半张脸。为独立埃图阿提供背面这一问题的一个更简单的解决办法，见替代布局“D”。这里有两个镜像反射的埃图阿，照同一原理，只需沿中线对折，就能构成一个背面埃图阿和一个正面埃图阿。所有玳瑁冠板都是这两种为二维浮雕雕刻提供（受保护的）“背面”的解决办法之一的变体。然而，马克萨斯人对给埃图阿形象提供对称背面的关注并未止步于此。有些板（ii. 182, illus. 174）事实上刻有与正面图案完全相同的背面，尽管在使用中，这些板的雕刻背面即使不是完全、也大多是不可见的。费力给视觉上不可达的表面添加装饰，似乎是乖张的浪费；但尽管如此，如果这些冠要如预期的那样提供来自一切方向的仪式保护，这就是必要的。
en: The most perspicuous instance of backlessness in Marquesan art is provided by the tortoiseshell ‘crowns' made of a series of curved, rectangular plates of shell carved with etua images of great richness and intricacy (

). These crowns are the ‘exception which proves the rule' in the sense that they are low-relief, two-dimensional carvings rather than three-dimensional carvings. The plates are, for the most part (but see below) only decorated on one side, the side facing out. Yet in fact, they are treated, conceptually as if they were works in three dimensions, Marquesan fashion, that is, with backs mirroring their fronts. This may be seen from the plate illustrated (ii. 176, illus. 166 ‘A'). This is a typical example in which the main motif is an etua, seen from the front, full length. But the main figure is flanked by two further etua figures seen in profile. The other standard layout for such plates is seen in ‘D’; here there are just two etua, each one of which is a mirror reflection of the other (see the arrangement of the arms). Meanwhile, there is not a single example of a plate consisting of just one etua filling the whole space. I argue that this is to be attributed to the need to ensure that these etua images, which are free-standing, should at least conceptually be provided with backs mirroring their fronts. These images are, as it were, folded outwards so that their backs are now in front. Thus, if we were to imagine that

, ‘A' were made of flexible material, we could turn the two outer ‘profile' etua faces around the back of the central one, so that they met in the middle, where they would join up to make a back etua mirroring the front one. In other words, these ‘profiles' are half-faces which can be put together again. A simpler solution to the same problem of providing a back for a free-standing etua is seen in the alternative layout ‘D'. Here there are two mirror-reflected etua which, on the same basis as before, could simply be folded down the middle to make a back etua and a front etua. All the tortoiseshell crown plates are variations on one or other of these solutions to providing two-dimensional relief carvings with (protected) ‘backs'. However, Marquesan concern with providing etua images with symmetrical backs did not end there. Some plates (ii. 182, illus. 174) have, in fact, carved backs identical to their frontal design, even though, in use, these carved backs to the plates would have been mostly, if not entirely, invisible. Laboriously adding decoration to visually inaccessible surfaces seems a perverse waste of effort; but it was necessary none the less if these crowns were to provide ritual protection from all directions, as intended.

zh: 可以看到，埃图阿的面孔与侧面从这些板上到处萌生；主埃图阿的身体／四肢常常变成从属的埃图阿，如此等等。施泰因对这方面的变体做了细致研究（ii. 174–82）。本可以做一个与前面纹身母题分析类似的分析，但我不打算提供。关于这些玳瑁板，我想提的最后一点，是博厄斯／列维-斯特劳斯式的“分割再现”问题，施泰因自然没有讨论（他没有引用任何非波利尼西亚的比较实例）。显而易见，两种类型的板——1/2 + 1 + 1/2布局与1 + 1布局——都是某种“分割再现”的实例，与美洲西北海岸部落艺术中那些著名例子相近（
），具体做法却相去甚远。马克萨斯的分割再现主要沿从左到右平分身体的平面（如D），而不是像列维-斯特劳斯讨论的美洲／古代中国实例那样从背到前（1963: 第xiii章）。偶尔也有从背到前的分裂（如

A，尽管分割再现的“两半”彼此背向而非相向），更罕见的是“两半”彼此相向的分割再现实例，如列维-斯特劳斯／博厄斯式的分割再现（例如见 ii. 179, illus. 169 a）。但分割再现的精确几何也许不如对它的解释重要。我认为，列维-斯特劳斯在毛利艺术中相当勉强地辨识出分割再现，本质上是因为毛利人的面部再现刻成浮雕时，倾向于把脸展开，使它开始像两个相对的侧面，而不是正面观看的一张脸。这一特征在马克萨斯的面部再现中同样明显，甚至更明显；但在我刚讨论的玳瑁板中，形象的重演也许是“分裂”原则的一个更清晰的实例，而分割再现真正要紧的正是这个原则。
en: As will be seen, etua faces and profiles sprout everywhere from these plates; often the bodies/limbs of the main etua become subsidiary etua, and so on. Steinen makes a detailed study of the variations in this regard (ii. 174-82). A similar analysis to the previous one of tattoo motifs might be undertaken, but I shall refrain from providing one. The last point I wish to raise with regard to these tortoiseshell plates is the Boasian/Levi-Straussian one of ‘split representation', which naturally Steinen does not discuss (he cites no non-Polynesian comparative examples). It will be apparent that both types of plates, the ½ + 1 + ½ layout and the 1 + 1 layout, are instances of ‘split representation' of a kind, cognate to, though by no means the same as, the famous examples from the art of the north-west coastal tribes of America (

). Marquesan split representation is primarily in the plane bisecting the body from left to right (as in D) rather than from back to front as in the American/ancient Chinese examples discussed by Levi-Strauss (1963: ch. xiii). Occasionally there is back to front splitting as well (as in

A, though the ‘halves' of the split representation face away, rather than towards, one another), and still more rarely, there are instances of split representation where the ‘halves' face one another as in the Levi-Strauss/Boas-type split representation (e.g. see ii. 179, illus. 169 a). But the precise geometry of split representation is perhaps less important than the interpretation one gives to it. Levi-Strauss identified split representation in a rather forced way, I think, in Maori art, essentially because Maori representations of the face, carved as reliefs, tend to open the face out so that it begins to resemble two opposed profiles rather than one single face viewed frontally. This characteristic is equally if not more evident in Marquesan representations of the face, but the doubling of images, in the tortoiseshell plates I have just discussed, is perhaps a more perspicuous example of the ‘splitting' principle which is really what is at issue in split representation.

zh: 然而，列维-斯特劳斯对分割再现的解释，在波利尼西亚语境中最发人深省。他主张，当社会因素阻碍二维形象与三维形象的分离时，分割再现就会出现。“归根结底，我们的问题可以表述如下：在什么情况下，［一个艺术体系的］造型部分与图形部分必然相关联？”他问道，并以如下断言回答自己的问题：当造型部分是面部或人体、图形部分是施加其上的面部或身体装饰（彩绘或纹身）时，造型与图形之间的关系“必然是功能性的”（1963: 261）。
en: Levi-Strauss's interpretation of split representation is most thought-provoking, however, in the Polynesian context. He maintains that split representation occurs when social factors militate against the dissociation of two-dimensional and three-dimensional images. ‘In the end, our problem may be formulated as follows: under what circumstances are the plastic and graphic components [of an art system] necessarily correlated?' he asks, and responds to his own question by asserting that the relationship between the plastic and the graphic ‘has to be functional when the plastic component consisted of the face or human body and the graphic component of the facial or corporeal decoration (painting or tattooing) which is applied to them' (1963: 261).

zh: 作为“装饰”（即魔法图形）画布的面部或身体，就其二维方面而言，不能与施加“装饰”的三维身体分离。因此，列维-斯特劳斯论证说，分割再现不仅与面具文化相联系，而且特别与那些面具与人不可分离地联系在一起的面具文化相联系——身体彩绘尤其是纹身的情形最为突出，纹身是完全无法去除的。回想莫斯（1902）关于“人格”概念起源于社会面具persona的讨论，可以说，当社会面具（persona）与人（person）合为一体时，再现就会采取分割的形式，因为三维的人与二维的社会面具无法分离。列维-斯特劳斯说，既高度等级化又高度竞争的社会，正是这些条件得到满足的社会。这类社会通常围绕把人连接到神的谱系资历展开竞争，美洲西北海岸部落如此，南美洲的等级社会如此，远东的古代社会（商代青铜器的制造者，E·贡布里希已指出其与波利尼西亚艺术的亲缘关系，1984: 262–70）如此，毛利人如此，马克萨斯人也同样如此。这种确立谱系地位的竞争斗争，就是分割再现背后的社会学理由。
en: A face or body in its two-dimensional aspect as the canvas for ‘decoration' (i.e. magical graphics) cannot be dissociated from the three-dimensional body to which ‘decoration' is applied. Hence, argues Levi-Strauss, split representation is associated, not just with masking cultures, but particularly with those masking cultures in which mask and person are indissociably linked—as is most particularly the case with body-painting and especially tattooing, which is quite irremovable. Recalling Mauss's discussion (1902) of the origin of the concept of the ‘person' in the social mask, persona, one might say that where persona and person unite, representations are split because the three-dimensional person and the two-dimensional persona cannot be dissociated. Levi-Strauss says that societies which are both very hierarchical and very competitive are ones in which these conditions are fulfilled. Such societies typically compete over genealogical credentials linking men with gods, as was the case among the tribes of the north-west coast of America, among the hierarchical societies of South America, the archaic societies of the Far East (producers of the Shang bronzes, whose affinities with Polynesian art have been noted by E. Gombrich 1984: 262-70), among the Maori, and, equally, the Marquesans. This competitive struggle to assert genealogical status is the sociological rationale behind split representation.

zh: 我不愿为列维-斯特劳斯这个宏大概括的普遍有效性辩护；显然，围绕谱系资历的竞争可以在不以面具、分割再现或任何这类特定方式表达的情况下进行。然而，列维-斯特劳斯关于“分割再现社会”的社会学特征所说的话，对马克萨斯来说是再真切不过的；他多半未曾见过马克萨斯的民族志资料，说法却像是预先洞悉了当地的情形，十分贴切，几乎令人不可思议。概括他的观点，他说：
en: I would not care to argue for the universal validity of Levi-Strauss's sweeping generalization; evidently, competition over genealogical credentials can be engaged in without this finding expression in the particular modality of masking, split representation, or anything of the kind. However, what Levi-Strauss says about the sociological characteristics of ‘split-representation societies' is quintessentially true of the Marquesas, and there is indeed something uncanny about the precision with which he rhetorically anticipates Marquesan ethnographic data of which it is most unlikely that he had foreknowledge. Summarizing his point of view, he remarks:

zh: 分割再现表达了行动者对其［社会］角色……以及对神话、仪式与谱系的严格遵从。这种遵从如此严格，以至于要把个体从其社会角色中分离出来，就必须把他撕成两半。（1963: 264）
en: split representation expresses the strict conformity of the actor to his [social] role and ... to myths, ritual, and pedigrees. This conformity is so rigorous that, in order for the individual to be dissociated from his social role, he must be torn asunder. (1963: 264)

zh: 我说这不可思议，是因为正如我在别处描述过的（1993: 213及以下），马克萨斯实际情况正是：死去的酋长被“撕成两半”，而且正是出于这个明确的目的——把他们经由纹身获得的社会身份从他们身上除去。酋长纹身的皮肤被剥去，因为在马克萨斯信仰中，由于纹身与凡人境况的关联，身上有纹身的人无法成神，也得不到美好的来世。死后，那经纹身强化的皮肤——酋长生前全靠这样的皮肤抵御身体和灵性所受的种种威胁——必须留下；社会之皮与不朽之魂分道扬镳，酋长重新加入皮肤不带纹饰的诸神之列。
en: I say this is uncanny, because, as I have described elsewhere (1993: 213 ff.), it was actually the case in the Marquesas, that dead chiefs were ‘torn asunder', and with this precise purpose in mind, that they should have removed from them the social identity conferred on them by their tattooing. The tattooed skin of chiefs was removed because, in Marquesan belief, deification and a pleasant afterlife were denied to the tattooed because of the association between tattooing and the mortal condition. After death, the skin reinforced by tattooing—so necessary to ward off the physical and spiritual dangers of a worldly and chiefly life-had to be left behind; social skin and immortal soul parted company and the chief rejoined the assembly of the clear-skinned gods.

zh: 我希望人们会注意到列维-斯特劳斯关于分割再现的论证，与前面提出的关于普遍倾向于给三维形象提供与正面互为镜像的“背面”这一论证相通。分割再现问题与双面形象问题——后者是波利尼西亚造型艺术特别突出的特征——在本质上是同一性质的。双面形象之于造型艺术，犹如分割再现之于图形艺术，即确保形象的任何部分都不偏离“标准的”（有仪式效力的）视图的手段。在博厄斯／列维-斯特劳斯的分割再现中，如果一只动物从正面看，那么整只动物都从正面看，包括那些从这样的视点看“真实”动物时事实上不可见的部分（体侧）。在马克萨斯（“波利尼西亚”）的分割再现中，策略略有不同：把正面的形象复制到背面。分割再现（一种图形方式）在二维空间中提供三维对象的标准视图，而双面形象的制作则允许本质上是二维图形扩展到三维的造型空间，同时不违背“只允许标准形象”的规定。于是：双面形象 : 分割再现 :: 图形艺术 : 造型艺术 :: 三维 : 二维
，等等。
en: I hope that the convergence between Levi-Strauss's argument on the subject of split representation and the one advanced earlier concerning the pervasive tendency towards providing three-dimensional images with ‘backs' reflecting, mirror fashion, their frontal aspect, will be appreciated. The problem of split representation and the problem of Janus-faced images-the latter being a particularly prominent characteristic of Polynesian plastic art-are of an essentially identical nature. Janus-faced images are to plastic art what split representation is to graphic art, that is, the means of securing that no part of an image departs from the ‘canonical' (ritually potent) view. In Boas/Levi-Strauss split representation, if an animal is seen from the front, then the whole of the animal is seen from the front, including those parts of it (the flanks) which are in fact invisible when a ‘real' animal is seen from such a vantage-point. In Marquesan ('Polynesian') split representation, the strategy is slightly different; the image of the front is reduplicated and becomes the image of the back as well. Where split representation (a graphic mode) provides a canonical view of a three-dimensional object in a two-dimensional space, the making of Janus-faced images allows for the expansion of essentially two-dimensional graphic images into three-dimensional plastic space without contravening the stipulation that ‘only canonic images are permissible'. Hence: Janus face: split representation :: graphic art : plastic art :: three dimensions : two dimensions, etc.

zh: 8.16　双面（雅努斯式）形象：尺度变换
en: 8.16　Janus-Faced Images: Scale Transformations

zh: 不过，前面谈分割再现时，我说得有些超前了。我还没有介绍马克萨斯三维造型艺术中大量出现的雅努斯式双面形象。因此，我要立即转向对这一类形象的描述。
en: However, in the course of the preceding digression into the problem of split representation, I have perhaps run a little ahead of myself, in that I have not yet introduced the full panoply of Janus-faced images with which Marquesan plastic art in three dimensions is strikingly replete. To the description of this type of image I will therefore turn without delay.

zh: 如果说马克萨斯人制作的每一个人形雕刻形象都采用施泰因所称的“doppeltiki”（双身提基）形式，那并不符合事实；但其中绝大多数确实如此。不属此类的包括：少数背面未加雕刻的石像、一些木质“柱像”，以及数目更大的一类小型木像与骨像——它们虽不是真正的雅努斯式小雕像，却雕有附属的（护佑性的）背面埃图阿，下文我将更详细地加以描述。
en: It would not be true to say that every single one of the anthropomorphic sculptural images produced by the Marquesans were in what Steinen describes as the ‘doppeltiki' (double tiki) form, but the great majority of them are. The ones that are not include a small number of stone images, with uncarved backs, some wooden ‘post figures', and a larger category of small wood and bone images which, though not true Janus-type figurines, are carved with subsidiary (protective) back-etua which I will describe in more detail below.

zh: 马克萨斯人也雕刻过可与著名的复活节岛石像相比的大型石像，尽管无论在数量、体量还是工艺的恢弘上，都从未达到复活节岛艺术的水准。我把它们缺乏前后对称这一点归因于这样一个事实：它们最初大概全都砌入酋长马拉埃（仪式平台）的石砌台基之中，而非独立竖立（
）。这些石像中最有趣的一尊是被称为Makii-taua-pepe的那尊（

），表现的是一位正在分娩的女神。马克萨斯艺术中还有其他分娩形象（以微型象牙雕耳饰的形式），但没有一件达到这样的尺度。等我处理这些耳饰时，再讨论马克萨斯人关于分娩的观念。眼下只需指出：尽管形式独特，这尊大石像在概念上同样是一尊“双身提基”，因为在分娩之际（一个极度危险而神圣的时刻），马克萨斯的母亲们在身体上呈现出那种“双重”形式——这种形式通常只与神祇相联系——而以这种方式生下的孩子本身也极为神圣（Gell 1993: 185）。在这件雕刻中，如
所示，“神子”由隆起腹部下侧的一个标准埃图阿母题来表现。
en: Large stone images comparable to the famous Easter Island statues were carved by the Marquesans, though they never attained the numbers, or the size, or the magnificent workmanship of Easter Island art. I would attribute their lack of back-to-front symmetry to the fact that they were probably all originally built into the stone terraces of chiefly marae (ceremonial platforms) rather than being free-standing (
). The most interesting of these stone images is the one known as Makii-taua-pepe (

), which represents a female divinity giving birth. There are other images of birth in Marquesan art (in the form of miniature carved ivory ear-ornaments) but none on this scale. I will discuss Marquesan ideas of parturition when I come to deal with these ear-ornaments. For the present, it is sufficient to note that despite its unique form, this large statue is conceptually a ‘double tiki' as well, in that during parturition (a moment of great danger and sacredness) Marquesan mothers physically assumed the ‘doubled' form, otherwise associated with divine beings, and children, produced in this way, were themselves very sacred (Gell 1993: 185). In this carving, the ‘divine child' is represented, as
shows, by a standard etua motif on the underside of the distended belly.

zh: 从风格学的观点看——这也是我们首要的关注所在——所有这些石像值得注意之处在于它们的块状形式，以及形体的各处细节，尤其是五官，处理成石块上的浅浮雕，没有塑出独立的立体形状。同样的考虑或多或少也适用于木质人形形象（
）。它们不是独立竖立的形象，而是房屋或其他结构的构件，如雕花柱、支撑梁；这一点与石像一样，解释了它们为何背面不加雕刻。
en: From the point of view of stylistics-which is our primary concern-the point to note about all these stone images is their block-like form, and the way in which the features, especially those of the face, are not modelled in three dimensions, but are incised on the block in low relief. More or less the same considerations apply to the wooden anthropomorphic images (
). These are not free-standing images but components of houses or other structures, such as carved posts, supporting beams, which, as with the stone images, explains their uncarved backs.

zh: 所有中等至大型马克萨斯雕刻中不成比例的大眼／大口以及鼻子的缺失，使我想到：这一尺度上的作品的风格惯例，是从尺度小得多的作品派生而来的。在一件微型骨雕上，这样的五官比例显得相当自然：那是清晰勾画眼与口的需要所致——若遵循“真实”眼口的自然比例，微型作品根本不可能做到这一点。另一方面，鼻子在这一尺度上是多余的，因为放大的眼与口之间的三角形空间已暗示出鼻三角，只需对鼻孔作极简处理即可；而突出鼻子的缺失，正与马克萨斯雕刻本质上二维的性质相吻合——它是以浅浮雕刻出，而非真正“雕造”出来的。在我看来，从风格学的观点看，一切较有意思的马克萨斯造型艺术都处于小型甚至微型的尺度。如我先前所提示的，马克萨斯艺术必须被理解为一种通过加上具有灵力的附属物来增强一个人的力量的技艺，而这些部件本质上全都采取埃图阿的形式。较大的作品依附在仪式平台或房屋之类的构筑物上。它们相当于放大了的“个人”附属物——如扇、护身符、头饰、耳饰、竞技用具（高跷）与武器（棍棒）——，也包括纹身。马克萨斯艺术的基本形式正是在这些增强人之力量的作品中生成的，因此我们必须把大部分注意力投向这一领域。
en: The disproportionately large eyes/mouths in all medium- to large-scale Marquesan sculpture, and the absence of noses, suggests to me that the stylistic conventions for work at this scale were derived from work at a much smaller scale. On a tiny bone carving, features of these proportions seem quite natural, the result of the need to delineate eyes and mouths visibly, which would be impossible in miniature work were the natural proportions of ‘real' eyes or mouths observed. Noses, on the other hand, are redundant at this scale, since the triangular space between the enlarged eyes and mouth implies the nasal triangle with no need for more than a summary treatment of the nostrils, and the absence of a protruding nose coincides with the essentially two-dimensional nature of Marquesan carving, which is incised in low relief rather than being truly ‘carved'. To my mind, all the more interesting Marquesan plastic art, from the stylistic point of view, is at the small or even miniature scale. Marquesan art, as I suggested earlier, has to be understood as a technique for enhancing the person by the addition of spiritually potent appendages or supernumeraries, all essentially in the form of etua. The larger art forms were appendages of structures, such as ritual platforms or houses; as such, they were enlarged equivalents of ‘personal' appendages, such as fans, amulets, head ornaments, ear-ornaments, sporting gear (stilts), and weapons (clubs)-and of course, tattooing. It was in the domain of these ‘person-enhancing' art forms that the basic forms of Marquesan art were generated, so it is to this area that we must devote most of our attention.

zh: 一旦进入这一领域，所见的就大多是“双身提基”了，因为如我上面所指出的，造型艺术形式（即三维形式）中巫术效力的要求，规定必须在一切空间维度上同时呈现规范性的（有效力的）形象。用作发饰的小型骨提基提供了一个合适的出发点。它们呈圆柱形（
）。它们有两种样式：或完全对称，或更常见地带有一个附属的背面形象；后者又或是一个小埃图阿母题，或是一个刻有卐字纹的方块。卐字纹母题是经由霍佩韦希内而来的埃图阿变体（
）（见上文）。
en: Once we enter this domain, the presence of the ‘double tiki' form becomes overwhelming, because, as I have noted above, the requirements of magical efficacy in plastic art forms (i.e. three-dimensional ones) demands the simultaneous presentation of the canonical (efficacious) image in all spatial dimensions. A suitable point of departure is provided by the small bone tiki which were used as hair ornaments. These are cylindrical in form (

). They came in two patterns, either fully symmetrical or, more commonly, with a subsidiary back-figure, which in turn was either a small etua motif, or a square engraved with a hakenkreuz. The hakenkreuz motif is a variant of the etua (
) via hope vehine (see above).

zh: 这些小型圆柱状骨饰大多有一个突出特点：与头部相比，身体尤其是腿部的处理极为简略。马克萨斯作品的头身比，似乎遵循着一条相当稳定的规则。如果我们把马克萨斯造型艺术中对身体的任何表现都视为一个经过修改的圆柱体，那么这条比例规则规定：随着“圆柱体”直径与高度之比趋近于1，头部在全身所占的比例就越大。其底层的约束似乎是把面部保持一定的长宽比例的需要：眉至下巴的距离必须大致等于两耳之间的宽度，换言之，脸必须或多或少能放进一个正方形。这条规则的适用与“圆柱体”的绝对尺寸无关。如
所示，相对修长的马克萨斯身体表现（1）中，头（A）、身（B）、腿（C）各部分尺寸之比符合自然界中的比例A<B<C。总高度的缩减则产生越来越不自然的头／身／腿比例：（2）A=B=C，（3）A>B=C，直至达到这些骨提基中所见的比例——处于“自然主义”对立极的（4）A>B>C。
en: Most of these small cylindrical bone ornaments are distinguished by the very summary treatment given to the body and especially the legs, by comparison to the head. There seems to be a relatively consistent rule of proportionality dictating the head/body ratio which is built into the Marquesan style. If we take it that any Marquesan plastic representation of the body is essentially a modified cylinder, the proportional rule decrees that as the ratio between the diameter and the height of the ‘cylinder' approaches unity, the ratio between the head and the body increases in favour of the head. The underlying constraint seems to be the need to keep the proportions of the head face within bounds; the distance between the brow and the chin must remain approximately equal to the ear-to-ear measurement, or in other words the face must fit, more or less, into a square. This rule applies independently of the absolute dimensions of the ‘cylinder'. As

shows, relatively elongated Marquesan representations (1) of the body show ratios between the dimensions of the head (A), the body (B), and the legs (C) which conform to the ratios found in nature A< B < C. Reduction in overall height produced progressively more unnatural head/body/legs ratios: (2) A = B = C, (3) A > B = C, until the ratios found in these bone tiki are attained, at the opposite pole from ‘naturalism' (4) A > B > C.

zh: 在造型艺术中，作为孤立实体的头极为罕见；每个头都必须有其身体；但身体可以像这里一样只用寥寥几笔刻出。我借助达西·汤普森式的变换坐标系统来表达这条比例规则——这是一种借自生物学形态研究的表述方式。正是这类可在数学上概括的性质之存在，赋予了马克萨斯风格以视觉上的连贯性。
en: In the plastic arts, the head as an isolated entity is very rarely found; every head must have its body; but it may be given very meagre representation, as here. I have expressed the proportionality rule by means of the D'Arcy Thompson-type system of transformed coordinates—an idiom borrowed from biological studies of morphology. It is the existence of such mathematically generalizable properties as these which lends visual coherence to the Marquesan style.

zh: 这些小型骨发饰还有第二个特点值得注意。由于尺寸小，它们总体上以极浅的浮雕雕成。因此，它们为马克萨斯艺术将二维埃图阿形象转化为三维独立对象的方法提供了极佳的例证。其程序很简单，无非是把一个“平的”埃图阿形式“包裹”在一个圆柱形骨架上。也就是说，西方艺术通过“增加一个维度”把二维平面形象（一幅画）转化为三维形象（一件雕塑作品），而马克萨斯的路径则是在三维“空间”中表现一个二维形象，同时让其二维性基本保持完好（就像贴在圆柱形电话杆上的海报所保持的二维性那样）。骨提基是一件把平面“弯曲”了的作品，而非三维形式。这种通过在基本平坦的母题上施加曲率来达成三维性的路径，是马克萨斯造型艺术的一个辨认这一风格的特征，在人形形象面部五官的刻画中尤其可见。
en: There is a second feature of these small bone hair ornaments to which we can draw attention. Because of their small dimensions, they are carved, on the whole, in very low relief. They therefore provide excellent instances of the method through which Marquesan art transforms two-dimensional etua images into three-dimensional free-standing objects. The procedure is simple, since it amounts to ‘wrapping' a ‘flat' etua-form around a cylindrical armature. That is to say, whereas Western art ‘adds a dimension' to convert a two-dimensional flat figure (a drawing) into a three-dimensional figure (a work of sculpture), the Marquesan approach is rather to represent a two-dimensional figure in a three-dimensional ‘space', while leaving its two-dimensionality essentially intact (like the two-dimensionality of a poster applied to a cylindrical telephone-pole). The bone tiki is a ‘curved' work in the flat, rather than a three-dimensional form. This approach to three-dimensionality via the imposition of curvature onto basically flat motifs is a diagnostic feature of Marquesan plastic art, visible particularly in the rendition of the facial features of anthropomorphic figures.

zh: 8.17　增殖、换位与长鼻形成：扇柄
en: 8.17　Multiplication, Transposition, and Proboscis-Formation: Fan Handles

zh: 这些小型骨雕是最“圆柱形”的人工制品。鲸牙扇柄——马克萨斯技艺在其中得到格外充分的展示——更长更扁，通常被划分为一系列节段，每段雕有以不同方式布置的双面（雅努斯式）形象（

），其中每一个都大致类似于我们刚才讨论过的小型圆柱状小雕像。不过，这些雅努斯形象中的每一个都被当作一个单元处理，因此它们被纳入相对修长的圆柱体之中，从而身体和下肢都完整刻出。扇柄的几个特点，也见于稍后要讨论的高跷踏板。首先，它们显示出纯粹增殖的倾向——这是马克萨斯艺术一个如此显著的特征。尽管它们是相对小的物件（约20厘米），每件上面至少表现四个形象，基部往往还多出一个甚至两个，此外还有种种附加的刻纹母题，而所有这一切都可以追溯到基本的埃图阿母题。这里所见的增殖源于扇柄的仪式重要性：扇柄是最有权势的酋长与女酋长所拥有的重要权标。酋长的权力取决于他拥有多少“支持者”：酋长们彼此进行你死我活的斗争，以扩充追随自己的人数。刻着许多形象的扇柄象征着“数量”在马克萨斯政治生活中的显著地位（见Gell 1993）。
en: These small bone carvings are the most ‘cylindrical' of artefacts. The whale-ivory fan handles, where Marquesan artistry is particularly well displayed, are longer and flatter, and are usually divided up into a series of segments, each carved with Janus figures in various dispositions (

) each of which broadly resembles one of the small cylindrical figurines we have just been considering. However, each of these Janus figures is treated as a unit, so they are inscribed in relatively elongated cylinders and hence have fully represented bodies and lower limbs. The fan handles present various points of interest, which they share with the stilt-steps I will consider in a moment. They show, first of all, the tendency towards sheer proliferation which is such a marked feature of Marquesan art. Although they are relatively small objects (about 20 cm.), each has a minimum of four figures represented on it, and often one or even two more on the base, besides sundry additional incised motifs, all of which can be traced back to the basic etua motif. The proliferation seen here is a function of the ritual importance of fan handles, which were important items of regalia owned by the most powerful chiefs and chiefesses. A chief's power was a function of how many ‘supporters' he had: chiefs engaged in deadly struggles with one another to increase their numerical followings. These multitudinous fan handles refer symbolically to the salience of ‘numbers' in Marquesan political life (see Gell 1993).

zh: 这些扇柄的第二个特征是形象倾向于切换朝向；即接受水平或垂直方向的旋转。这类切换可能意味着一对雅努斯形象中的两个都朝同一方向，从而其中之一暴露出背面，如
中的第二个形象；上面一对形象则朝相反方向，护住这一侧。或者，身体朝内而脸朝外，如
（3）。另一种切换影响形象在垂直轴上的朝向（见
），其中一些相对于其他形象可能是倒置的。最后，这些扇柄展示了头／面的种种“变形”。如果脸被表现为横跨柄的宽面（如
（4）），脸便展平为类似于马塔霍阿塔的形状。但如果需要把脸表现为从柄的顶端或底端突出、形成一种“柄头”，就会产生一种全新的形态，它在纹身中没有对应物（
）。施泰因把这些扇柄归入一个独立的类别，称其为“锚形”或“双锚形”柄。在这些“柄头”位置上生成的头部新形态，（从侧面看）类似鸟喙，或许可说是爬行动物尖出的鼻与颌。然而从正面看，这种相似性便消失了，人们只看到一个程式化的鼻与口，附着于一段扁平的长鼻，看不出像哪种动物。
en: A second feature of these fan handles is the tendency for figures to switch their orientation; that is, be subjected to rotation horizontally or vertically. This kind of switching can mean that both of a pair of Janus figures may face the same way and that consequently the back of one of them is exposed as in the second figure in
, but this is always offset by the upper pair of Janus figures which will face in opposite directions, protecting that side. Alternatively, bodies may face inwards but the faces outwards, as in
(3). Another kind of switching affects the orientation of figures in the vertical axis (see

), some of which may be upside-down relative to the others. Finally, these fan handles demonstrate a variety of ‘distortions' of the head face. If represented spanning the broad side of the handle (as in

(4)) the face flattens out to a shape similar to mata hoata. But if the need is to represent the face projecting out of the top or bottom of the handle, making a kind of ‘pommel', a completely new morphology is generated, which has no tattooing analogue (

). Steinen places these fan handles in a distinct class, describing them as ‘anchor' or ‘double-anchor' handles. The new morphology of the head which is generated in these ‘pommel' positions resembles (from the side) the beak of a bird or perhaps the pointed nose and jaw of a reptile. From the front, however, the resemblance disappears, and one sees only a formulaic nose and mouth attached to a kind of flattened proboscis which has no obvious counterpart in any family of creatures whatsoever.

zh: 把脸表现为这种长鼻，是马克萨斯之外其他岛屿波利尼西亚艺术的一个特征；人们立刻会想到从南方群岛输入塔希提的拂尘柄上的类似做法（

）。这一手法也见于马克萨斯艺术的其他地方，见于穿耳器与高跷踏板（见下文）。它是如何生成的？实际上，前面看到的那些典型的平脸形象，原本几乎看不出鼻梁。这里却仿佛捏住泥塑的鼻梁，猛地向前、向下拉长。嘴唇仍附着在长鼻的外表面、位于其尖端，但与正常人脸的一切相似性都丧失了。尽管如此，我不认为马克萨斯艺术家真的意图让这些长鼻脸的生灵被看作鸟或兽，尽管它们根本违背了正常的人“脸”图式。它们只不过是在几何上重新配置的脸，以所需的方式填充空间（例如满足给扇柄提供圆柄头的需要）。
en: Representing the face as a proboscis of this kind is a feature of Polynesian art from other islands besides the Marquesas; parallels with the fly-whisk handles imported into Tahiti from the Austral Islands immediately spring to mind (

). This device occurs elsewhere in Marquesan art, in ear borers and in stilt-steps (see below). How is it generated? In effect, the bridge of the nose (which is hardly even suggested in the typically flat-faced images of the kind we have been looking at up till now) is sharply seized and drawn forwards and downwards, as if it were made of plasticine. The lips remain attached to the outer surface of the proboscis, at the tip, but all resemblance to a normal human face is lost. None the less, I do not think the Marquesan artists actually intended that these proboscis-faced creatures should be seen as birds or animals, despite their radical contravention of the normal human ‘face' schema. They are simply geometrically reconfigured faces which fill space in the required way (e.g. accommodate the need to provide fan handles with rounded pommels).

zh: 8.18　再论形态变换：高跷踏板
en: 8.18　The Same Continued: Stilt-Steps

zh: 长鼻形成的过程以及其他种种几何变换，可以在高跷踏板的雕刻中得到清晰的研究——高跷踏板是马克萨斯艺术的一种极具特色的形式（Steinen, ii, illus. 104-9; iii, βF, G, H, I）。踩高跷格斗的游戏是马克萨斯的一项主要竞技活动，人们把大量心力投入绑缚在高跷主杆上的硬木脚踏支撑的雕刻与装饰。高跷足部的一切雕刻形象本质上都起女像柱的作用，支撑着外伸的踏脚。女像柱形象斜接回高跷杆，夹角为锐角，形成一个可施以装饰处理的三棱柱。由于朝外的女像柱形象在背面与高跷杆相连，它们不像扇柄上的形象那样雕成雅努斯形式。最简单形式的高跷踏板由单个朝外的女像柱支撑，如
。然而，鉴于这些形象是一项危险运动的附属物——在这项运动中超自然的助力最为必需——增殖的倾向便迅速显现。即使在我刚引用的那个简单而相对早期（1804年）的例子中，一张附属的脸也已出现在基部、主女像柱形象的双脚之下。不过更常见的是，在主形象（上方那个）之下插入第二个完整形象（
）。基本女像柱形象还可以有许许多多种进一步的复杂化，我稍后加以描述。在此之前，让我回到高跷踏板上常见的“长鼻脸”这一话题。
en: The process of proboscis-formation, and various other geometric transformations, can be perspicuously studied in the carving on stilt-steps, a very characteristic form of Marquesan art (Steinen, ii, illus. 104-9; iii, β F, G, H, I). The game of fighting on stilts was a major sporting activity in the Marquesas, and much care was devoted to the carving and ornamentation of the hardwood foot-supports which were lashed to the main shafts of the stilts. All carved figures on stilt-feet essentially function as caryatids, supporting the projecting foot rest. The caryatid figure rejoins the shaft of the stilt at an acute angle, creating a triangular prism which can be subjected to ornamental treatment. Because outward-facing caryatid figures are joined at the back to the shaft of the stilt, they are not carved in Janus form, like the figures on fan handles. Stilt-steps in their simplest form are supported by a single outward-facing caryatid, as in

. However, given that these figures were adjuncts to a dangerous sport in which supernatural assistance was most necessary, the tendency towards proliferation rapidly asserts itself. Even in the simple and relatively early (1804) example I have just cited, a secondary face makes its appearance at the base, below the feet of the main caryatid figure. Very commonly, though, a second complete figure is inserted beneath the main, upper one (

). Very many further complications of the basic caryatid figure are possible, which I will describe in a moment. Before doing so, let me return to the subject of the ‘proboscis face' which commonly occurs on stilt-steps.

zh: 展示了几件高跷踏板中，鼻与口经过坐标变换形成长鼻的过程。应当指出，这些不是历时性的或进化性的过渡。马克萨斯艺术家可以随意制作他们喜欢的脸部比例；长鼻脸恰好填满上方主女像柱“脚”下留下的小三棱柱；解释这种变形的是“机械”理由而非进化理由，因为它是这样一种手段：在一个几何形状与真实头部全然不同的空间（锐角三棱柱）中，最大限度地利用可用表面来勾画具有巫术灵力的面部特征（尤其是朝外的大眼）。马克萨斯艺术中占统治地位的反自然主义毫不费力地就能满足这类要求；的确，对空间问题的巧妙解决似乎本身就是被追求的目的。这种处理空间的巧思，在改变前面所举的最简单的女像柱姿势时，表现得更加明显。
总结了高跷踏板上单个与多个女像柱形象的这些姿态的多样性。
en: shows the coordinate transformations involved in the transformation of nose/mouth into proboscis from a series of stilts. It should be noted that these are not diachronic or evolutionary transitions. Marquesan artists were free to produce facial proportions as they pleased; proboscis faces neatly fill the small triangular prism left beneath the 'feet' of the main Caryatid above; ‘mechanical' rather than evolutionary reasons explain this distortion, since it is a means of making maximum use of the available surface for the delineations of magically potent facial features (large outward-facing eyes, especially) in a space (an acute-angled prism) whose geometry is totally unlike that of a real head. The reigning anti-naturalism of Marquesan art has no trouble meeting such demands, indeed, ingenious solutions to spatial problems seem to have been pursued for their own sake. This spatial ‘wit' is even more apparent in the contortions introduced into the basic caryatid pose seen in our simplest example.
summarizes the variety of these poses of single and multiple caryatid figures on stilt-steps.

zh: 第一种变换（单个女像柱的变换）在于将身体旋转180度，而让脸保持原来的朝向、朝外。这一手法突出了反转女像柱的臀部，使其撅出，用当下的说法，仿佛在“露臀”。这种撅臀姿势毛利人无疑曾用来侮辱敌人；在我看来马克萨斯人很可能也有同样的想法，若如此，这一手法便可解读为向高跷格斗者的竞技对手发出的侮辱。它在高跷踏板上无疑比在任何其他地方都更常见，尽管扇柄上也能见到。下一种可能的变换是从一个形象到两个形象。这可以通过两种方式实现。其一，通过复制单个女像柱并旋转90度
，把它转化为雅努斯形式的女像柱，使两个女像柱现在分别朝前和朝后（
）。或者，把一个女像柱叠放在另一个之上，使其加倍（
en: The first transformation (of a single caryatid) consists of rotating the body 180 degrees while leaving the face in its original orientation, facing outwards. This device gives prominence to the buttocks of the reversed caryatid, which poke out, as if it were ‘mooning', to use the current expression. This buttock-poking gesture was certainly used by the Maori to insult their enemies and it seems probable to me that Marquesans had the same idea, in which case this device can be interpreted as an insult offered to the stilt-fighter's sporting opponent. It is certainly more common on stilt-steps than anywhere else, though it is also seen on fan handles. The next possible transformation is from one figure to two figures. This can be achieved in two ways. First, by converting the single caryatid into a Janus-form caryatid by duplicating it and rotating by 90 degrees, so that the two caryatids now face forwards and backwards (
). Or the caryatids can be doubled by placing one on top of the other (

zh: 最后，还可以通过引入朝向各异的更多附属形象来使设计进一步繁复。我先前就扇柄指出过，“支持者数量”这一主题在马克萨斯酋长权标的象征体系中意义重大，附属形象由此增殖。这一点也适用于高跷踏板，而且更为字面化，因为雕在这些人工制品上的形象确实“支撑”着其主人高人一头的地位。因此，发现附属的“支持者”从基本女像柱形式上萌生出来，并不令人惊讶。做法之一是把主女像柱的“四肢”转化为小埃图阿形象，即前面提到的层级化手法。其中最引人注目的例子在
中加以分析。在这件高跷踏板中，主女像柱下添了一尊长鼻的女像柱来“支撑”它。上方女像柱的头部又另外复制了两次（若这个形象没有同时配备普通手臂，这些就会是举起的“手臂”）。该女像柱身体的下部由两个埃图阿形象表现为（水平、朝内的）“腿”，而其“露臀”的臀部则变成了另外两个埃图阿“脸”。因此总计起来，这件高跷踏板包含八个不同的埃图阿形象，以增加其主人获胜的机会；或者说十六个，因为这只是一对中的一个。
en: Finally, the design can be elaborated by introducing further subsidiary figures in various orientations. I made the point earlier, with respect to fan handles, that the theme of ‘numbers of supporters' was of great significance in the symbolism of Marquesan chiefly regalia, hence the proliferation of subsidiary figures. This applies also to stilt-steps, though even more literally, since the figures carved on these artefacts do indeed ‘support' their owner's elevated position in the world. Hence it is not surprising to find subsidiary ‘supporters' sprouting from the basic caryatid form. One way of doing this is by converting the ‘limbs' of the main caryatid into little etua figures, that is, the device of hierarchization mentioned earlier. The most striking example of this is analysed in

. In this stilt-step, the main caryatid is doubled with a subsidiary ‘supporting' one, below (with a proboscis face). The head of the upper caryatid is secondarily doubled twice more (these would be raised ‘arms' were this figure not equipped with ordinary arms as well). The lower portion of the body of this caryatid is represented by two etua figures as (horizontal, inwards-pointing) ‘legs' and its ‘mooning' buttocks have become two more etua ‘faces'. So in total, this stilt-step contains eight distinct etua figures to increase its owner's chances of victory; or sixteen, since this is only one of a pair.

zh: 8.19　乌乌：三重叠合的双身提基
en: 8.19　Uu: The Ultimate Double-Double-Double Tiki

zh: 马克萨斯人之间的冲突并不限于高跷格斗这类竞技；他们也常打真正的仗。他们的主要战争武器，一如波利尼西亚人通常的情形，是沉重的木棍。马克萨斯棍棒的设计源自他们划独木舟所用的桨；事实上，非酋长阶层的战斗者的武器就是这样一支桨，或其用于格斗的加重版本。更富有、更重要的战士则拥有带雕刻装饰的特殊而相当标准化的棍棒，称为乌乌（u'u）。
en: Conflicts among the Marquesans were not confined to sports like stilt-fighting, they were also very prone to more serious battles. Their main weapons of war were, as usually among Polynesians, heavy wooden clubs. The design of Marquesan clubs was derived from the paddles they used to propel their canoes, and indeed the non-chiefly combatants' weapon would be one of these paddles, or a heavy version of one for fighting use. Richer and more important warriors had clubs of a special and rather standardized kind, with carved decoration, called u'u.

zh: 施泰因对这些雕花棍棒花了很大篇幅讨论；它们是各收藏中最令人印象深刻、也最常见的马克萨斯人工制品之一。马克萨斯棍棒是被制作成致命武器的雅努斯式埃图阿形象。鉴于前面关于前后对称与马克萨斯式分割再现的讨论，可以想见：棍棒没有背面或正面，因而没有“不设防”的后方，总是向观者展示其辟邪的“脸”。棍棒体现了我们已描述过的马克萨斯艺术的许多风格特征。实际上，从马克萨斯人的观点看，问题是怎样让人看出棍棒上的埃图阿，同时保留它原先那种光滑、浑圆、没有纹样的独木舟桨外形。施泰因在一幅分析图中展示了这是如何做到的，我把它复制为

（Steinen, iii, g β 1）。自上而下，我们首先看到顶端一个小的护佑性埃图阿脸，然后是一张极大的“脸”的上部，有两只圆睁的眼，其瞳孔本身又是附属的脸。其下是一条粗重的横杠。它通过上方一个缺口与下方另一个凹口，与上面的“脸”分隔开来。这条横杠构成了作为人形形象的棍棒的“肩”线。横杠中央还有一个突出的埃图阿头／面。再往下，我们看到两侧各有一个对称的梳状纹样，由一个“V”形相连；其下是一个卐字纹类型的护佑装置。我很快会给出施泰因对这些的巧妙解释。接着是另外两只“眼”，最后是一条包含埃图阿与“编织”母题的装饰带。施泰因另一幅棍棒图展示了两侧脸之间的“鞍”形凹陷；毫无疑问，棍棒既是经典的雅努斯式或“双身提基”形象，也是完全实用的武器。然而，施泰因对棍棒各部分的解释不止于此，因为他能够论证——我相信是正确的——每根棍棒是四个而非两个主形象的复合体。
en: Steinen devoted an enormous amount of attention to these carved clubs, which are among the most impressive and commonest Marquesan artefacts in collections. The Marquesan club is a Janiform etua image rendered as a lethal weapon. As might be anticipated in the light of the previous discussion of back-to-front symmetry and the Marquesan form of split representation, the club has no back or front, hence no ‘unguarded' rear, and always shows its apotropaic ‘face' to the viewer. The club manifests many of the stylistic characteristics of Marquesan art we have already described. In effect, the problem posed by the club from the Marquesan point of view, is to incorporate references to the etua schema into an artefact whose overall form remains modelled on the smooth, ovoid, and featureless canoe-paddle from which it is derived. Steinen shows how this is done in an analytical figure which I reproduce in

(Steinen, iii, g β 1). Descending, we see, first of all, a small protective etua face on the crown, then the upper part of a very large ‘face' with two staring eyes, whose pupils are themselves subsidiary faces. Below this, there is a heavy horizontal bar. This is set off from the ‘face' above it by a notch above and another indentation below. This bar constitutes the ‘shoulder' line of the club as an anthropomorphic figure. In the middle of the bar there is a further protruding etua head face. Descending further, we see a symmetrical comb-like pattern on either side connected by a ‘V' shape, and below this, a protective device of the hakenkreuz type. I shall shortly give Steinen's ingenious explanations for these. Then there come two more ‘eyes' and finally a decorative band containing etua and ‘woven' motifs. Steinen's other drawing of a club shows the depression of ‘saddle' between the faces on either side; there can be no doubt that clubs are classic Janiform or ‘double tiki' images as well as perfectly practical weapons. However, Steinen's interpretation of the parts of the club goes further than this, since he is able to argue, correctly I believe, that each club is a composite of four, rather than two, main figures.

zh: 施泰因的论证从一件外观迥异、尺度也迥异的人工制品出发：一个小型骨埃图阿形象，它的背面有一个四肢张开的附属小像护佑，其上还有一个卐字纹埃图阿护佑头部。正如我们刚才看过的高跷踏板上的“露臀”形象，这个小小“背驮”形象的身体朝向前方、露出臀部，只有头被旋向后方（
）。施泰因的巧妙提示是：这正是棍棒中所见的基本布局。突出于“肩杠”中央的头，是伏在背上的小人转向后方的头。横杠下方左右两侧的梳状纹样是小人张开的双手，“V”形则在它的双肩之间——护佑性的卐字纹母题就置于其下。伏在背上的小人看不见腿，但撅起的臀部仍看得见——它们已被变形为底部装饰带上方的第二组眼。
en: Steinen's argument starts out from a very different-looking artefact on a very different scale, a small bone etua figure which has a splayed subsidiary figure protecting its back, above which is a further hakenkreuz etua protecting the head. As with the ‘mooning' figures on the stilt-steps we have just looked at, the body of the little ‘piggy-back' figure is orientated forwards, showing the buttocks, and only the head is rotated backwards (

). Steinen's ingenious suggestion is that this is the basic layout seen in the club. The head which protrudes in the centre of the ‘shoulder-bar' is the backwards-pointing head of a piggy-back rider. The comb-like patterns to the left and right below the bar are the splayed hands of the rider, and the ‘V' shape between its shoulders, beneath which is placed the protective hakenkreuz motif. The legs of the piggy-back rider are not seen, but its mooning buttocks are-they have been transmogrified into the second set of eyes above the decorative band, at the bottom.

zh: 换言之，正对着我们的大像双臂张开，其中间有个小像的头。那小像伏在另一面的大像背上，护佑着棍棒另一侧巨大形象的背面。不仅棍棒的背面受到“护佑”——通过与正面对称——棍棒背面的背面还由正面的一个附属形象护佑（

）。到这一步，马克萨斯的空间思维似乎简直要用尽一切维度，以预判并抵御灵性危险。尤其当我们记得：伏在背上的小像也有自己的护佑者，即第三级的卐字纹埃图阿。同时，那种把附属的头与下方的臀／眼视为棍棒正面埃图阿母题简单重复的解释，也绝未被排除；人们可以说，棍棒的主“脸”既沿垂直轴（自上而下）也沿前后轴被复制。然而在我看来，基本图式恰恰如施泰因所主张的那样，而这种对维度的几何游戏与马克萨斯造型艺术的基本风格倾向完全合拍。
en: In other words, the subsidiary figure whose head we notice between the outstretched arms of the large figure facing us, is a piggy-back rider, protecting the back of the large figure on the other side of the club. Not only is the back of the club ‘protected'-by being symmetrical with the front-the back of the back of the club is protected by a subsidiary figure on the front (

). At this point it must seem that Marquesan spatial thinking is simply running out of dimensions in which to anticipate, and ward off, spiritual dangers. Especially when we remember that the back of the piggy-back rider is itself protected by a ‘third-order' protective figure in the form of the ‘hakenkreuz' etua. At the same time, the interpretation which would see the subsidiary head and the buttocks/eyes below as simple reduplications of the etua motif on the front of the club is not by any means ruled out; one could say that the main ‘face' of the club is duplicated in the vertical axis (top to bottom) as well as the proximal-distal axis (back to front). However, it seems to me that the basic schema is exactly as Steinen claims, and this geometric play with dimensions is absolutely in tune with the basic stylistic tendency of Marquesan plastic art.

zh: 8.20　融合：耳饰的叙事艺术
en: 8.20　Fusion: The Narrative Art of Ear-Ornaments

zh: 最后，为收束这一对马克萨斯风格的分析，我要简短讨论一种少些杀气的艺术形式——的确，若排除翻绳游戏，它是马克萨斯传统艺术中最富游戏性的一种。这就是象牙雕耳饰（插入耳垂上的大孔中），男女皆佩戴，施泰因在“miniaturplastik”（微型雕塑）这一恰当标题下加以讨论（Steinen, ii. 136-48）。如人们所料，这些耳饰中有许多以各种埃图阿型形象为特色，以不同构型加以重复。但比这些有趣得多的，是两类与我们迄今所考虑的其余艺术根本不同的耳饰：它们包含对神话叙事细节的明确指涉。唯一可与之相比的另一例子，是前面讨论过的纹身母题瓦伊奥凯纳（vai o kena），它指涉英雄凯纳纹身神话中的某一特定情节（讨论见Gell 1993: 186-8）。
en: Finally, to round off this analysis of the Marquesan style, I shall briefly discuss a less ferocious art form, indeed the most playful of the traditional Marquesan arts if one excludes string-figures. These are the carved ivory ear-ornaments (inserted into large holes in the earlobes) worn by both sexes and discussed by Steinen under the appropriate heading of ‘miniaturplastik' (Steinen, ii. 136-48). As one might expect, many of these ear-ornaments feature sundry etua-type figures, reduplicated in various configurations. But much more interesting than these are two types of ear-ornaments which depart radically from the rest of the art we have been considering in that they involve explicit references to details of mythic narratives. The only other comparable instance is the tattoo motif discussed earlier, vai o kena, which refers to a particular episode in the tattooing myth of the hero Kena (for discussion, see Gell 1993: 186-8).

zh: 我认为，这些耳饰之所以用来“讲故事”，和它们戴在耳朵上有关。神话正是通过耳朵进入身体的。耳不用说是一个身体孔窍，作为孔窍，它是脆弱的、需要护佑的。但护佑耳的主要方式，是在面颊上、靠近耳孔边缘处纹刺一类特殊的埃图阿纹样。既然耳孔已由此得到护佑，耳饰便难得地可以充当纯粹“世俗”的装饰。事实上，它们可以被看作造型艺术版的索尼随身听耳机，不停地把神话讲给佩戴它们的人听。
en: The fact that these ear-ornaments embody ‘narrative' is, I think, connected to the fact that they are specifically ear-ornaments, and it is through the ear that myths enter the body. The ear is, needless to say, an orifice of the body, and, as such, vulnerable and in need of being protected. But the main way of protecting the ear was by tattooing a special category of etua designs on the cheek, near the margin of the ear orifice. Since the ear orifice was protected in this way, the ear-ornaments could function, for once, as purely ‘secular' adornment. In fact, they might be seen as the plastic-art equivalents of Sony Walkman headphones, continually relaying mythic information into the ears to which they were attached.

zh: [图 8.20/1] 叙事艺术：耳栓上表现的“帕胡阿蒂蒂的女儿们荡秋千”。来源：Von den Steinen, iii, βR
en: FIG. 8.20/1. Narrative art: ‘Pahuatiti's daughters on their swing' depicted on ear-plugs. Source: Von den Steinen, iii, βR
parallelFigureCaption: [图 8.20/1] 叙事艺术：耳栓上表现的“帕胡阿蒂蒂的女儿们荡秋千”。来源：Von den Steinen, iii, βR
FIG. 8.20/1. Narrative art: ‘Pahuatiti's daughters on their swing' depicted on ear-plugs. Source: Von den Steinen, iii, βR

zh: 现存两类“叙事”耳饰所指涉的神话情节都与女性主题有关，我认为这些饰物专属于女性装束。第一类是“帕胡阿蒂蒂的女儿们荡秋千”母题（

）。帕胡阿蒂蒂的两个女儿被酋长托阿埃蒂尼说服，去羞辱神话英雄阿考伊：往他的卡瓦酒里撒尿。她们就在他上方荡秋千，等他把杯子举到唇边，便把尿撒进杯里。为这一冒犯，悬挂她们秋千的树枝被折断，她们被抛入深渊。（关于波利尼西亚秋千与秋千神话的新分析，见Lavondés, Journal of the Polynesian Society。）故事的不幸结局在耳饰中未被指涉，刻出的只有荡秋千那段恶作剧，而秋千由两个“奴隶”而非树枝撑起。从风格学的观点看，这组耳饰有趣之处在于马克萨斯雕刻者以何等精湛的技艺把四个形象（2个奴隶＋2个女孩）塞进如此微小的方寸之地，往往还把女孩倒置，让她们倒挂着“荡秋千”（第17、18号）。然而，设计常常自行转化为排列成行的小头和四肢，着眼于形式本身，如第25号。或者，设计屈服于埃图阿母题的引力（也许因其内在的对称性）。第33号已大大接近这一归宿，而
只保留对“叙事”设计最微弱的指涉，已成为一个埃图阿／马塔霍阿塔设计。
en: The mythic episodes referred to in the two types of ‘narrative' ear-ornaments which have survived both relate to feminine themes and I think that these ornaments were specifically items of female attire. The first of these types is the ‘Pahuatiti's daughters on their swing' motif (

). Pahuatiti's two daughters were persuaded by the chief Toaetini to humiliate the mythic hero Akaui, by pissing into his kava. They did so by swinging above him on their swing, and just at the critical moment, directing their urine into his cup, as he was raising it to his lips. For this affront, the branch from which their swing was suspended was broken off, and they were cast into the abyss. (For a new analysis of swings and swing-myths in Polynesia, see Lavondes, Journal of the Polynesian Society.) The unfortunate conclusion of the story is not referred to in the ear-ornaments, only the delicious episode of the swing, which is held up by two ‘slaves' rather than the branch of a tree. From a stylistic point of view, what is interesting about this set of ear-ornaments is the virtuosity with which Marquesan carvers manage to cram four figures (2 slaves + 2 girls) into such a tiny compass, often by inverting the girls, who ‘swing' upside down (nos. 17 and 18). However, the design often transforms itself into a purely formal exercise in rows of miniature heads and limbs, as in no. 25. Alternatively, the design succumbs to the gravitational pull of the etua motif (perhaps because of its intrinsic symmetry). Number 33 is well on the way to this destination, while
retains only the faintest reference to the ‘narrative' design, and has become an etua/mata hoata design.

FIG. 8.20/2. Ear-plug with swing narrative moving towards the etua/mata hoata motif. Source: Von den Steinen, ii. 148, illus. 128

zh: 最后，让我转向第二组“叙事”耳饰，它们关涉卡埃神话中的一个情节（讨论见Gell 1993: 184-6）。卡埃娶了希娜——这个女人通过定期到海里像螃蟹一般被打碎，以此返老还童：随后她被冲上海滩，带着一层新的软皮，软皮变硬，使她能重新成为少女。然而希娜和她的同伴们不知道如何分娩。她们岛上的接生者是两位凶兆女神法努阿，她们通过剖开母亲来接生婴儿，致使母亲死亡。卡埃教会希娜和岛上其他女人如何正确接生，法努阿愤而离去（分娩的并发症被归因于她们的恶意作祟）。法努阿的本义是“双重融合”——因此，一根茎上长成两根融合在一起的香蕉（香蕉有时确实如此生长）就是“法努阿”香蕉（Dordillon, “fanaua”）。如果我们相信佩戴这一类型的是女性这一点没错，那么这个产科神话非常适合以耳饰的形式来叙述。而且必须说，在这些身体纠缠的微观场景中，马克萨斯技艺显得比在任何其他地方都更富灵感。有五个主角，尽管施泰因给出了详细分析（见

），却不可能把他们与神话中的角色对应起来。右下角那个鸟头形象似乎是正在出生的婴儿，但这可能不对，因为事实上马克萨斯母亲分娩时由丈夫支撑着，躺在由姻亲和母方亲属的身体构成的平台上。因此这也可能是其中一位亲属。无论如何，图像志解释不如雕刻怎样利用身体互相融合而难以辨认这一构思重要，而法努阿神话真正关乎的正是后者。这一游戏性的、我认为本质上非辟邪的形象，与马克萨斯关于塔普（tapu，即可因接触而传递的神圣性）的仪式规则所严格维持的身体间的隔离恰恰对立；相反，它展示身体在难以分辨的纠缠中彼此融合。它本身不是一个仪式形象，而是对一个处处提防神圣性因接触而越界传递的世界的反讽性评论。但这引出了需要在更一般的文化框架中讨论的问题。是时候放下这些对具体马克萨斯艺术品及其变换的细微分析，重新提出先前暗示过的文化与风格之关系的问题了。之所以能够这样做，是因为到此为止，马克萨斯风格在图形与造型两种模式中的形式与形态方面，都已得到较为透彻的阐明。
en: Finally, let me turn to the second set of ‘narrative' ear-ornaments, which relate to an episode in the myth of Kae (discussed in Gell 1993: 184-6). Kae marries a woman who rejuvenates herself by periodically being smashed in the sea, like a crab, before being washed up on the beach with a new, soft skin, which hardens so that she can become a young girl again. However Hina and her companions do not know how to give birth. The midwives on their island are two female divinities of evil omen, Fanaua, who deliver babies by cutting the mother open, so that she dies. Kae teaches Hina and her women how to deliver babies properly and the Fanaua depart in anger (complications of childbirth were attributed to their malign efforts). Fanaua really means ‘fused together double’—thus, a banana which grows (as they sometimes do) as two bananas fused together on one stem is a ‘fanaua' banana (Dordillon, ‘fanaua'). This obstetrical myth is a very suitable one for narration in the form of ear-ornaments, if we are correct in believing that women were the ones who wore this type. And it must be said that nowhere does Marquesan artistry seem more inspired than in these microscopic tableaux of entangled bodies. There are five protagonists, whom it is impossible to identify with the characters in the myth, though Steinen gives a detailed analysis (see

). The birdheaded individual at the bottom right seems to be the child being born, though this may not be right because in fact Marquesan mothers gave birth supported by their husbands and lying on a platform composed of the bodies of their affinal/maternal kin. So this could be one of them. The iconographic interpretation is anyway less important than the technical exploitation of the idea of ambiguously fused bodies, which is what the Fanaua myth is really about. This playful and I think essentially non-apotropaic image is the antithesis of the separation and insulation of body from body which Marquesan ritual rules about tapu (contagious sacredness) upheld with such stringency; instead, it shows bodies merging into one another in an indistinguishable tangle. Rather than being a ritual image in itself, it is an ironic commentary on a world suffused with the magical danger of contagion and unboundedness. But this raises issues which need to be discussed in a more general cultural framework. The time has come to leave aside these minute analyses of specific Marquesan artworks and their transformations, and to raise once more the problem of the relationship between culture and style alluded to earlier. It is possible to do this because, by now, the formal and morphological aspects of the Marquesan style, in both the graphic and plastic modes, have been more thoroughly elucidated.
