zh: 8.21　结论：马克萨斯艺术与社会关系中的连贯性
en: 8.21　Conclusion: Coherence in Marquesan Art and Social Relations

zh: 是时候回到前面提出的风格问题了。我主张，风格是形式的“关系之间的关系”。前面对马克萨斯艺术形式的分析，目的在于展示个别母题（尤其在纹身中，也在造型艺术形式中）如何经由种种修改而相互转化。从形式的观点看，马克萨斯风格就是由所有这些变换或修改之间成立的关系所构成的复合体。也就是说，支配马克萨斯艺术品生产（在文化所规定的风格参数之内的创新）的约束，是支配一个母题或形式能否转化为相关形式的约束；只有当这种转化可能时，一个母题或形式才可以说“属于”马克萨斯风格。在这个意义上，马克萨斯风格既是统一的又是动态的：构成这种风格的，是规则所允许的一切母题变换，范围比现存实例广。
en: It is time to review the problem of style in the light of the ground just traversed. Style, I argue, is ‘relations between relations' of forms. The aim of the preceding analyses of Marquesan art forms was to show how individual motifs (particularly in tattooing, but also in plastic art forms) could be transformed into one another by various modifications. The Marquesan style, from a formal point of view, is the complex formed by the relationships which hold between all these transformations or modifications. That is to say, the constraints governing the production (innovation within culturally prescribed parameters of style) of Marquesan artworks were constraints governing the possibility of transforming a motif or form into related forms; only if such a transformation is possible can a motif or form be said to ‘belong' to the Marquesan style. In this sense, the Marquesan style is both unitary and dynamic; it is a field of possible or legitimate motivic transformations, rather than the totality of existing instantiations of such transformations.

zh: 现在出现的问题是马克萨斯视觉艺术中的风格与更广泛意义上的马克萨斯“文化”之间的关系。这里其实有两个需要区分的问题：其一，以人工制品形式存在的“文化”与其他面貌的“文化”——亲属制度、经济、政治与宗教——之间的关系。其二，文化与视觉艺术风格之间的关系问题，这是一个窄得多的问题。文化与器物制作之间的关系，至少在一定程度上独立于器物的风格，因为各种风格的人工制品都可以服务于任何给定文化中指派给人工制品的文化角色。举一个例子。在马克萨斯语境中，亲属制度的一般形式（德拉维达型，优先选择母方交表婚）与纹身／身体艺术之间存在可证明的关系。纹身是一种“包裹”形式（pahu tiki，“以形象包裹”），而pahu也是一个亲属称谓范畴，意为“母方亲属＋姻亲”（Gell 1993: 176 ff.）。换言之，德拉维达式亲属关系有一种向内包裹的特点。政治援助由环绕个人的母方亲属提供，新娘也来自这个亲属圈。纹身以保护性的纹样裹住个人，正是这套关系图式迁移到身体艺术后的表现。然而让我们假设，马克萨斯纹身并不具有它实际具有的视觉外观，而是看起来像萨摩亚纹身。萨摩亚纹身母题的生成方式与马克萨斯纹身母题完全不同，代表的是一个全然不同的风格系统。但是，如果像我们的思想实验所假设的那样，马克萨斯人拥有的是“萨摩亚”纹身而非他们自己的纹身，那么关于德拉维达亲属制度与纹身之联系，仍然完全可能提出恰恰相同的论证。
en: The question that now arises is the relationship between style in Marquesan visual art and Marquesan ‘culture' in the wider sense. There are really two questions here which need to be distinguished; first, the relationship between ‘culture' in the form of artefacts and ‘culture' in other guises-kinship, economy, politics, and religion. Secondly, there is the problem of the relationship between culture and visual-art style, which is a much narrower question. The relationship between culture and the material artefact production is at least relatively independent of stylistic considerations, in that artefacts in a variety of styles might subserve the cultural role assigned to artefacts in any given culture. Let me give an example. In the Marquesan context, there is a demonstrable relationship between the general form of the kinship system (Dravidian, with preferential matrilateral cross-cousin marriage) and tattooing/body arts. Tattooing is a form of ‘wrapping' (pahu tiki, ‘wrapping in images') and pahu is also a kinship category meaning ‘matrikin + affines' (Gell 1993: 176 ff.). In other words, the characteristic involution of the Dravidian kinship universe, where political succour and brides come from an enclosing circle of matrilateral relatives, is connected, via a scheme transfer, to body arts which enclose the individual in a protective wrapping of tattooing. Let us suppose, however, that Marquesan tattooing did not have the visual appearance it actually does have, and that it looked instead like Samoan tattooing. Samoan tattoo motifs are generated in a quite different way from Marquesan tattoo motifs, and represent a different stylistic system altogether. But if, as our gedankexperiment supposes, the Marquesans had had ‘Samoan' tattooing in place of their own, it would still have been perfectly possible to advance exactly the same argument concerning the connection between Dravidian kinship and tattooing.

zh: 因此，如果一些关于“风格”与文化之关系的推论实际上基于人工制品在文化中的角色、而完全独立于其风格，那么人们必须警惕做出这类推论。同样，如果所用论证依赖图像志，人们也没有证明艺术风格与文化之间的联系。这一点例如适用于具有宗教或崇拜意义的形象。一个表现或体现某神祇的形象可能采取多种多样的视觉形式；先验地无法断言，神像实际采用的那种合乎风格规范的形式必然与该神祇的任何其他文化方面相联系。神祇的标准表现可能不同，而与该神祇相联系的其他一切文化参数却保持不变。
en: For this reason, one has to beware of making inferences about the relationship between ‘style' and culture if these inferences are really based on the role of artefacts in culture, quite independently of their style. Similarly, one has not demonstrated a link between art style and culture if the arguments used rely on iconography. This applies, for instance, to images of religious or cult significance. An image which represents or embodies a certain divinity might take on a wide variety of different visual forms; there is no saying, a priori, that the stylistically standardized form actually assumed by a representation of a divinity is necessarily connected to any other cultural aspect of this divinity. The standard representation of the divinity might be different, yet every other cultural parameter connected with the divinity remain the same.

zh: 事实上，设想某种一般意义上的“文化”对人工制品的视觉风格负责，是一个错误。文化可以规定人工制品的实践和／或象征意义及其图像志解释；但支配人工制品视觉外观的唯一因素，是它们与同一风格中其他人工制品的关系。视觉风格是一个自主领域，意思是它只能依据人工制品与其他人工制品之间的关系来定义；把“文化”想象成某种“总部”，一方面规定政治竞争采取什么形式，另一方面规定人工制品长什么样，是错误的。器物的形式是在“器物之间的关系领域”中塑造出来的。它们遵循器物之间既有的形式与风格关系，不受某个想象中的“总部”支配。
en: In fact, it is an error to imagine that ‘culture' in some general sense, is responsible for the visual style of artefacts. Culture may dictate the practical and/or symbolic significance of artefacts, and their iconographic interpretation; but the only factor which governs the visual appearance of artefacts is their relationship to other artefacts in the same style. Visual style is an autonomous domain in the sense that it is only definable in terms of the relationships between artefacts and other artefacts; it is a mistake to think of ‘culture' as a kind of ‘head office' which decrees, on the one hand, what form political competition will assume, and on the other, what artefacts will look like. Artefacts are shaped in the ‘inter-artefactual domain', obeying the immanent injunctions governing formal stylistic relationships among artefacts, not in response to external injunctions from some imaginary ‘head office'.

zh: 如果像我刚才论证的那样，视觉风格的相对自主性意味着支配人工制品外观的因素主要属于人工制品领域，那么这是否意味着风格与文化之间的完全脱节？我认为不完全是；但为了构造一个不落入汉森（1983：上文已讨论）同样陷阱的关于这一关系的理论，必须小心推进。我们当然不能像他那样，直接从艺术品的风格属性（如两侧对称）论证社会文化系统的属性。另一方面，也许可以构造论证，把作为系统的风格内部的“贯通风格的主轴”与文化的其他系统属性联系起来。
en: If it is true, as I have just argued, that the relative autonomy of visual style implies that the factors governing the appearance of artefacts belong primarily to the artefactual domain, then does that imply a complete disjunction between style and culture? Not quite, I think, but in order to formulate a theory of this relationship which does not fall into the same pitfalls as Hanson's (1983: discussed above) it is necessary to proceed with care. We certainly cannot argue, as he does, directly from stylistic properties of artworks (such as bifold symmetry) to properties of socio-cultural systems. On the other hand, it may be possible to construct arguments connecting the ‘axes of coherence' within styles as systems, and other systematic properties of culture.

zh: 诚然这相当拗口，所以我必须试着把自己解释得更清楚。这些“贯通风格的主轴”是什么？在前面对马克萨斯艺术的讨论中，我展示了人工制品之间的关系可以通过应用变换来产生；其中包括：
en: This is admittedly rather a mouthful, so I must try to explain myself more clearly. What are these ‘axes of coherence'? In the preceding discussion of Marquesan art, I showed that relationships among artefacts could be produced by applying transformations; among these were:

zh: • 整体或部分母题的平面几何变换（平移、旋转、反射等）
en: • plane geometric transformations of whole or part-motifs (translation, rotation, reflection, etc.)

zh: • 剪贴操作（如霍佩韦希内分析中描述的那些）
en: • cutting-and-pasting operations (such as those described in the analysis of hope vehine)

zh: • 坐标变换（在不同坐标中重新配置母题，参见凯阿分析或“长鼻形成”分析）
en: • coordinate transformations (reconfiguring motifs in different coordinates cf. the analysis of Kea or the analysis of ‘proboscis formation')

zh: • 层级化（一个母题从属于另一个母题，如“棍棒”设计中从属埃图阿护佑上级埃图阿的“背面”）
en: • hierarchization (one motif being subordinated to another, e.g. a subordinate etua protecting the ‘back' of a superior etua as in the ‘club' design)

zh: • 母题变换（一个母题变成另一个母题，如埃图阿 → 马塔霍阿塔）
en: • motif-transformation (one motif becomes another, e.g. etua → mata hoata)

zh: • 经由图底反转的变换（如玳瑁头饰分析中）
en: • transformation by figure-ground reversal (as in the analysis of shell diadems)

zh: • 经由正反面的复制从二维到三维的变换（雅努斯形象）
en: • transformation from two to three dimensions by front-to-back reduplication (Janus figures)

zh: • 把平面“弯曲”从二维到三维的变换（小型骨提基）
en: • transformation from two to three dimensions by ‘curvature' (small bone tiki)

zh: • 受规则支配的比例变换，如头身比
en: • rule-governed transformations of proportions, as in the head-to-body ratio

zh: • 立体几何变换（如“露臀”高跷形象中身体相对于头的朝向切换）
en: • solid-geometry transformations (e.g. switching the orientation of the body with respect to the head as in ‘mooning' stilt-figures)

zh: • 形式化（如埃图阿 → 卐字纹变换）
en: • formalization (as with the etua → hakenkreuz transformation)

zh: • 融合（如法努阿耳饰分析中）。
en: • fusion (as in the analysis of fanaua ear-ornaments).

zh: 这是一份相当长的清单。我的主张是：它或多或少覆盖了定义马克萨斯艺术品之间关系的那些母题或形状变换类型。这是人们所能得到的对“马克萨斯风格”最明确的描述。可以合理假设：任何地方的任何其他艺术风格，若从同一观点分析，都不会产生恰恰相同的清单。清单上的某些项目可能被包括，但不会全部；还可能检测到马克萨斯艺术中找不到的其他变换模式。
en: This is quite a long list. My claim is that it more or less covers the types of motivic or shape transformations which define the relationships between Marquesan artworks. This is the nearest one can get to an explicit description of ‘the Marquesan style'. It is reasonable to assume that no other art style, anywhere, would produce exactly the same list if analysed from the same point of view. Some items on the list might be included, but not all, and other transformational modes might be detected, which are not to be found in Marquesan art.

zh: 下一步是以“关系之间的关系”来表述马克萨斯风格——清单上列出的每一种变换，都是器物之间的一种基本“关系”。
en: The next step is to formulate the Marquesan style in terms of ‘relations between relations'-given that the primary inter-artefactual ‘relations' are the ones identified in the preceding listing.

zh: 这里重要的是记住：这份“清单”归纳自马克萨斯器物，不能用它断定器物之间会有哪些关系。我所建议的路径在这方面完全开放。我所断言的只是：“风格”建立在人工制品之间的联系之上。这一点既适用于“伦勃朗作品全集”，也适用于“所有马克萨斯人工制品”。伦勃朗作品之间的关系当然存在，但它们与马克萨斯纹身母题或雕刻之间存在的关系全然不同。伦勃朗作品间的关系来自手法、光线、姿态、面相等——这些考虑在马克萨斯集体风格中不起作用。（伦勃朗绘画之间的）“关系之间的关系”会涉及不同于我即将就马克萨斯人工制品提出的那些因素，并相应地把讨论引向全然不同的方向（情感心理学、戏剧等）。
en: Here, it is important to bear in mind that the ‘list' has been arrived at via induction from Marquesan artefacts; it is by no means a theory about the intrinsic possibilities of inter-artefactual relationships. The approach I suggest is totally permissive in this respect. All I assert is that ‘style' is founded on connections between artefacts. This would apply to ‘the complete works of Rembrandt' just as much as to ‘all Marquesan artefacts'. Relationships between Rembrandt's works certainly exist, but they are nothing like the ones which exist between Marquesan tattoo-motifs or carvings. Inter-Rembrandt relationships derive from handling, lighting, pose, physiognomy, etc.-considerations which are completely foreign to the Marquesan collective style. ‘Relations between relations' (between Rembrandt paintings) would involve different factors from the ones I am about to advance with respect to Marquesan artefacts, and would, accordingly, orient the discussion in an entirely different direction (emotional psychology, drama, etc.).

zh: 实际上，不难感觉到这份清单中的各项变换共有的倾向。我认为这种同质性来自一个结构原则，可以称之为“最小差异原则”：即形成一个新的母题或形象时，只对相近的母题作足以显出区别的最小改动。因此，“脸”（马塔霍阿塔）看起来像“坐着的埃图阿”并没有内在理由；但马克萨斯风格规定：既然二者事实上要被区别，它们就应尽可能彼此相像。同样，三维的“脸”（在雕刻形象上）应当是二维脸的“弯曲”版本、而非以三个充分实现的维度雕出的脸，这也没有内在理由。但马克萨斯风格要求雕刻的脸被表现为“弯曲”的二维脸；即对三维性做出尽可能小的让步。同样，二维形象在前后两面复制，成为三维的雅努斯式形象，使二维与三维之间的概念距离最小化。再举一例：坐着的埃图阿可以转化为龟，只需对母题的规范朝向做一次纯粹“虚拟”的移动（从垂直到水平），而母题的形式不发生任何改变。同样的考虑适用于坐标变换、图底反转等等。
en: As it is, there is no difficulty in sensing a certain homogeneity in this listing, a certain basic trend. This homogeneity derives, I think, from a structural principle which one could call ‘the principle of least difference', that is to say the forms taken by motifs and figures are the ones involving the least modification of neighbouring motifs consistent with the establishment of a distinction between them. Thus, there is no intrinsic reason why a ‘face' (mata hoata) should look like a ‘seated etua'; but the Marquesan style decrees that they should look as much like one another as possible, given that they are, in fact, to be distinguished. Similarly, there is no intrinsic reason why a three-dimensional ‘face' (on a carved image) should be a ‘curved' version of a two-dimensional face rather than a face carved in three fully realized dimensions. But the Marquesan style demands that carved faces be represented as ‘curved' two-dimensional faces; that is, the least possible concession to three-dimensionality. Similarly, two-dimensional images become three-dimensional Janus figures by back-to-front reduplication, minimizing the conceptual distance between two and three dimensions. A seated etua, to give a further example, can be transformed into a tortoise, by a purely ‘virtual' shift in the canonic orientation of the motif (from vertical to horizontal) without any change in the form of the motif whatsoever. The same considerations apply to coordinate transformations, figure-ground reversals, and so on.

zh: 最小差异原则也适用于层级化的语境。马克萨斯艺术与其他东波利尼西亚艺术风格共有的一种倾向，是制作可称为“分形”的形象：如著名的鲁鲁图“阿阿”那样的形象，其中一个形象由较小的形象构成（上文7.11已讨论）。马克萨斯的例子由高跷踏板（
）与“棍棒”设计（
）提供。“分形”艺术品体现了最小差异原则，因为（上级）形象的（附属）“部分”是本身即为形象的形式，因而与独立存在的相邻形象（或母题）尽可能相似（事实上相同）。在常见的情形中（参见
、8.19/1与8.20/3），从属母题实际上是上级母题的变换版本，此时部分与整体也经由“最小差异”原则相联系。
en: The principle of least difference also applies in the context of hierarchization. Marquesan art shares with other eastern Polynesian art styles a propensity for producing what might be termed ‘fractal' figures, images such as the famed Rurutan ‘A'a' in which a figure is composed of lesser figures (discussed above, 7.11). Marquesan examples are provided by stilt-steps (
) and the ‘club' design (

). ‘Fractal' artworks exemplify the least difference principle in that (subsidiary) ‘parts' of (superordinate) figures are forms which are themselves figures, and hence are as similar as possible (in fact, identical) to neighbouring figures (or motifs) leading independent existences. Where, as is commonly the case (cf.
, 8.19/1, and 8.20/3), the subordinate motif is actually a transformed version of the superordinate one, parts are related to wholes by the ‘least difference' principle as well.

zh: “最小差异原则”（也许最后一种情形除外）在孤立看待的任何特定马克萨斯人工制品中都检测不到，而只在所有马克萨斯人工制品构成的关系总体中才能检测到。（马克萨斯人工制品之间的）“关系之间的关系”以向“最小差异”原则的收敛为特征：这就是贯通整个马克萨斯风格的“主轴”。既然我们现在考虑的是一个完全抽象的原则——它只有在器物彼此联系的总体中才会显现——那么或许可以合理地说：在这一点上我们已达到一个抽象层次，在此层次上也许可能对马克萨斯风格做出文化解释。也就是说，尽管如我先前论证的，相信“马克萨斯文化”直接规定马克萨斯人工制品所采取的视觉形式是错误的，但推断支配“关系之间的关系”的抽象原则属于更广泛意义上的“文化”、而非人工制品间领域，却并非那么不合理。
en: The ‘least difference principle' (except possibly in the last instance) is not detectable in any specific Marquesan artefact, taken in isolation, but only in the ensemble of relations constituted by all Marquesan artefacts. ‘Relations between relations' (between Marquesan artefacts) are characterized by convergence towards the ‘least difference' principle: this is the ‘axis of coherence' of the Marquesan style, overall. Since we are now considering a totally abstract principle which is not concretely instantiated in any given Marquesan artefact, but only in the ensemble of their relations with one another, it may be reasonable to suggest that at this point we have arrived at a level of abstraction at which it may be possible to provide a cultural interpretation of the Marquesan style. That is to say, although it would be mistaken, as I argued earlier, to believe that ‘Marquesan culture' dictates the visual form taken by Marquesan artefacts directly, it is not so unreasonable to infer that the abstract principles governing ‘relations between relations' belong to ‘culture' in the wider sense, rather than the inter-artefactual domain.

zh: 让我们从文化立场考虑“最小差异原则”。如我在别处所描述的（1993，尤其借助Thomas 1990的研究），马克萨斯社会的特征是在等级秩序分散或瓦解的政治环境中对“社会差异”的强烈关注——在这种语境中，“差异”在实践中极难维持。由于普遍的政治不稳定与动荡，以及地位竞争的激烈，马克萨斯人必须不断寻求加固和保护自己的社会身份，以抵御对其财富、权力与社会支持的外部威胁。这种在身份分散、差别消失威胁下维持完整性的斗争，在仪式上表现为对个体间接触与共食规则的强烈关注。社会互动中遵守严格规则，以使个人的塔普（可因接触而传递的神圣性）不致伤害他人，也不致因被侵犯而伤害其拥有者。我已在别处详细展示马克萨斯纹身与其他身体艺术如何与这幅个人与灵性完整性不断受威胁的图景相一致。但身份之所以受威胁，恰恰因为它极易随关系与场合而变。马克萨斯人可以随意切换社会身份（通过交换名字、收养及其他实践），于是我们得到这样一个（表面上）悖谬的局面：一个以主张和保护社会／灵性身份为核心关注的文化，同时也是身份异常脆弱的文化。回想我们先前对列维-斯特劳斯的讨论：这是一个社会地位在理论上完全取决于谱系的社会——而同时，谱系可以是任意的政治虚构这一点也被接受。
en: Let us consider the ‘least difference principle' from a cultural standpoint. Marquesan society, as I have described elsewhere (1993 drawing particularly on the work of Thomas 1990) was characterized by an acute preoccupation with ‘social difference' in a political context of ‘devolved' or fractured hierarchy in which ‘difference' was exceptionally difficult to sustain, practically. Because of the prevailing political instability and turmoil, and the vehemence of status-competition, Marquesans had continually to seek to reinforce and protect their social identities against external threats to their wealth, power, and social support. This struggle to maintain integrity against the threat of dispersal and de-differentiation was expressed ritually in an acute preoccupation with rules of inter-individual contact and commensality. Stringent rules were observed in social interaction so that an individual's tapu (contagious sacredness) should not harm others, or, by being infringed, harm its possessor. I have shown in detail elsewhere how Marquesan tattoo and other body arts are consistent with this picture of continually threatened personal and spiritual integrity. But identity was only under threat because it was so labile, so relative and situational. Marquesans could switch social identities at will (by name-exchange, adoption, and other practices) so we have the (apparently) paradoxical situation that a culture whose central preoccupation seems to have been the assertion and protection of social/spiritual identity is also the culture in which identity is exceptionally tenuous. This was a society, to recall our earlier discussion of Levi-Strauss, in which social status was, theoretically speaking, wholly a matter of pedigree-and in which it was, simultaneously, accepted that pedigrees could be arbitrary political fictions.

zh: 至少可以合理主张：马克萨斯风格中的“最小差异原则”，与在差异容易消解时着力维持差异的普遍倾向之间存在联系——后者正是马克萨斯社会文化态度总体的标志。
en: It seems at least plausible to argue that there is a connection between the ‘principle of least difference' in Marquesan stylistic, and the prevailing preoccupation with differentiation in the context of dissolution which is the hallmark of Marquesan socio-cultural attitudes generally.

zh: 这种契合如何产生？这里必须记住：马克萨斯风格只是马克萨斯艺术家在漫长历史发展过程中采取的无数细小的创作行动累积的结果。每一件新的人工制品，无论多么标准化，其产生都离不开风格决策的需要，无论这些决策表面上多么琐碎、多么无关紧要。这些风格决策——马克萨斯风格的连贯性、稳定性与长期变换由此而来——是在没有刻意反思的情况下做出的，但却从未脱离一种处处提防灵性或政治越界的社会处境。也就是说，在人工制品领域中稍加改动便从一个母题得到另一个的操作方式，与社会领域中在难分彼此的同质背景中人为地划出“差异”的操作方式之间，存在一种选择亲和性。马克萨斯风格在生成各各微妙有别的变体形式上的无限丰产力，加上其显著的形式同质性，同时暗示了一种确立差异的压倒性需要，以及对一切差异仅具相对性质的承认。
en: How did this consonance arise? Here one must recall that the Marquesan style is only the sedimented product of an infinite number of tiny social initiatives taken by Marquesan artists over a long period of historical development. Each new artefact, however standardized, cannot come into being without the need for stylistic decisions, be they ever so apparently trivial and inconsequential. These stylistic decisions, from which the coherence, stability, and long-term transformation of the Marquesan style ensued, were taken without deliberate reflection, but never without cognizance of a prevailing social context of social forms, pervaded by a dread of spiritual/political transgression. That is to say, there was an elective affinity between a modus operandi in the artefactual domain, which generated motifs from other motifs by interpolating minuscule variations, and a modus operandi in the social realm which created ‘differences' arbitrarily against a background of fusional sameness. The limitless fertility of the Marquesan style in generating variant forms, each subtly distinct, coupled with its striking formal homogeneity simultaneously suggest an overwhelming need to establish difference and a recognition of the merely relative character of all differences.

zh: 在这个意义上，可以说马克萨斯艺术风格中母题与形象之间的关系，类似于社会层面上马克萨斯人彼此之间存在的关系。艺术品类似于社会施动者，因为它们是人们以社会习得的特定感受方式付诸行动的产物。这一判断在本质方面与马克萨斯人自己对其艺术的看法相合。我讨论过的母题与形象在他们的语言中都被归类为提基（tiki）：“形象”。这个词还有另外两个有意义的语境。“提基”（作为神话英雄的名字）是马克萨斯的亚当。人类最初是由原初祖先（提基）使一个沙造的女人受孕而创造的：沙做的女人生下一个人类女儿，父亲又与女儿乱伦，使她受孕——父亲为掩盖自己的容貌而把脸涂黑来伪装自己。人类据说即源于这一结合（Steinen 1988）。这位塑造和消去容貌的人就是提基，第一个人。这里我们观察到形象制作与人之制作之间的基本图式迁移。
en: In this sense, it is true to say that the relationships among motifs and figures in the Marquesan art style are akin to the relations which existed, on the social plane, between the Marquesans themselves. Artworks are like social agents, in that they are the outcome of social initiatives which reflect a specific, socially inculcated sensibility. This judgement coincides in essential respects with the view taken by the Marquesans themselves of their art. The motifs and figures I have discussed are all categorized, in their language, as tiki: ‘images'. There are two other contexts in which this word has meaning. ‘Tiki' (as the name of a mythological hero) is the Marquesan Adam. Humankind were originally created through the impregnation of a woman made of sand by the original ancestor (Tiki), who produced a human daughter, who was in turn incestuously impregnated by her father, who disguised himself by blackening his face in order to conceal his appearance. From this union humankind are supposed to spring (Steinen 1988). This maker and un-maker of appearances is Tiki, the first man. Here we observe the fundamental scheme-transfer between image-making and the making of persons.

zh: 提基的另一个意义是某个分布式对象的“部分”或“份额”（Dordillon）。如果我把一个蛋糕切成十二片，每一片都是蛋糕的一个提基。人之所以是提基，是因为他们的身份依据他们所参与并从中分出的集体来定义。同时，这一用法预示了贯穿本章的一个主题观念：艺术品是“更大统一体”的全息碎片，它们经由风格纽带与这些统一体相联。表现（或更准确地说，构成）埃图阿的提基（形象／部分），是所有埃图阿之想象总体的全息碎片或折射。艺术品是一个分布式对象的份额或部分，该对象对应于马克萨斯系统中散布于不同时刻和地点的全部作品。这一观念将在下一章更详细地探讨。
en: The other meaning of tiki is ‘portions' or ‘shares' of some distributed object (Dordillon). If I cut a cake into twelve slices, each slice is a tiki of the cake. Human persons are tiki because their identities are defined in terms of the collectivities they participate in and divide from. At the same time, this usage adumbrates an idea which has been thematic throughout this chapter, namely that artworks are holographic fragments of the ‘larger unities' to which they are united by stylistic linkages. The tiki which represent (or more precisely, constitute) etua, are holographic fragments, or refractions, of the imaginary totality of all etua. Artworks are shares or portions of a distributed object corresponding to all of the artworks in the Marquesan system, distributed in time and space. This idea will be explored in more detail in the next chapter.

zh: 底本在此并列1804与1813–14两组年份，后文8.9说兰斯多夫1804年发表版画，图8.11/6又标1813。保留底本各处记载。
en: The print edition gives both 1804 and 1813–14 here. Section 8.9 gives 1804, and Fig. 8.11/6 gives 1813. The dates are retained as printed.

zh: 类比式中“图形艺术”在前、“造型艺术”在后，照录印本。上文分别将双面形象和分割再现归于造型艺术和图形艺术。
en: The order ‘graphic art : plastic art’ follows the printed formula. The preceding prose associates Janus-faced images with plastic art and split representation with graphic art.

zh: 印本此处写“旋转90度”，随后又说两个形象分别朝前和朝后，均照录。
en: The printed text gives a 90-degree rotation and then describes the figures as facing forwards and backwards. Both readings follow the print edition.

zh: 如果说“视觉句法”的想法还有什么可取之处的话，那在于安排或构图的原则，比如约尔恩古树皮画布局中所显现的那些原则，莫菲（1991, 1992）对此做过描述与分析。不过，这里不打算沿这一特定路线走下去。
en: To the extent that there is any mileage at all in the idea of ‘visual syntax’ it concerns principles of arrangement or composition, such as those which are manifested in the layout of Yolngu bark-painting, as described and analysed by Morphy (1991, 1992). This particular approach will not be pursued here, however.

zh: 当然，把身体艺术当作首要的，把雕刻、刻纹之类的艺术当作次要的，从西方艺术理论的观点看是一种古怪的做法；西方艺术理论主要关心被视为独立审美实体的绘画与雕塑，而不是活的存在者与社会施动者的单纯附属物。纹身在西方被视为相当次要的艺术形式，但在马克萨斯语境中并非如此。
en: Of course, treating body-art as primary, and such arts as carving and engraving as secondary, is an eccentric procedure from the standpoint of Western art theory, which concerns itself primarily with paintings and sculptures viewed as independent aesthetic entities rather than as the mere appurtenances of living beings and social agents. Tattooing in the West is a very second-rate form of art, but in the Marquesan context this was not so.

zh: 读者中若有人熟悉列维-斯特劳斯对神话施行的那类剪开、倒转再拼接的操作——他借此展示表面上看来毫不相似的神话之间的亲缘关系——就会领会这类程序的意义。
en: Readers of this who happen to be familiar with the type of cutting, inverting, and pasting operations to which Lévi-Strauss subjects myths in order to demonstrate the affinities between myths which do not, on the surface, appear to be at all similar, will appreciate the significance of this type of procedure.

zh: 一个有趣的问题由以下事实引出：这些成对的埃图阿的“龟”母题又被称为莫科（moko），即“蜥蜴”——凭其弯曲的四肢与拉长的体形，它们确实更像蜥蜴。波利尼西亚纹身文献中一个未解之谜是：新西兰毛利人著名的纹身艺术为什么被称为莫科。莫科在马克萨斯纹身中作为凯阿（卡凯）的别称出现，无疑富于暗示。蜥蜴与龟一样是神圣的存在，在马克萨斯艺术中多次出现。龟与蜥蜴这类如此不同的爬行动物在马克萨斯艺术中变得视觉上同义，部分反映了它们相似的象征关联。
en: An interesting question is raised by the fact that these double-etua ‘tortoise’ motifs are alternatively known as moko, i.e. ‘lizards’ which they do indeed much more resemble by virtue of their crooked limbs and elongated body shape. One of the unsolved mysteries of the literature on Polynesian tattooing is why the famous tattoo art of the New Zealand Maori should have been known as moko. The presence of moko as an alternative designation for kea (kake) in Marquesan tattoo is certainly suggestive. Lizards were, like tortoises, sacred beings, and they make numerous appearances in Marquesan art. The way in which such dissimilar reptiles as tortoises and lizards have become visually synonymous in Marquesan art partly reflects their similar symbolic associations.

zh: 尽管本章主要关注形态与风格，但或许不妨指出——尤其在谈到这些骨雕饰物时——马克萨斯艺术品几乎总是用本身就具有意义（即具有仪式灵力）的材料制成的。例如这些发饰便是用人骨制成的；它们的护佑之力既来自形态，也来自材质。尽管它们是独立的对象，它们却仍是身体的一部分：既因为它们附着于佩戴者的身体，也因为它们取自他人的身体——作为骨骼被取出，随后雕成饰物。因此，它们与纹身母题的比乍看之下更相似。纹身用活人的血肉制作，骨饰则用骨骼制作。两种作品的含义在很大程度上相同。
en: Though this chapter is primarily concerned with morphology and style, it might be as well to point out, especially in connection with these ornaments of carved bone, that Marquesan works of art are almost always created from materials which were significant (i.e. ritually potent) in their own right. These hair ornaments, for instance, were made of human bone; their protective powers stemmed from their substance as much as their form. Although they are independent objects, they are parts of bodies, both because they were attached to the body of the wearer, and because they were extracted from the bodies of others, as bones which were subsequently carved and made into ornaments. These are thus much more like tattoo motifs than might be readily apparent. Tattoo motifs are artworks made of living flesh; these are artworks made of bones, but the implications, in either case, are very much the same.
